headline: Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu hits back at BJP’s ‘Himachal on Sale’ charge
content: Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday hit back at the BJP’s ‘Himachal on Sale’ charge, accusing the previous Jai Ram Thakur-led government of allotting thousands of bighas of prime industrial land to private players at throwaway rates and facilitating real estate deals in the name of industrial development.Replying to the Opposition’s adjournment motion on corruption in the Vidhan Sabha, Sukhu levelled a series of allegations regarding land allotments, hotel projects and the handling of public assets during the BJP’s 2017-22 tenure.The motion was subsequently rejected by the Assembly through a voice vote in the absence of BJP members, who had walked out in protest after their remaining legislators listed to participate in the debate were allegedly denied an opportunity to speak.As the Speaker invited the Chief Minister to reply, opposition members entered the Well of the House and raised slogans against the government. Amid the protests, Sukhu alleged that the previous regime allotted 300 bighas in Baddi to a private company at Re 1 per square metre under a customised package, along with electricity duty concessions, but the proposed project had made little progress.He further claimed that nearly 4,000 bighas were allotted at the same rate for an ammunition manufacturing project, raising concerns that the land could eventually be converted into real estate. Another 150 bighas were allegedly allotted to a private firm, while nearly 5,000 bighas in the Baddi-Nalagarh belt were proposed to be leased for 99 years at nominal rates. Stamp duty concessions on these transactions, he claimed, could have cost the state exchequer Rs 400-500 crore.Defending his government's record, Sukhu cited the Wildflower Hall case, claiming that the state had recovered Rs 401 crore in dues after winning the legal battle. He said the property was now being managed through transparent bidding via the Centre's MSTC platform. The agreement guarantees the state a minimum annual return of Rs 24 crore, apart from 47 per cent of additional revenue, taking the estimated yearly earnings to Rs 35-40 crore.The Chief Minister also questioned the allotment of a hotel project in Seraj through nomination after changes in evaluation criteria and the transfer of 124 bighas in Manali to a company that he alleged had defaulted in Uttarakhand.On the Kangra airport land acquisition, he said an SIT had been constituted to investigate alleged land purchases using forged agriculturist certificates and warned that benami transactions would invite action.Sukhu also flagged alleged irregularities in the Himcare health insurance scheme, citing audit findings that included bills for medically impossible procedures. A Vigilance inquiry was underway, he said.Defending the procurement of electric buses, he said his government had introduced a 12-year maintenance clause and withheld payments wherever irregularities were suspected. He also clarified that Hotel Peterhoff was not being sold; its existing structure would be dismantled and replaced with a new 100-room facility.Dismissing the adjournment motion as politically motivated, Sukhu assured the House that salaries and pensions would not be stopped despite the withdrawal of the Revenue Deficit Grant. Describing the current financial year as one of consolidation and self-reliance, he reiterated his government's resolve to make Himachal Pradesh the country's most prosperous state by 2032.

headline: BJP stages walkout in Himachal Assembly over minister’s remarks against armed forces
content: The Himachal Pradesh Assembly witnessed a stormy start to Friday’s proceedings as the BJP staged a walkout over Revenue Minister Jagat Singh Negi’s alleged derogatory remarks against the armed forces and demanded his removal from the Council of Ministers. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, meanwhile, dismissed the opposition’s allegations while defending his Cabinet colleague.Leader of Opposition Jai Ram Thakur accused Negi of insulting the armed forces and demanded his removal from the Cabinet, saying his remarks had caused anguish among serving Army personnel across the state.Raising the issue as soon as the House assembled, Thakur pointed out that despite the opposition’s demand on Thursday, the minister’s alleged objectionable remarks had not been expunged from the Assembly proceedings. He said the BJP had received messages from Army personnel across Himachal Pradesh expressing resentment over the remarks.Thakur sought the Chief Minister’s response and demanded Negi’s dismissal, alleging that the minister had repeatedly made such comments.Speaker Kuldeep Singh Pathania said he had not been present in the House on Thursday and would examine the proceedings. He assured the House that any words found to be derogatory towards the armed forces would be expunged.The Chief Minister’s defence of Negi, however, triggered fresh sloganeering.BJP members raised slogans demanding the minister’s dismissal and labelled him a “Pakistan sympathiser”.Dismissing the allegations, Sukhu maintained that Negi had not used any words against the armed forces in his speech. He challenged the opposition to either participate in the discussion on the adjournment motion or stage a walkout instead of disrupting the proceedings.“Do not teach us patriotism. Leaders of the Congress have sacrificed their lives for the unity and integrity of the country,” Sukhu retorted amid loud protests.Thakur hit back, insisting that the minister had used derogatory expressions while referring to Operation Sindoor. He said the remarks were on record and that the issue could not be brushed aside as a political controversy.The Leader of Opposition urged the Speaker to adjourn the House briefly, listen to the recording and then deliver his ruling. Pathania said he would personally examine the proceedings and decide the matter during the day. He also appealed to both sides to allow the House to function, pointing out that the discussion under Rule 67 had already stretched to four days, although the rule envisaged its conclusion within a day.Thakur, however, maintained that the seriousness of the issue warranted the opposition’s intervention. He accused the Chief Minister of shielding his Cabinet colleague and said the opposition could do little if the head of the government chose to defend him.With the treasury and opposition benches trading charges and BJP members persisting with their protest, the saffron party legislators eventually staged a walkout from the House.

headline: ‘She spoke to me in French’: Sonia recalls first meet with Indira on ex-PM’s birth anniversary
content: For the world, she was the Iron Lady of India. For Sonia Gandhi, she was a gentle woman who spoke to a nervous young girl in French to make her feel at home.On the 109th birth anniversary of former PM Indira Gandhi on Thursday, Congress parliamentary party chairperson Sonia Gandhi offered a rare glimpse into the personal side of her mother-in-law, recalling how their relationship began with nervousness, hesitation and an unexpected gesture of warmth.Sonia revealed that she had initially refused to meet Indira Gandhi and changed her mind only the following day. When the meeting finally took place, she was anxious about her limited command of English, but Indira immediately put her at ease by switching to French.For Sonia, the gesture revealed a side of Indira Gandhi that rarely found space in the public image of one of India’s most powerful political leaders. “That was the first thing I learnt about her: she noticed what you were struggling with and quietly made it easier,” she said.Her daughter Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, the Congress MP from Wayanad, remembered her grandmother in a brief but emotional tribute. “Happy Birthday, tigress! There will never be another like you,” Priyanka wrote on X.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla joined Congress leaders to pay tributes to Indira at the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan in Parliament. PM Narendra Modi also remembered the leader on her birth anniversary.

headline: Punjab Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khuddian passes Lambi baton to nephew Dhira
content: Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khuddian on Friday formally handed over the political baton of the Lambi Assembly constituency to his nephew Randhir Singh ‘Dhira’ Khuddian by participating in an ‘ardas’ (prayer) held at Gurdwara Thehri Sahib and launching his official poll campaign.The uncle-nephew duo, accompanied by a large number of Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) workers and supporters, entered the Lambi Assembly constituency in a roadshow.Gurmeet Singh Khuddian sought the blessings and support of people for his nephew, saying that the constituency had elected him as an MLA and he now hoped that people would extend the same affection to Dhira.“People of the constituency elected me as their MLA. If they now want to elect Dhira, I appeal to everyone to bless him. Dhira is an extension of me. He is part of my family and household. I had made it clear from the very first day that I would extend my full support to him,” said Gurmeet Singh Khuddian. He added that Dhira would be the family’s third-generation candidate in electoral politics. Earlier, Gurmeet’s father Jagdev Singh Khuddian was elected as an MP from Faridkot.“Before announcing Dhira’s name from Lambi, Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann had sought my opinion. I had told him that I would be delighted,” Khuddian said.On the possibility of contesting from other constituency, he said, “If we get another ticket, we will win both the seats.”Gurmeet Khuddian had defeated five-time Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal on his home turf Lambi in the 2022 Assembly elections by a margin of 11,396 votes, ending Badal’s five consecutive victories from the constituency.Dhira, 55, was appointed chairman of the Punjab State Container Warehousing Corporation in June. He had earlier worked alongside his uncle in the constituency before embarking on independent political career.The development assumes political significance as the AAP has replaced Gurmeet Singh Khuddian with Dhira in its second list of candidates for the 2027 Assembly elections.The Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) is expected to field its president Sukhbir Singh Badal from Lambi, setting the stage for a possible contest between the Badal and Khuddian families.The Congress, too, has several ticket aspirants in the constituency, including Fateh Badal, son of former minister Maheshinder Singh Badal; Jagpal Singh Abulkhurana, foster son of former Cabinet Minister Jagpal Singh Abulkhurana; and Gurjant Singh, a PCC delegate and Muktsar district president of the Rajiv Gandhi Panchayati Raj Sangathan.

headline: Rattled Modi knows exit is near, repeats Congress manifesto at FICCI, blames industry for economic woes: Ramesh
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has realised that he will soon be an “outgoing Prime Minister” and is now blaming industrialists for the failures of his own economic policies, the Congress said on Friday, claiming that his remarks at the FICCI event reflected his growing frustration over stagnant wages, sluggish private investment and inadequate job creation.Addressing a press conference here, Congress general secretary and Rajya Sabha MP Jairam Ramesh said that for the first time in 12 years, a “rattled, worried and frustrated” Prime Minister had questioned the country’s wealth creators over their failure to increase wages, generate employment and boost private investment, the very concerns raised by the Congress in its 2024 Lok Sabha election manifesto, Nyay Patra. “The difference is that we blamed the government and the PM held the industry responsible,” said the former Union Minister.He said that the Prime Minister has realised that he will soon become an outgoing Prime Minister. “Before picking up his bag and leaving, he wants to blame and defame everyone else. But the responsibility for the serious challenges facing our economy lies with his own policies and his style of functioning,” Ramesh said.Referring to Modi’s address at the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) event at Bharat Mandapam on Thursday, Ramesh said the Prime Minister had repeated the same concerns that the Congress had raised during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.“In 2024, when we raised these issues in our manifesto, the Prime Minister accused us of having an ‘urban Naxal’ mindset and insulting wealth creators. Yesterday, he repeated exactly what we had said. He questioned industrialists over why they were not increasing wages, creating jobs or investing more,” Ramesh said.He recalled that Modi, who had earlier described himself as “non-biological”, had accused the Congress of disrespecting wealth creators. “Earlier, he called us urban Naxals. Now he uses the term ‘dimaagi Naxal’. But yesterday, he himself spoke the language he had criticised,” he said.Ramesh said Modi had addressed FICCI only three times since assuming office, in November 2017, 2020 and Thursday, compared with 17 addresses by Jawaharlal Nehru and around 12 by Indira Gandhi during her 16 years in office.Referring to FICCI’s century-long association with India’s industrial development and freedom struggle, he said hundreds of industrialists and entrepreneurs present at the event must have been surprised by the Prime Minister’s remarks.“The Prime Minister told them that despite everything his government had done, they were not increasing employment, wages or investment. He questioned their mindset and intentions. This is the first time in 12 years that he has spoken to the country’s wealth creators in this manner,” Ramesh said.He said Modi should examine his own policies instead of holding industrialists responsible for the country’s economic difficulties. “Why are wages not rising? Why is employment not increasing? Why is private investment not growing? Why are inequalities widening? The Prime Minister should look within himself. The answers lie in his own policies and his style of functioning,” he said.Listing the reasons behind sluggish private investment, Ramesh alleged that the Modi government had created an atmosphere of fear and intimidation in the business community through tax authorities, investigating agencies and threats of government action. “Industrialists have not created this atmosphere of fear. The Prime Minister himself is responsible. When businessmen cannot trust government policies or fear action by investigating agencies, why would they invest?” he asked.He alleged that government regulators and investigating agencies had been used in ways that appeared to benefit particular business groups, weakening investor confidence. Ramesh also accused the government of allowing economic power to become concentrated in the hands of a few industrialists, reducing competition and hurting smaller businesses.“Look at airports, ports or the power sector. Monopolies are increasing everywhere. A handful of capitalists are getting the benefits, announcing investments and acquiring national assets. Competition is disappearing, and small businesses and ordinary people are paying the price,” he alleged.The Congress leader also blamed the government’s China trade policy for the difficulties faced by India’s micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). He claimed that India’s trade deficit with China, which stood at around $112 billion in 2025-26, could reach a record $150 billion by March 2027.“In the Prime Minister’s home state of Gujarat, one-third of MSMEs in the stainless steel industry have shut down. Not one per cent or 10 per cent, but one-third. Cheap Chinese imports are hurting domestic industries. Why would Indian industrialists invest when cheaper Chinese goods continue to flood the market?” he asked.Ramesh said the growing trade deficit was affecting domestic manufacturing, threatening livelihoods and discouraging fresh private investment. Turning to demonetisation and the Goods and Services Tax (GST), he described the two decisions as major shocks that had weakened India’s economy. “Who took the decision on demonetisation in November 2016? Did the Prime Minister consult FICCI, economists or even his senior Cabinet colleagues? It was a Tughlaqi decision that destroyed livelihoods and badly affected MSMEs. Then, in July 2017, a complicated and confusing GST was imposed on the economy,” he said.He alleged that millions of workers, including migrant labourers, suffered because of these decisions, while small businesses continued to struggle with the GST system. Ramesh said the government had failed to generate adequate employment or boost private investment despite reducing corporate tax rates.“Tax rates were reduced, but private investment did not increase substantially. Employment opportunities have not grown at the required pace, wages remain stagnant and inflation continues to hurt ordinary people,” he said.Questioning the government’s claims of economic success, Ramesh said headline GDP growth figures did not reflect the difficulties faced by workers and businesses. “GDP growth may be increasing, but are wages increasing? Are jobs increasing? Is private investment increasing? What is certainly increasing is inequality,” he said.He maintained that sustained economic growth was impossible without higher private investment and claimed that the investment momentum witnessed under former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had not been matched during Modi’s tenure. “Indian investors are investing abroad rather than in India. The Prime Minister has given tax officials and investigating agencies enormous powers, creating fear and uncertainty. This is the result of his own policies,” he alleged.Ramesh said Modi should stop lecturing industrialists and accept responsibility for the economic challenges facing the country. “The Prime Minister considers himself all-knowing, all-powerful and omnipresent. But speeches and lectures to industrialists cannot run an economy. India needs sound policies, investor confidence and an accountable government. The country’s industry deserves much better,” he said, adding that “Make in India” has become “Make in China”.

headline: Irregularities in quarrying minerals: police search former DMK Minister P. Moorthi’s house in Madurai
content: MADURAI The Madurai District Police on Friday (November 20, 2026) conducted searches at the house of former DMK Minister for Registration, P. Moorthi, and other premises in connection with a case registered over irregularities in the quarrying of minerals in Madurai district. A team of police, led by the Deputy Superintendent of Police, District Crime Branch, began the searches at Mr. Moorthi’s house at Iyer Bungalow and his son’s house in the neighbourhood. Similar searches were also conducted at Poovanthi, Alanganallur, and Vadipatti, a police source said. What is the case about? According to the police, the DCB had registered a case over irregularities in quarrying minerals beyond the permitted quantity and outside the permitted area. The case was registered following a survey conducted by officials of the Revenue Department and the Mines Department. As the news broke about the searches at the premises of Mr. Moorthi, who is also the DMK rural North district secretary, party cadres from different areas gathered in front of his house. As some of the cadres raised slogans against the police, Mr. Moorthi reprimanded them. The searches, which began at around 6.30 a.m., were wound up at around 10.45 a.m. The police had taken some documents with them, the source added. ‘Only leased land’ Meanwhile, Mr. Moorthi told journalists that he had leased his land in Chathravellalapatti for quarrying for five years and added that he was not aware of the irregularities. Though the permit was obtained for stone quarrying in 2019, the lessee gave it up as the quality of the stone was not good. “I have already told the Revenue Divisional Officer that I was not aware of the quarrying of earth from my land,” Mr. Moorthi said, adding that he would approach the court. Mr. Moorthi said the police did not question him during the search.

headline: Madras High Court injuncts circulation of Junior Vikatan illustration of former DMK Minister E.V. Velu
content: CHENNAI The Madras High Court has restrained Ananda Vikatan Publishers Private Limited from printing, publishing, distributing, selling, displaying, circulating, uploading or otherwise disseminating in any medium an illustration of former DMK Minister E.V. Velu seated on the floor of a prison cell with a frightened expression and hugging to his chest a pile of currency notes. Justice Hemant Chandangoudar granted the interim injunction, till November 26, 2026, against all others too in a John Doe suit (a case filed against unknown entities as well) filed by Mr. Velu through his counsel Rahul Balaji. The judge was convinced that the balance of convenience was in favour of the plaintiff for the purpose of granting the ex-parte interim injunction as sought for by him pending adjudication of the suit. The judge also specifically directed the publishers of Junior Vikatan magazine to remove the illustration from their website, mobile application and all social media pages as well as handles operated by them, and to withdraw all posters and display material bearing the illustration. In his affidavit, Mr. Velu said, the illustration carried on the cover page and also in one of the inside pages of the latest issue of Junior Vikatan falsely portrays him as a criminal though he had not been charge sheeted, tried or convicted in any criminal case so far and even the two First Information Reports (FIRs) registered against him recently had been challenged before the High Court. Making it clear that he does not seek to stop anyone from reporting about the investigation being conducted in the two cases or the court proceedings related to those cases, the plaintiff said, he was only seeking a limited order against the illustration which falsely projects him of being guilty of corruption. Mr. Velu also stated the illustration on the cover page of the magazine had been published with the headline ‘After Anbil, Velu... ₹5,000 crore scam... Next raid ready!’ though the news article published in the inside pages does not support the illustration or the headline on the cover page. “The article that accompanies it (illustration), at pages 44, 46 and 47, does not support the cover. It attributes the figure of ₹5,000 crore to unnamed persons, says that only a preliminary enquiry has commenced, and puts as a question what the cover states as a fact,” the plaintiff’s affidavit read. He said the figure of about ₹5,000 crore was the value of the State highway road civil contract works that were the subject matter of one of the two FIRs and not an amount that he had allegedly received. He said, the police had conducted searches at his premises on June 25, 2026 but found nothing incriminating. Asserting there was no allegation of him having received or being in possession of ₹5,000 crore, the plaintiff said, the illustration gives an impression as if he had committed corruption to the tune of ₹5,000 crore, holds large quantities of illicit cash and that he would go to jail soon. “The picture (illustration) is not a photograph of anything that has happened. It is an invented scene, drawn to look real, which shows the applicant (plaintiff) as a prisoner in possession of the proceeds of crime. The impugned (under challenge) illustration is spreading rapidly amongst the public and is causing immense harm to the applicant’s reputation,” Mr. Velu said.

Hostility and non-engagement cannot resolve these issues. Both countries should come to the table and resume dialogue for peace and development in the subcontinent,” he said.

headline: BJP hits back at Rahul Gandhi over ‘compromised PM’ jibe, calls him ‘clueless on geopolitics’
content: New Delhi The BJP on Friday (November 20, 2026) criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi following a Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting, calling him “clueless on geopolitics” and accusing him of pushing “pro-Pakistan propaganda”. The ruling party also mocked Mr. Gandhi’s remarks by sharing an AI-generated image showing the Congress leader serving drinks to U.S. President Donald Trump at the trilateral meeting involving Mr. Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral: Compromised PM can never sit at this table, says Rahul Gandhi Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral: Compromised PM can never sit at this table, says Rahul Gandhi Rahul Gandhi calls India a “side player” in the Iran war, expresses surprise over Pakistan’s role in negotiator Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral: Compromised PM can never sit at this table, says Rahul Gandhi storyline 1 Sharing the image on X, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia took a dig at Mr. Gandhi with the caption, “Kuch aise (Something like this)”, accompanied by laughing and fire emojis. Talking to reporters in New Delhi, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said Mr. Gandhi should not make statements against India, whether inside the country or abroad. Mr. Gandhi had shared a picture from the rare three-way talks of Mr. Trump, Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin, and said, “A compromised PM can never sit at this table.” “If Congress were in power, India’s Prime Minister would be sitting at this table. A compromised PM can never sit at this table,” the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha had said on X. In response, BJP national media convenor Ashish Usha Agarwal said a trilateral meeting of the United States, China and Russia does not define India’s global standing, pointing to New Delhi’s engagement with competing powers through platforms such as BRICS, the Quad, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), the G20 and the G7. 'Pak Fan Boy': BJP slams Rahul Gandhi over remarks on India's foreign policy 'Pak Fan Boy': BJP slams Rahul Gandhi over remarks on India's foreign policy Mr. Bhandari alleged that Mr. Gandhi's "love for Pakistan" had made him overlook India's diplomatic efforts, including its peace initiatives in the Russia-Ukraine conflict 'Pak Fan Boy': BJP slams Rahul Gandhi over remarks on India's foreign policy storyline 1 In a post on X, Mr. Agarwal said India joined the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR) in 2016, the Wassenaar Arrangement in 2017 and the Australia Group in 2018, and became a full member of the SCO in 2017. He also questioned why Congress leader Sonia Gandhi was engaging with foreign heads of state while Manmohan Singh was the Prime Minister, and asked what her official mandate was. “India’s global standing is built on strategic autonomy, national interest and institutional strength — not dynastic privilege or photo opportunities,” Mr. Agarwal said. “Rahul Gandhi should stop confusing a photograph with foreign policy. Congress must answer for its own record before lecturing India,” he added. BJP’s social media national convenor Deepak Mhaskey said: “Not every international grouping revolves around India, Rahul Gandhi! A little understanding of diplomacy would help.” “Established in November 1989, when Rajiv Gandhi (your father, Rahul) was India’s Prime Minister, APEC is a forum for economies bordering the Pacific. India, despite its vast coastline along the Indian Ocean, DOES NOT border the Pacific. So, questioning its absence from APEC makes NO SENSE,” he said in a post on X. Boycotting polls will end democracy, says Rahul Gandhi; calls Indian democracy ‘sacred’ Boycotting polls will end democracy, says Rahul Gandhi; calls Indian democracy ‘sacred’ During an interaction at University of Chicago, the Congress leader says the Opposition will continue to contest elections despite alleged irregularities Boycotting polls will end democracy, says Rahul Gandhi; calls Indian democracy ‘sacred’ storyline 1 “Every grouping has its own purpose, membership and strategic priorities. That is how international diplomacy works,” Mr. Mhaskey said. BJP leader C.R. Kesavan claimed Mr. Gandhi was “utterly clueless” about global geopolitics, and accused him of being a “leader of pro-Pakistan propaganda”. He asked Mr. Gandhi to first speak about Nehru’s foreign policy, alleging that it was “riddled with failure and fiasco”. “While Nehru blundered and internationalised Kashmir by taking it to the United Nations, PM Modi abrogated Article 370. It was Nehru who gave up claim on India’s permanent seat at the UNSC in favour of the Chinese and forfeited about 38,000 square km of territory in Aksai Chin,” he said in a post on X. “The Congress-led UPA Govt in the most cowardly manner failed to retaliate against the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks while Operation Sindoor under PM Modi’s leadership was one of India’s greatest military victories,” he added. In a series of posts on X, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said: “Why is Rahul Gandhi so obsessed with Pakistan! At every global stage Rahul acts like Pak Fan Boy!” “Yet again he idolises Pakistan as a role model for him in foreign policy outreach!” he added. BJP mocks Rahul Gandhi's U.S. remarks, says AI can predict his speeches BJP mocks Rahul Gandhi's U.S. remarks, says AI can predict his speeches The BJP also said that Congress should consider sending an AI-generated version of its leader abroad because he keeps repeating the same words BJP mocks Rahul Gandhi's U.S. remarks, says AI can predict his speeches storyline 1 Mr. Bhandari alleged that Mr. Gandhi’s “love for Pakistan” had made him forget India’s peace efforts in the Russia-Ukraine conflict. “His love for Pakistan has made him forget that it is India which Russia and Ukraine both acknowledged for its peace efforts and Iran waived off any Hormuz restrictions,” he said. Interacting with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Mr. Gandhi said India had always had a sophisticated understanding of geopolitics, but had become a side player in global affairs, as he cited the role Pakistan played in negotiating peace between the U.S. and Iran. “India, by its size, naturally has a global voice and India should be actively involved in global conversations. But frankly, India has become a side player,” he said. In another post, Mr. Bhandari shared a photograph and claimed that Rasheed Ahmed of the Indian American Muslim Council (IAMC) was present at Mr. Gandhi’s event in the U.S. “IAMC has links to Pakistan’s terror group Jamaat-e-Islami and Muslim Brotherhood!” he alleged. Speaking to PTI Videos, Mr. Kesavan targeted Mr. Gandhi over his remarks abroad. “Rahul sitting in a foreign country and maliciously attempting to spoil India’s international reputation by defaming our nation as a side player is most condemnable and inexcusable,” he said, describing Mr. Gandhi as an “eager cheerleader and a shameless propagandist for Pakistan”. “His reckless remarks only expose how clueless Rahul Gandhi is when it comes to global geopolitics,” Mr. Kesavan said. Mr. Gandhi was on a two-day visit to the U.S., during which he interacted with students of Columbia University in New York on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and those of the University of Chicago on Wednesday.

headline: Health Minister orders regular surprise inspections at major government hospitals
content: Thiruvananthapuram Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has directed the Health department to conduct surprise inspections at one major government hospital in every district on a daily basis to improve the functioning of public hospitals and to ensure quality healthcare and services for patients. The Additional Chief Secretary (Health) has been tasked with the coordination of the inspections. District medical officers, deputy district medical officers, junior administrative medical officers and Aardram nodal officers have been directed to lead the surprise inspections at major hospitals in their respective districts. The inspections will examine the attendance and punctuality of doctors and other staff, cleanliness of hospital premises and the functioning of operation theatres, intensive care units (ICUs) and emergency departments. The inspecting teams have also been asked to interact directly with patients’ caregivers to assess the quality of treatment, availability of facilities and understand the problems and difficulties faced by patients. The teams will examine basic infrastructure in in-patient wards, availability of medicines in hospital pharmacies, and measures to ensure that expired medicines are neither stocked nor dispensed. The functioning and maintenance of procedure rooms should also be scrutinised. Compliance with biomedical waste management protocols and infection control measures should also be ensured. The Minister has directed that detailed reports on identified deficiencies, corrective measures taken and issues that need further action must be submitted to the Additional Director of Health Services (Medical) by 4 p.m. every day. The department has also been asked to consolidate the findings and submit monthly reports to the government. The inspecting teams have also been asked to check if the directives of the Health department in recent circulars are being complied with by hospitals Continuous monitoring of hospital functioning will improve the quality of healthcare services available to patients, Mr. Muraleedharan said.

headline: BJP targets Rahul Gandhi over Telangana CM’s ‘$30-trillion India by 2047’ remark
content: NEW DELHI The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Friday (November 20, 2026) targeted Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, arguing that Congress’s Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy had contradicted his criticism of India’s economic performance by expressing confidence that the country could become a $30-trillion economy by 2047. At the 85th Annual Session of the Indian Roads Congress in Hyderabad on Thursday (November 19, 2026), Mr. Reddy said, “Telangana is moving forward with a vision we call ‘Telangana Rising’. headline: Modi’s attack on industry shows he is rattled by thought of soon becoming ‘outgoing PM’, says Congress
content: NEW DELHI The Congress on Friday (November 20, 2026) said Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s “verbal assault” on industry leaders reflected his realisation that he would soon become an “outgoing PM”. PM Modi pulls up industry leaders over static wages, employment, manufacturing standards storyline 1 Mr. Modi’s remarks also amounted to an acknowledgement of what the Congress had been highlighting for several years about the state of the economy, the party added. Why is PM Modi upset with corporate India? | Explained Why is PM Modi upset with corporate India? | Explained The Prime Minister pulled up industry leaders on four different issues. Government data and anecdotal evidence shows why he is angry Why is PM Modi upset with corporate India? | Explained storyline 1 Woken up after 12 years Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the Prime Minister acted like the Leader of the Opposition by blaming the business community for the failures of his government. “True to habit, PM Modi blamed the business community for his own failures in his speech at FICCI! It felt as though the Prime Minister were the leader of the opposition. He has woken up after 12 years,” Mr. Kharge said in a post on X. Mr. Kharge pointed that the Congress had always advocated a level playing field, but the Modi government had handed over the country’s resources to “capitalist cronies”. “The lack of healthy competition stifled innovation, compromised manufacturing quality, and weakened the credibility and global brand value of Indian products,” he said, adding that the country was facing a situation of high inflation, unemployment and declining savings. “Make in India” had become “Buy from China”, the Congress chief alleged. On Thursday (November 19, 2026), addressing the FICCI annual general meeting, Mr. Modi had questioned industry leaders over the lack of commensurate job creation and salary increases despite the government’s tax concessions. Referring to income tax relief of up to ₹12 lakh per year and reductions in corporate tax and GST rates, he asked industrialists whether they had increased their employees’ salaries or expanded their workforce. “I know you won’t applaud. I know that very well, because your appetite is so enormous that no matter how much you are given, it is never enough,” he told the gathering. ‘Frustrated, dejected’ Reacting to these remarks at a press conference on Friday (November 20, 2026), Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said the Prime Minister’s remarks showed that he was “rattled, frustrated, dejected, concerned and disappointed”. He said Mr. Modi was now making the same arguments that the Congress had raised in its 2024 Lok Sabha election manifesto, the Nyay Patra, but he had then dismissed it as reflecting “urban Naxal thinking”. The Congress manifesto for 2024 general elections had flagged stagnant incomes, inadequate job creation, declining private investment and widening inequalities, Mr. Ramesh said. “He attacked the same wealth creators. He repeated what we had said in our manifesto,” he added. “It seems he has realised that he would soon become the outgoing PM and, before picking up his ‘jhola’, he is defaming others when the reality is that economic failures are due to his policies,” Mr. Ramesh said. The head of Congress’ communications division also accused the government of allowing economic power to become concentrated in the hands of a few business groups, at the expense of competition and smaller enterprises. He alleged that the use of investigative agencies and pressure on businesses had created an atmosphere of fear, undermining investor confidence. A record trade deficit with China and growing dependence on imports, demonetisation and the implementation of a faulty Goods and Services Tax (GST) hurt the domestic micro, small media enterprises (MSMEs) which were into manufacturing, said Mr. Ramesh. “The Prime Minister must look within why income is not rising, jobs are not getting created, and inequalities are rising. The reason is his own policies and his own working,” he added.

headline: Why Rajasthan panchayat results are bad news for BJP, CM Bhajan Lal Sharma
content: In a significant rebuff to the BJP, rural voters in Rajasthan handed the Congress a decisive victory in the panchayat and Zila Parishad polls Friday. The Opposition party made inroads in the turf of some of the BJP’s heavyweights, leaving the ruling party with a massive rebuilding task before the Assembly elections that are a couple of years away. The Congress had a clear majority in at least 23 of 37 Zila Parishads and the BJP in only six. The Opposition party secured nearly 70% more Panchayat Samiti seats than the BJP and won more than double the Zila Parishad seats. The Congress won 3,758 Panchayat Samiti seats and the BJP 2,213. In the Zila Parishad polls, the Opposition party bagged 794 seats and the BJP 357. There are 7,543 panchayat seats and 1,275 Zila Parishad seats in the 37 districts where votes were counted, with the counting for the remaining four districts in the state to be held next month. In 2020-21, the ruling Congress edged out the BJP in panchayat samitis, securing 39.54% of the votes while the BJP had 38.06%. In the Zila Parishads, both BJP and Congress were neck and neck, with Congress at 42.59% of the vote share against BJP's 42.42%. While the Congress was expected to fare better in this year's rural elections compared to the Urban Local Body (ULB) elections held two months ago, its substantial lead over the BJP reflects an almost tangible anti-incumbency against the Bhajan Lal Sharma-led BJP government. Turfs of BJP heavyweights breached In CM Sharma’s Sanganer Assembly constituency in Jaipur, the Hanuman Beniwal-led Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) won 8 of the 15 seats in Sanganer Panchayat Samiti while the BJP and the Congress won three each. In the CM’s home district of Bharatpur, the Congress bagged 21 of 31 Zila Parishad seats, while the BJP managed just 9 and the RLP 1. The outcome in the rural areas around Jaipur also reflected the mandate against the government. The Congress left the BJP far behind in the Zila Parishad, winning 41 of 57 seats against the BJP’s 12. And, the ruling party managed a clear majority in only two of the 22 Panchayat Samitis in Jaipur. Among the other notable poll losses were the ones suffered by Urban Development and Housing minister Jhabar Singh Kharra’s four immediate family members, including his wife and two sons, in the Shrimadhopur Panchayat Samiti. In Cabinet Minister Rajyavardhan Rathore’s Jhotwara Assembly, the BJP managed to win just 1 out of 15 seats in Jhotwara Panchayat Samiti, while the Congress won 8 and the RLP and Independents bagged 3 each. Similarly, in Pali's Sumerpur, the Assembly constituency of Cabinet Minister Joraram Kumawat, the BJP won just 4 out of 21 seats in Sumerpur Panchayat Samiti, against the Congress’s 14. In Churu, where former BJP Minister Rajendra Rathore was in the news for reciting the Islamic kalma during campaigning, his son and daughter-in-law won their respective Zila Parishad seats. However, the party fell short of a majority with 17 seats against Congress’s 21 out of a total of 39. Both Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge hailed the verdict. Gandhi said the verdict was a response to the BJP’s “attack” on MGNREGA, the move to “strip panchayats of their powers”, along with “inflation, unemployment, and migration” that had “emptied the villages”. Former Rajasthan CM Ashok Gehlot said that “voters in the state's rural areas have sent the BJP government a clear message that its time is now up”. State Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra termed the results as “historic”. State BJP president Madan Rathore said the party accepts “the mandate” and that the party would review its losses and work harder to win people’s trust. The RLP also made a comeback of sorts on its home turf of Nagaur, winning 19 of 37 Zila Parishad seats, against the Congress's 11 and the BJP's 7. Overall, the RLP won 497 Panchayat Samiti and 51 Zila Parishad seats, emerging as the third-largest party in the polls. While both the RLP and the Congress haven’t seen eye to eye lately, Dotasra emphasised that the Beniwal-led party was part of the INDIA bloc and would form the Boards together. The tribal Bharat Adivasi Party (BAP) fared well in pockets in tribal districts of Banswara, Dungarpur, and Salumber.   Decoding the results Across all 41 districts, over 2.7 crore votes were polled. This translates to nearly every third person in Rajasthan voting in the elections, signifying the strength of the mandate. The results point to a bigger worry for the BJP. In both the urban and rural elections, voting happens on hyperlocal issues. The results, thus, may be read as an indictment of sorts of the ruling party’s local leadership and administrative abilities. Next, the results will likely reinforce the perception that the Congress does well in rural areas while the BJP performs better in urban belts. The BJP will need to set its house in order, with the silver lining being that the Assembly elections are two years away. For the Congress, the immediate challenge is to keep its flock together and keep factionalism in check for the next couple of years. For now, the Congress will aim to convert its wins into forming Boards, while the BJP will move to curtail its losses. The elections for Zila Pramukh in 37 districts will be held on November 25 and up-Zila Pramukhs will be elected on November 26. This will be followed by voting for Pradhan on November 27 and for up-Pradhan on November 28. CM Sharma's challenge For the BJP, the choice is between doubling down on backing CM Sharma or considering an alternative arrangement. The CM is set to face a formidable challenge in the coming days. Though the CM, a first-time MLA, has tried to portray himself as a strict taskmaster, his government has faced flak for being slow on making crucial policy decisions. A section of the BJP leadership also pointed fingers at bureaucrats, with a top Cabinet Minister telling The Indian Express that it took them “around a year and a half” to “get them in line”. This, in part, may also be attributed to seasoned government officials knowing their way around relatively inexperienced politicians at the top. In choosing a first-time MLA as the CM, the BJP’s Rajasthan experiment was about the decentralisation of the state unit, where the party veterans and satraps were gradually sidelined. Earlier, the power was concentrated in the CM’s hands — Vasundhara Raje, for instance — and there was a clear devolution of power from her to regional satraps and her loyalists, who had the necessary experience and heft to mobilise support on the ground before the polls. Now, as per the experiment, Prime Minister Narendra Modi remains the party's face. And the party has steered the BJP government's policies, with the message being that the party is larger than any regional faces. In doing so, the BJP has also ceded space to smaller players within the party in the state. The BJP has attempted to compensate for the lack of tall leaders through the administration, but that also means bad optics and may be beneficial only in the short run. A recent example is the urban local body polls in September, where the difference between the BJP and the Congress was just 0.91% of votes in the BJP’s favour. But eventually, the Boards that the BJP managed to form far outnumbered those of the Congress. This was partly due to the tradition of Independents supporting the ruling party, but also due to the administration’s alleged coercive action against the winners who did not support the BJP. The BJP had then managed to paper over its underwhelming performance and kept the perception strongly in its favour, but the cracks were showing. Despite the results, the constitution of its Boards in the ULB polls helped the state BJP create and push a perception tailor-made for the party high command, rather than necessarily reflecting the ground reality. The rural poll verdict indicates that the state BJP’s reliance solely on PM Modi’s face and its projection as one umbrella organisation may not always yield the same results. The Congress has held that CM Sharma’s attempts to portray himself as a strong leader have been undone precisely due to the perception that under his tenure, actual power rests outside the state.

headline: Why Shiv Sena has seized on Savarkar references in Sonia Gandhi’s book
content: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s critical references to Hindutva ideologue Vinayak Damodar Savarkar in her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, have triggered a political backlash from the ruling Shiv Sena in Maharashtra. On Wednesday, taking serious objection to the references, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde’s Shiv Sena demanded the withdrawal of passages on pages 201 and 443 of the book and also sought a ban on its circulation in Maharashtra. In the 544-page memoir, formally launched in New Delhi on November 16, Gandhi, while reflecting on the Congress’s political history and its opposition to the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), refers to Savarkar’s mercy petitions to the British, a subject that has remained a point of political debate and polarisation. “While Congress freedom fighters were enduring assaults and imprisonment at the hands of the British rulers, senior ideologues of the RSS like Vinayak Damodar Savarkar were writing mercy petitions to their colonial masters, and their members were colluding with the British authorities as informers,” Gandhi writes. In the same passage, she describes the RSS as having viewed the Congress and its values as the “primary stumbling block” in its design of a Hindu nation, with people of other faiths becoming second-class citizens. She also writes that the RSS’s chief ideologues had expressed admiration for Hitler and his policies concerning minorities. On page 443, Gandhi contrasts Savarkar’s vision of Hindutva with the constitutional vision of India. She writes: “A contrary vision, articulated by Gandhiji’s contemporary Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, the founder of the ideology known as Hindutva, views India as primarily a nation where Hindus are supreme — an outlook espoused by the RSS, the BJP, and their numerous affiliates across the country known collectively as the ‘Sangh Parivar’, or ‘Family of the RSS’.” She goes on to say that this ideology dismisses the constitutional rights of citizens as being opposed to the ethos of Hindu civilisation. She describes it as conservative, patriarchal and hierarchical, favouring the centralisation of power and wealth, and says this is what the BJP’s present leadership embodies. Savarkar’s association with the RSS is also a point of historical distinction. He was a prominent leader of the Hindu Mahasabha and served as its president from 1937 to 1943. The Hindu Mahasabha and the RSS were separate organisations, although Savarkar’s formulation of Hindutva became an influential strand of Hindu nationalist politics. Why is Savarkar a political issue in Maharashtra? For the Shiv Sena and BJP, Savarkar has long been an important symbol of Hindutva politics. Over the years, he has also become a potent political issue with which to corner the rival Shiv Sena (UBT), particularly after Uddhav Thackeray broke the alliance with the BJP and formed a government in Maharashtra with the Congress and the undivided NCP following the 2019 Assembly elections. Founded in 1966 around the demand for employment opportunities for Marathi-speaking people, the Shiv Sena increasingly embraced Hindutva in the 1980s. Its alliance with the BJP in 1989 consolidated this shift. Despite his father Prabodhnkar, being a critic of Savarkar, Bal Thackeray held the Hindutva ideologue in high regard politically. The Congress, meanwhile, has consistently opposed Savarkar’s political ideology. When his portrait was unveiled by then President A P J Abdul Kalam in Parliament’s Central Hall on February 26, 2003, the Congress and Left parties boycotted the event. Sonia Gandhi, then Congress president and Leader of the Opposition, had written to Kalam asking him not to attend the unveiling. The following year, in August 2004, Bal Thackeray led the Sena’s “Jode Mara” agitation against then Union Petroleum Minister Mani Shankar Aiyar after the latter ordered the removal of a plaque bearing Savarkar’s poem at the Swatantrya Jyot near the Cellular Jail in Port Blair. The protest became a major political issue in Maharashtra ahead of that year's Assembly elections. Uddhav Thackeray’s own public position on Savarkar was clear even before the formation of the Opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) alliance. In September 2019, he demanded that Savarkar be conferred the Bharat Ratna and said Pakistan would not have come into existence had Savarkar been the Prime Minister at the time of the Partition. The differences between the Congress and the Sena over Savarkar surfaced soon after the MVA government was formed. In January 2020, a booklet distributed at a Congress-affiliated Seva Dal camp in Madhya Pradesh contained an insinuation about Savarkar’s relationship with Nathuram Godse. Shiv Sena MP Sanjay Raut reacted sharply, saying, “Veer Savarkar was a great man and will remain a great man.” In February 2020, the Maharashtra Congress’s Marathi publication Shidori carried articles criticising Savarkar’s record and ideology. These episodes exposed the ideological differences within the MVA even as the three parties continued to share power in the state. The faultline became central to the Sena split. In June 2022, Shinde led a rebellion against Uddhav, accusing him of compromising Bal Thackeray’s Hindutva politics by joining hands with the Congress and the undivided NCP. The Congress alliance was one of the central arguments used by the rebels to justify the split. The differences resurfaced after Rahul Gandhi criticised Savarkar over his mercy petitions during the Bharat Jodo Yatra in November 2022. In March 2023, following his disqualification from the Lok Sabha, Rahul said, “My name is not Savarkar. I am a Gandhi. I won’t apologise.” In response, Uddhav described Savarkar as his “idol” and said his insult would not be tolerated. He also cautioned Rahul against making remarks that could create divisions in the Opposition alliance. The disagreement was serious enough for then NCP chief Sharad Pawar to step in as a mediator. After the March 2023 controversy, Pawar advised the Congress leadership to avoid further references to Savarkar. Rahul subsequently assured Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut that he would refrain from making such remarks. Pawar, who now heads the NCP (SP), has otherwise adopted a more cautious position than the Congress, recognising Savarkar’s emotive connect among sections of Maharashtra’s electorate. At separate events in Nashik in 2021 and Nagpur in 2023, Pawar acknowledged aspects of Savarkar’s contribution, including his writing, poetry and scientific outlook, while clarifying that he did not endorse Savarkar’s ideology or that of the Hindu Mahasabha. Differences back to the forefront The controversy has brought these disagreements back to the forefront. On Thursday, Shiv Sena spokesperson Anand Paranjpe asked whether Uddhav would condemn Sonia Gandhi’s memoir and accused the Sena (UBT) chief of abandoning Bal Thackeray’s Hindutva. Paranjpe also asked Uddhav if he had forgotten that he had joined the 2004 protest against Aiyar. The Shiv Sena (UBT) has consistently responded to the BJP and the Shinde-led Sena by saying it does not require lessons on Hindutva from parties whose support for Savarkar is “restricted to electoral politics”. Raut said he had not read the entire memoir and questioned why BJP leader Nitesh Rane’s remarks on Savarkar were not being scrutinised. Maharashtra Congress spokesperson Atul Londhe has defended the passages in Gandhi’s memoir as factual, saying Savarkar’s grandson had acknowledged that he wrote a mercy petition. Londhe was also photographed presenting a copy of the memoir to Uddhav in the presence of Raut, which the Sena cited while questioning Uddhav’s position. On Thursday, Savarkar’s grandnephew Satyaki Savarkar said he was consulting his legal team and could initiate proceedings against Sonia Gandhi if the references were found to have no factual basis. He clarified that he had not read the entire book and was not seeking a ban at this moment. For Shinde, the controversy is an opportunity to question Uddhav’s association with the Congress and his claim to Bal Thackeray’s Hindutva legacy. For Uddhav, it underlines the tension between his own defence of Savarkar and the sharply different position of his allies.

headline: Congress’s Salman Khurshid: ‘Bharat Summit was not a secret meeting, government cleared it’
content: With the Supreme Court scheduled to hear on Friday a plea seeking the removal of videos of Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck’s remarks at the Bharat Summit 2026, which was held in Hyderabad on November 13 and 14, senior Congress leader and former External Affairs Minister Salman Khurshid tells The Indian Express why the summit was important for the Congress, the alleged hurdles posed by the government, and the controversy sparked by Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck’s remarks at the summit. * What is the reason for building a platform such as the Bharat Summit? We (Congress) have been in Opposition now for over a decade and needed to have a foreign policy conversation with our counterparts across the globe. And our counterparts are those who believe in progressive ideology … We do have connections with a lot of counterparts, including the Democrats in the US, the Labour Party in the UK and Australia, and some socialist parties. Mr Gandhi (Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi) was also travelling and reaching out to universities, think tanks, and important leaders in the world inclined towards the same view of the world as he has. The Foreign Affairs Department of the party and the Indian Overseas Congress decided to back these efforts. We needed a platform to do it and combine it with a platform to create investment opportunities as well. We chose Hyderabad, where we have a state government. The first summit was enormously successful and we felt we needed to do more of it. * Were there any hurdles in hosting the second edition? You cannot organise a summit just on your own. When people are coming for any conference, they need visas and political clearances which are given by the MEA and the MEA needs sufficient time to do routine checks and then allow people. Last year, they gave us some guardrails and said we will not clear people from the neighbourhood or from any area of conflict in the world. We agreed, saying, if you have an issue with Gaza, Palestine, Israel, Ukraine, and places in the neighbourhood, we have no problem with that. We did not invite people from these places. This time around, we had a huge challenge as elections were happening in many parts of the world (Brazil, US, Spain) during the time fixed for the summit. But then the MEA started dragging its feet and stopping clearances for people. For example, they gave a visa to a Norwegian journalist and later cancelled it at the last moment. But then several people who were given clearances could make it, and coupled with the domestic delegates, the event was a success once again. * How many international delegates were not allowed entry into the country? As many as 116 delegates were not given visas. In the normal course of events, I would have given them the benefit of the doubt. But then a pattern emerged of important persons not getting visas. Persons who were given visas were suddenly asked to stop. But we had a good number of around 200 foreign delegates who came. It was a perfect show, either way. * In the middle of the valedictory session, Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck said, ‘Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhor’ (vote thief, resign). This sparked a controversy, with the BJP accusing the Congress of platforming anti-India sentiments. They can spin a controversy around anything. We believe in freedom and cannot tell people to say this or not to say this. Should we give write-ups to people who come to India saying these are the things you should avoid? We believe in freedom. We believe that if people, in their assessment and judgment, want to say something, they should be allowed to say it. But the point is, do we support something which someone has said? Now, in domestic politics there are many things which we say. Our positioning as far as domestic politics is concerned is unselfconscious. In international events in the country or abroad, we are completely committed to freedom of speech, thought, and dissent. That cannot be equated with an anti-Indian, non-patriotic position. We reject that completely. * Now that the matter has reached the Supreme Court, what do you expect will happen? I do not expect anything from the courts except to stand by the people who are upright, who believe in democracy, and who believe in transparency; people who are completely compliant with everything that the government wanted. This was not a clandestine secret meeting. This was a meeting cleared by the government and the visas were given by the government. The event was conducted by an elected state government. * Wasn’t Samruddha Bharat Foundation one of the organisers of the event along with the Telangana government? Samruddha Bharat Foundation work as a backroom for the Foreign Affairs Department of the Congress. It is a registered organisation, transparent, and has conducted many events that coincide with the Congress’s ideology. They are an independent NGO, an independent think tank, and a very good one at that. * Will there be a third edition of Bharat Summit? We had announced during the first edition of the summit that we will have an annual summit for the next five years. So, absolutely, there will be a third edition.

headline: Surjit Bhalla: Dear Prime Minister, with due respect, the fault is not in India Inc
content: Addressing FICCI this week, Prime Minister Narendra Modi read the riot act to the people in the room. India Inc, he said, is not creating enough jobs, is not paying good salaries, is not innovating, and is not taking advantage of the trade agreements the government has graciously signed. And all this after the government did industry the favour of cutting taxes! It was an unusual speech: A head of government blaming the private sector for outcomes that, in a market economy, are shaped mostly by the policies of the government. Government data provides the evidence to contradict the “conclusions” the government has provided the PM to present to the public. Start with jobs of the kind industry provides — salaried jobs. In 2004-05 India had 67.9 million salaried workers. In 2011-12 there were 85.2 million salaried jobs, and in 2025, 147.6 million (all data from NSS-PLFS surveys). During the much-celebrated growth, not jobs, boom of 2004-11, salaried jobs grew by 2.5 million a year. Since 2011, the years in which industry has supposedly failed the nation, they have grown by 4.6 million a year, nearly twice as fast. Salaried jobs are now a quarter of all jobs, against a sixth in 2004. No previous period in India’s history comes even close to this record of salaried jobs creation. Total employment rose by a record 20 million a year between 2019-20 and 2024, mostly outside agriculture. The record for women's jobs is even more striking. Women held 13.1 million salaried jobs in 2004-05 and 16.7 million in 2011-12. By 2025 they held 38.9 million. The number has more than doubled since 2011, growing by 1.6 million a year against half a million a year in 2004-11. Nearly one in five working women now draws a regular salary. If that is a failure to create jobs, one would like to know what success looks like. PM's advisers and speech-writers, please note. Salaries. Here the PM has a point, but not the one he made. The average real salary, at 2024 prices, rose from Rs 18,442 a month in 2004-05 to Rs 23,637 in 2011-12, 3.5 per cent a year. Since then it has fallen slightly, by 0.4 per cent a year, to Rs 22,314 in 2025. The salary of a graduate fell from Rs 41,782 to Rs 35,046. Is this greed? No — it is economics 101. The number of employed graduates rose from 42 million in 2011-12 to 97 million in 2025. When the supply of anything more than doubles in 13 years, its price does not rise. Across developing countries, real wages grew 2.5 per cent a year in 2000-11 and 0.7 per cent a year after 2019 (ILO data). Since 2019, real wages have fallen in Indonesia (0.7 per cent a year), Egypt (0.8) and Bangladesh (2.5), and barely moved in Thailand (0.3). India, at 0.7, is in the middle of the pack. China does not publish its labour force survey results. And the workers at the bottom have done well. The daily wage of casual labourers, the poorest workers in India, has risen 3.4 per cent a year in real terms since 2011. A salaried worker earned 4.4 times a casual worker in 1999-2000, reduced to 2.4 times in 2024. That is a large fall in inequality, not stagnation. Asking firms to pay above the market rate is asking them to hire fewer people. Is that what the government wants? Taxes. India’s corporate tax cut of September 2019, from 30 to 22 per cent, was not a favour. It was a correction of one of the highest tax burdens in the developing world. Over 2019-24, general government tax revenue (excluding social security contributions) averaged 17.3 per cent of GDP in India. In China it was 14.3 per cent, in Vietnam 13.2 and in Indonesia 9.7. India, a much poorer country, taxes more than all of them. Allowing for income, India taxes 3.3 points of GDP more than expected; every major East Asian economy taxes less. The East Asian miracle was built on low taxes, not on lectures to industry. Trade deals and innovation. This complaint is a bit rich. Trade agreements open foreign markets to our firms; they do little for a firm whose inputs are taxed and rationed at home. Since 2018, budget after budget has raised import tariffs, and quality control orders (often dictated by members of the FICCI audience) now cover hundreds of products, from polyester fibre to footwear. Their effect is to keep out cheaper imported inputs and to protect the domestic suppliers of those inputs. Add the non-tariff barriers and an ultra-regressive 2015 model investment treaty, and it is easy to see why foreign investors are cautious (net FDI fell to under half a billion dollars in 2024-25). Firms innovate when they have to compete. A firm protected by tariffs and QCOs has every incentive to lobby, and none to innovate. The sad reality is that industry asks for protection, and the government obliges. Who makes policy? Industrialists do not write the customs tariff or the QCOs. The government does. If the policies are bad, and many are, the fault lies with those who advocate and implement them. Blaming firms for responding rationally to the incentives the government itself has created is the same as the age-old Indian saying: Ulta chor kotwal ko daante (the thief scolds the policeman). Exhortation is not policy. Individuals and firms respond to incentives, to prices, taxes, tariffs and regulations, not to speeches. They hire when hiring pays and invest when investment pays. When they do not, the question for the government is not what is wrong with them, but what is wrong with its policies. The PM has rightly earned credit for a renewed push towards openness and for concluding the trade agreements with Britain and the EU. The best way to honour that vision is not to lecture FICCI. It is to overrule the babus who undermine reform, scrap the QCOs, cut tariffs, and let competition prevail. India Inc will respond to incentives. Just like the government. Bhalla is chairperson of the Technical Expert Group for the first official Household Income Survey of India. Views are personal

headline: Rahul Gandhi’s ‘confession’ barb after PM’s ‘hunger’ charge at India Inc
content: A day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi questioned India Inc on job creation and employee salaries, Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha, said the Prime Minister’s “accusations” on industrialists are his “confession”. “Yesterday, Modi ji was taunting industrialists: ‘We cut taxes, yet you neither raised wages nor created jobs.’ Modi ji, these aren't accusations against them—they're your own confession,” Gandhi said on X. “You say, ‘They're so hungry they can't even fill their stomachs.’ Well said. The whole country knows whose hunger this is. Airports, ports, mines, forests, electricity, coal, roads—all handed over to them. How many jobs did they create?” he added. “The small traders and MSMEs that create jobs—you destroyed them with demonetisation and a flawed GST. And for the big companies that competed honestly, you wiped out the playing field altogether. Monopoly doesn't create jobs. It drives up prices and eliminates competition. ‘You do it, we'll see’? Modi ji, you and your friends did the looting – the country saw it, and is still seeing it,” Gandhi said. मोदी जी कल उद्योगपतियों को ताना मार रहे थे - "टैक्स घटाया, फिर भी न तनख्वाह बढ़ाई, न नौकरियाँ दीं।" मोदी जी, ये उन पर आरोप नहीं - आपका कबूलनामा है। आप कहते हैं - "भूख इतनी है कि पेट भरता ही नहीं।" सही कहा। ये भूख किसकी है, पूरा देश जानता है। एयरपोर्ट, बंदरगाह, खदानें, जंगल, बिजली, कोयला, सड़कें - सब जिनके नाम कर दिए, उन्होंने कितनी नौकरियाँ बनाईं? नौकरियाँ देने वाले छोटे व्यापारी और MSME - उन्हें तो आपने नोटबंदी और गलत GST से तबाह कर दिया। और जो बड़ी कंपनियाँ ईमानदारी से मुक़ाबला करती थीं, उनके लिए मैदान ही ख़त्म कर दिया। Monopoly नौकरी नहीं देती। महंगाई बढ़ाती है, और मुक़ाबला ख़त्म करती है। "आप करो, हम देख लेंगे"? मोदी जी, लूट आपने और आपके मित्रों ने की - देश ने देखा, और देख रहा है। तालियाँ नहीं बजीं तो बुरा मान गए? आपकी नीतियों ने उद्योगपति, छोटे व्यापारी, महंगाई से त्रस्त गरीब और मध्यम वर्ग, बेरोज़गार युवा - किसी को ताली बजाने लायक छोड़ा ही नहीं। तालियाँ और थालियाँ अपने बचे-खुचे भक्तों से ही बजवा लीजिए। — Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) November 20, 2026 Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge criticised the Prime Minister for blaming the business community for his failures and said his speech sounded as if he were the Leader of the Opposition. Addressing FICCI’s Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention in New Delhi, the Prime Minister said, “In 2014, the corporate tax rate was 30%. We reduced it to 22%. Today, in India, there is no tax on earnings up to Rs 12 lakh… I know you won’t clap. I know this very well. Kyonki aap ki bhookh itni hai, kitna hi khilao pet bharta nahin hai (Because your appetite is so insatiable, no matter how much you are given, it is never enough). But have you increased the salaries of your employees? Have you increased the number of employees in your organisations? No. You say, ‘Modi ji, you do your part, we will see.’ It will continue like this.” “The market of 1.4 billion people is both a strength and a challenge. Because you know that whatever you manufacture, it will definitely sell. Someone or the other will buy it. If someone in a big city does not buy it, someone in a small city will. If someone in a small city does not buy it, someone in a large village will. But this cannot continue. You will have to improve your quality… I feel ashamed. Are our own people not entitled to good-quality products? This mindset must change. My countrymen deserve quality,” he said. In a post on X, Kharge said the Congress is the mother of economic liberalisation. “The highest decadal average growth in the country occurred during the Congress-UPA’s tenure. But, true to habit, PM Modi blamed the business community for his own failures in his speech at FICCI! It felt as though the Prime Minister were the leader of the opposition. He has woken up after 12 years,” he said. “The Congress has always advocated a level playing field; it warned time and again. But the Modi government handed over all the country’s resources to 1–2 capitalist cronies and broke the backs of MSMEs and small traders. The lack of healthy competition stifled innovation, compromised manufacturing quality, and weakened the credibility and global brand value of Indian products,” Kharge added. “Today, there are no jobs, no savings, and inflation is at its peak. PSUs have been shut down, and Make in India has been turned into Buy From China. In pursuit of its own interests, the BJP has allowed a select group of capitalists to take structural control of the Indian economy. This is proving to be the biggest challenge facing the Indian economy today and an economic disaster,” he said. अगर देश में 👇 ⦿ वेतन नहीं बढ़ रहा ⦿ रोजगार नहीं बन रहे ⦿ निवेश नहीं आ रहा ⦿ विषमताएं बढ़ रही हैं तो इसका कारण नरेंद्र मोदी के कामकाज का तरीका और उनकी नीतियां हैं, इसके लिए PM मोदी दूसरों को जिम्मेदार नहीं ठहरा सकते। : कांग्रेस महासचिव (संचार) @Jairam_Ramesh जी 📍 दिल्ली — Congress (@INCIndia) November 20, 2026 Jairam Ramesh, Rajya Sabha MP and the Congress’s communications head, told the media that the Prime Minister is “rattled”. “PM Modi's address at FICCI clearly shows that he is rattled, disappointed and worried. Everything he said yesterday was a repetition of what the Congress had said in its Lok Sabha poll manifesto, 'Nyay Patra'. The PM said that despite him doing everything for the industry, the industry was not increasing employment, investment, or salaries. When we had pointed out the very same things, we were accused of being "Urban Naxals". The PM should introspect on why salaries and private investment are not increasing. There is only one reason behind this: the PM's policies and his style of work,” he said. ⦿ प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने देश के उद्योग जगत में भय का माहौल बना दिया है। व्यापार जगत के लोग यह समझ रहे हैं कि जांच एजेंसियों के इस्तेमाल से कई फैसले लिए गए हैं। ⦿ आज देश में कुछ चुनिंदा बड़े कारोबारियों का एकाधिकार बढ़ रहा है और उन्हें संपत्तियां सौंपी जा रही हैं। ये नरेंद्र मोदी की नीतियों का नतीजा है। ⦿ नोटबंदी का आत्मघाती निर्णय खुद नरेंद्र मोदी ने लिया। उन्होंने इस फैसले से पहले किसी से राय नहीं ली। इसके कारण MSMEs बंद हो गए, देश के सामने रोजगार का संकट पैदा हो गया। जैसे- गुजरात में एक तिहाई स्टेनलेस स्टील के MSMEs बंद पड़े हैं। यही हाल पूरे देश का है। ⦿ वहीं, नोटबंदी के बाद नरेंद्र मोदी ने देश पर गलत GST थोप दी, इसका असर पूरे देश ने झेला और अब देश की अर्थव्यवस्था डांवाडोल है। ⦿ हालात ये हैं कि वित्त वर्ष 2026-27 में चीन के साथ हमारा व्यापार घाटा 150 बिलियन डॉलर के करीब पहुंच जाएगा। - नोटबंदी और गलत GST शॉक ट्रीटमेंट थे, जिसकी जिम्मेदारी नरेंद्र मोदी को लेनी होगी और दूसरों पर दोष मढ़ना बंद करना होगा। : कांग्रेस महासचिव (संचार) @Jairam_Ramesh जी 📍 दिल्ली — Congress (@INCIndia) November 20, 2026 Ramesh also said there is an "atmosphere of fear" in the business world and the Narendra Modi government's policies has resulted in the concentration of assets in the hands of some chosen platers. He also blamed the Prime Minister's demonetisation decision for the closure of MSMEs, calling it a "suicidal move". "Noteban and GST were wrong shock treatment. Narendra Modi will have to take responsibility and stop blaming others," he added.

headline: Eknath Shinde’s helicopter develops snag; deputy CM travels by road
content: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde’s helicopter developed a technical snag before take-off from Pandharpur in Solapur district on Wednesday, forcing him to travel by road instead. The issue, reportedly related to the aircraft’s battery, was detected before departure and the helicopter did not take off. According to the police, Shinde was scheduled to travel to Thane. “But before take-off, the pilot realised there was a technical snag. The chopper did not take off, and Shinde left by road to Pune,” Atul Kulkarni, Superintendent of Police, Solapur, said. PTI reported that Shinde was in the temple town of Pandharpur to review preparations for Kartiki Ekadashi. A video of the incident circulating on social media shows police officials and others standing near the helicopter. Shiv Sena leader Shivaji Sawant said it was the “blessing of Pandurang” that the technical issue was detected before the flight. “His blessings will remain with Eknath Shinde and his onward journey will be safe,” he added. Shinde is scheduled to attend Kartiki Ekadashi Puja at the Lord Vitthal Temple in Pandharpur on November 21, PTI reported. Kartiki Ekadashi symbolises the end of Lord Vishnu’s four-month-long cosmic rest. (With inputs from PTI)

headline: After Mumbai unit's Rs 1 lakh offer, Pimpri Chinchwad Shiv Sena (UBT) announces cash reward for slapping
content: PIMPRI CHINCHWAD: Shiv Sena (UBT) has announced a reward of Rs 71,000 for anyone who slaps Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC, escalating the political row over an incident involving a photograph of party founder Balasaheb Thackeray.Making the announcement on Thursday, Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Pimpri Chinchwad unit president Chetan Pawar told reporters that the reward was being offered in response to a similar announcement by a Shiv Sena (UBT) office-bearer from Mumbai."As everyone knows, our party office-bearer from Mumbai has already announced a reward of Rs 1 lakh for anyone who slaps Shaina NC. Similarly, we, as the Pimpri Chinchwad unit of Shiv Sena (UBT), announce a reward of Rs 71,000 for anyone who slaps her," Pawar said.Row over Balasaheb Thackeray's photographThe controversy erupted on Wednesday during a press conference organised by the Shinde-led Shiv Sena in Mumbai to protest against references to Hindutva ideologue V D Savarkar in Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love.During the protest, party leaders tore pages from the book. Shaina was also seen tearing a portion of a photograph depicting Balasaheb Thackeray striking an effigy of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar with a slipper. The incident was captured on camera and drew criticism from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Shaina denied deliberately disrespecting Balasaheb, maintaining that she had torn the portion showing Aiyar and not the photograph of the late Shiv Sena founder. Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde also defended her explanation.On Thursday, Shaina apologised to Balasaheb's admirers if her actions had hurt their sentiments, while insisting that she had no intention of disrespecting him.The incident has triggered a fresh confrontation between the rival Shiv Sena factions led by Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news.
