headline: 'No special invite, ties unchanged': BJP leader fends off Congress attack over Pak minister's India visit | India News
content: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Nalin Kohli on Friday said there could be no dialogue with Pakistan as long as terror activities targeting India continue. Underlining the government's stance on the issue, he said India's bilateral ties with Pakistan remain unchanged.Kohli was speaking on the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) 'Civilisational Dialogue' forum in Delhi, which Pakistan's climate change minister Musadik Masood Malik is also attending.The BJP leader said Pakistan was not extended any special invite and that India's stand on bilateral ties remains the same.ALSO READ: 'All of our relationships will improve’: Visiting Pak minister on bilateral ties with India Malik's visit to India drew focus as Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate targeted the government for inviting a Pakistani leader who is known to make anti-India comments. Malik had previously threatened to "cut off the hands" which would try to touch Pakistan's waters after India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty last year.BJP vs CongressShrinate said on Friday that the government should be "ashamed" to invite a person who has "repeatedly" threatened India. "Threatened to cut off hands, threatened to shed blood. Pakistan is not stopping its promotion of terrorism in our country and the Modi government is busy feeding them biryani and kheer,” she wrote in a post on X on Friday.Fending off the attack, Kohli said, "India did not extend any special invitation to Pakistan. Our bilateral relations remain exactly as they were. The PM Modi-led government has made this clear. There can be no dialogue as long as terrorism is directed against us. This is a multilateral forum."He hit back at Congress, saying, "We do not need to learn any of this from the Congress party. If they wish to discuss foreign policy, they should look at what kind of foreign policy existed during the times of Pandit Nehru and Indira Gandhi."Earlier on Sunday, Congress MP Manish Tewari said that Islamabad has not taken any action against terrorism directed at India. “Nothing has changed in the last four decades. Pakistan began this phase of terrorism in 1977. India's objection is that Pakistan has built an entire network of terrorism on its soil and uses it against India. There has been no change in that," he told news agency PTI.Pakistan minister in IndiaPakistan's minister Musadik Masood Malik arrived in New Delhi earlier in the day, in what came to be the first visit by a Pakistani minister to India in three years.As India continues to raise the issue of cross-border terrorism, Malik reportedly dodged direct questions on the issue during the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi on Friday. "I think tomorrow, once I give my statement, we'll have a lot of conversations," news agency ANI quoted him as saying.According to Pakistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Malik is scheduled to participate in thematic sessions at the forum to share Pakistan's perspective on dialogue among civilisations and its role in diplomacy.Shanghai Cooperation OrganisationThe inaugural forum, hosted by India to promote cultural exchange, mutual understanding, and people-to-people ties among Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member states, observers, and dialogue partners, was announced by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh while addressing the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 20.The SCO comprises 10 member states, including India, Pakistan, China, and Russia, with India having become a full member of the grouping in 2017.(With ANI inputs)

headline: Congress slams PM Modi govt over ‘red carpet’ for Pakistan minister at SCO dialogue, cites Pahalgam | India News
content: Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate on Friday questioned the Modi government over Pakistan Minister Musadik Malik being invited to India for the SCO Civilisational Dialogue, saying the move of "rolling out the red carpet" for him was like "rubbing salt into the wounds" of the families of those killed in the Pahalgam attack.Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Dr Musadik Malik, who arrived here on Friday, would share the country's perspective on inter-civilisational dialogue.Also read: 'No special invite, ties unchanged': BJP leader fends off Congress attack over Pak minister's India visit Hitting out at the Modi government, Shrinate said the Modi government is organising the SCO Civilisational Dialogue in India on Saturday and Sunday and the question is why Pakistan was invited to this event."Why have you invited Pakistan, a country that sponsors terrorism in India? You invited Pakistan, and its minister, Musadik Malik, has arrived here," Shrinate told PTI Videos.She said he is grinning and enjoying the welcome being accorded to him. This is the same person who had openly threatened just a few months ago to chop off the hands of Indians and shed our blood, she added."The question is that Pakistan has not stopped sponsoring terrorism, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government is busy welcoming its representatives. Musadik Malik be served biryani, kebabs and kheer?" Shrinate said.The Congress leader alleged that the government is rolling out the red carpet to welcome Malik.Also read: Congress questions Centre for inviting Pakistan minister who threatened India over Indus waters"Why does your work not get done without an anti-India Pakistan?" she said, hitting out at Pakistan."The point is that you should also say and do what Rahul Gandhi has stated unequivocally: as long as Pakistan continues to sponsor terrorism, no dialogue with it is possible," she said.Shrinate accused the Modi government of changing stance."Sometimes you travel there, sometimes you reach Lahore, at other times you abruptly call off Operation Sindoor, and now you invite them here. What exactly is Prime Minister Modi doing?"The funeral pyres of those martyred in the Pahalgam massacre have not even cooled yet, and you are rubbing salt into the wounds of their families," Shrinate said.

headline: Shiv Sena MLA’s son moves court for relief in Palghar hospital attack case
content: <p>Palghar: Rohit Gavit, son of Palghar <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/shiv-sena">Shiv Sena </a>MLA Rajendra Gavit, has approached a local court seeking discharge in a hospital attack case, a government lawyer said on Friday. The court is likely to hear the matter on November 25.</p>.<p>Of the 23 accused in the <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/hospital">hospital </a>violence case, Rohit Gavit and 10 others are in judicial custody, said Special Public Prosecutor Sudhir Gupta.</p>.<p>A group of people, including the legislator’s son, had assaulted the staff at a private hospital in Palghar on the intervening night of September 5-6, alleging that it was charging exorbitant fees for treating a few injured ‘Govindas’ who had participated in the Dahi Handi celebrations.</p>.<p>They also allegedly vandalised the property, threatened the doctors, assaulted staff members and forcibly took away one of the injured persons from the ICU.</p>.Bombay HC raps police over 'casual approach' in Palghar hospital attack case probe; calls it 'unacceptable'.<p>Gupta said a charge sheet has already been filed and the prosecution has requested the court to frame charges. “The court will take up all the matters together on November 25,” he said.</p>.<p>Earlier, a Palghar court had rejected bail pleas filed by Rohit Gavit and several other accused.</p>.<p>In July, a Shiv Sena corporator from Thane district, Ramesh Mhatra, was arrested for assaulting doctors at a civic hospital. The Supreme Court cancelled his bail in September, citing his criminal antecedents, the possibility of influencing witnesses and concerns over the alleged misuse of influence during custody. It stressed that doctors must be protected from attacks. </p>

headline: BJP hits back at Rahul Gandhi over 'compromised PM' jibe, calls him 'clueless on geopolitics'
content: <p>New Delhi: The <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/bjp">BJP </a>on Friday slammed Congress leader <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/rahul-gandhi">Rahul Gandhi</a> over his swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi following the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting, calling him "clueless on geopolitics" and accusing him of pushing "pro-Pakistan propaganda".</p>.<p>In response to Gandhi's post on the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting, BJP national media convenor Ashish Usha Agarwal said a trilateral meeting of the US, Russia and China doesn't define India's global standing, pointing to India's engagement with competing powers through platforms such as BRICS, Quad, SCO, G20 and G7.</p>.<p>Gandhi had shared a picture from the rare three-way talks of Trump, Xi and Putin and said, "A compromised PM can never sit at this table".</p>.'Pak Fan Boy': BJP slams Rahul Gandhi over remarks on India's foreign policy.<p>"If Congress were in power, India's Prime Minister would be sitting at this table. A compromised PM can never sit at this table," he said on X.</p>.<p>In a post on X, Agarwal said India joined the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR) in 2016, the Wassenaar Arrangement in 2017 and the Australia Group in 2018, and became a full member of the SCO in 2017.</p>.<p>He also questioned why Congress leader Sonia Gandhi was engaging with foreign heads of state while Dr Manmohan Singh was prime minister and asked what her official mandate was.</p>.<p>"India's global standing is built on strategic autonomy, national interest and institutional strength - not dynastic privilege or photo opportunities," he said.</p>.<p>"Rahul Gandhi should stop confusing a photograph with foreign policy. Congress must answer for its own record before lecturing India," Agarwal added.</p>.<p>BJP social media national convener Deepak Mhaskey said, "Not every international grouping revolves around India, Rahul Gandhi! A little understanding of diplomacy would help."</p>.<p>"Established in November 1989, when Rajiv Gandhi (your father, Rahul) was India's Prime Minister, APEC is a forum for economies bordering the Pacific. India, despite its vast coastline along the Indian Ocean, DOES NOT border the Pacific. So, questioning its absence from APEC makes NO SENSE," he said on X.</p>.<p>"Every grouping has its own purpose, membership and strategic priorities. That is how international diplomacy works," he said.</p>.<p>In a post on X, Kesavan, responding to Gandhi's remarks, called him "utterly clueless" about global geopolitics and accused him of being a leader of "pro-Pakistan propaganda".</p>.<p>Kesavan asked Gandhi to first speak about Nehru's foreign policy, alleging that it was "riddled with failure and fiasco".</p>.<p>"While Nehru blundered and internationalised Kashmir by taking it to the United Nations, PM Modi abrogated Article 370. It was Nehru who gave up claim on India's permanent seat at the UNSC in favour of the Chinese and forfeited about 38,000 square km of territory in Aksai Chin," he said.</p>.<p>Drawing a comparison with the Modi government, Kesavan said, "The Congress-led UPA Govt in the most cowardly manner failed to retaliate against the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks while Operation Sindoor under PM Modi's leadership was one of India's greatest military victories."</p>.'A compromised PM can never sit at this table': Rahul Gandhi takes dig at PM Modi over Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meet.<p>In a series of posts on X, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said, "Why is Rahul Gandhi so obsessed with Pakistan! At every global stage Rahul acts like Pak Fan Boy!"</p>.<p>"Yet again he idolises Pakistan as a role model for him in foreign policy outreach!" he said.</p>.<p>Bhandari alleged that Gandhi's "love for Pakistan" had made him forget India's peace efforts in the Russia-Ukraine conflict.</p>.<p>"His love for Pakistan has made him forget that it is India which Russia and Ukraine both acknowledged for its peace efforts and Iran waived of any Hormuz restrictions," he said.</p>.<p>Interacting with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday, Gandhi said India always had a sophisticated understanding of geopolitics, but has become a side player in global affairs, as he cited the role Pakistan played in negotiating peace between the US and Iran.</p>.<p>"India, by its size, naturally has a global voice and India should be actively involved in global conversations. But frankly, India has become a side player," Gandhi said.</p>.<p>In another post, Bhandari shared a photograph and claimed that Rasheed Ahmed of the Indian American Muslim Council (IAMC) was present at Gandhi's event in the US.</p>.<p>"IAMC has links to Pakistan's terror group Jamaat-e-Islami and Muslim Brotherhood!" he alleged.</p>.<p>Talking to PTI Videos, Kesavan targeted Gandhi over his remarks abroad and said, "Rahul sitting in a foreign country and maliciously attempting to spoil India's international reputation by defaming our nation as a side player is most condemnable and inexcusable."</p>.<p>He described Gandhi as an "eager cheerleader and a shameless propagandist for Pakistan".</p>.<p>"His reckless remarks only expose how clueless Rahul Gandhi is when it comes to global geopolitics," he said.</p>.<p>Gandhi was on a two-day visit to the US, during which he interacted with the students of Columbia University in New York on Tuesday and the University of Chicago on Wednesday. </p>

headline: PM 'rattled', realised he will soon become 'outgoing PM': Congress on Modi's FICCI address
content: <p>New Delhi: Congress on Friday pounded on the Prime Minister for his FICCI speech where he accused industrialists of not doing enough to create jobs or increase wages with its top leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge claiming they were actually Narendra Modi's "confessions".</p><p>Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi alleged Modi was "taunting" industrialists at FICCI event on Thursday by saying that the government cut taxes but they neither raises wages nor created jobs.</p>.'A compromised PM can never sit at this table': Rahul Gandhi takes dig at PM Modi over Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meet.<p>"Modi-ji, these are not accusations against them but they are your own confession. You say, 'they're so hungry they can't even fill their stomachs'. Well said. The whole country knows whose hunger this is. Airports, ports, mines, forests, electricity, coal, roads -- all handed over to them. How many jobs did they create?" he said on 'X'.</p>.<p>"The small traders and MSMEs that create jobs -- you destroyed them with demonetisation and a flawed GST. And for the big companies that competed honestly, you wiped out the playing field altogether. Monopoly doesn't create jobs. It drives up prices and eliminates competition...Modi-ji, you and your friends did the looting. "Get your applause and your thali-banging from whatever followers you have left," he added.</p><p>Insisting that his party was the "mother of economic liberalisation", Congress president and Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge said true to his habit, Modi "blamed" the business community "for his own failures".</p><p>"It felt as though the Prime Minister were the Leader of the Opposition. He has woken up after 12 years. The Congress has always advocated a level playing field; it warned time and again. But the Modi government handed over all the country’s resources to 1–2 capitalist cronies and broke the backs of MSMEs and small traders," he said.</p><p>"Today, there are no jobs, no savings, and inflation is at its peak. PSUs have been shut down, and Make in India has been turned into Buy From China. In pursuit of its own interests, the BJP has allowed a select group of capitalists to take structural control of the Indian economy. This is proving to be the biggest challenge facing the Indian economy today and an economic disaster," he said.</p><p>Congress General Secretary (Communication) Jairam Ramesh alleged that Modi has realised that he would soon become the "outgoing PM" and is putting the blame on others when he must look within at his policies, which are responsible for the economic situation.</p><p>He said Modi must admit that "inflation remains uncontrolled, sufficient employment opportunities are not being created, and the pace of private investment is sluggish" after 12 years of him leading the government.</p><p>The economy cannot be run merely by delivering speeches or offering advice to industrialists. It requires sound policies, an environment of trust, and an accountable government. The nation's industrial sector deserves far better treatment and policies," Ramesh told reporters.</p>

headline: 'A compromised PM can never sit at this table': Rahul takes dig at PM Modi over Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meet
content: <p>Leader of Opposition <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/rahul-gandhi">Rahul Gandhi</a> has claimed that India's prime minister would be sitting at the table alongside US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin had it been from the <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/congress">Congress</a>. </p><p>Gandhi shared a picture of the first three-way talks between Turmp, Xi and Putin, saying "a compromised PM can never sit at this table".</p><p>"If Congress were in power, India's Prime Minister would be sitting at this table. A compromised PM can never sit at this table," he said on X, sharing a picture from the trilateral meeting.</p>.<p>This came after China, Russia and the US agreed on Thursday to seek reforms at the United Nations, increase oil supplies and engage in dialogue to reduce nuclear risks at the APEC summit. </p><p>Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) is a regional economic forum established in 1989 that brings together 21 member economies to promote free trade, investment, and economic cooperation across the Asia-Pacific. India is not a part of the 21-member bloc. </p>

headline: Tamil Nadu illegal quarrying case: Police raid former DMK Minister P Moorthy's residence in Madurai
content: <p>Madurai (Tamil Nadu): Police on Friday searched the residence of former <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/dmk">DMK </a>Minister P Moorthy here in connection with two cases of alleged illegal quarrying that reportedly caused a loss of Rs 5.39 crore to the state exchequer.</p><p>According to police, the Madurai District Central Crime Branch (DCB) registered two cases based on a report submitted by the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO).</p><p>The report followed an inspection by the Department of Geology and Mining into quarrying activities at Chathiravellalapatti in Vadipatti taluk of Madurai district.</p><p>The inspection revealed that a quarry lessee had allegedly excavated excessive quantities of gravel illegally from unauthorised land. The RDO's report estimated the financial loss to the government at Rs 2.32 crore and Rs 3.07 crore in the two instances, totalling Rs 5.39 crore.</p><p>Following the registration of the cases, a police team led by Madurai District Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) R Ponnarasu launched searches at Moorthy's residence on Roja Street in Ezhil Nagar, Iyer Bungalow.</p><p>Police said the searches were being carried out after informing the Judicial Magistrate No. 1 to verify whether documents or materials linked to the alleged illegal quarrying were kept at the premises. Further investigation is underway.</p>

headline: GTA VI buzz: BJP hits back with 'UPA Era 2004-2014' video after Congress jibes at PM post
content: <p>The launch of the much-awaited game <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/bengaluru/from-dhruva-to-rockstar-how-bengaluru-helped-shape-gta-and-red-dead-4223398">GTA VI</a> did not just excite gaming enthusiasts but also sparked a buzz in Indian politics.</p><p>The <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/india/pm-modi-uses-gta-vi-release-meme-to-highlight-indias-progress-apt-as-the-game-follows-a-criminal-duo-says-congress-4223753">BJP tapped into the craze around Grand Theft Auto VI</a>. The party shared a video on X, with the caption, "Throwback to GTA: UPA Era. Same open world. Different loot. 2004–2014, the heists weren't missions. They were manifestos."</p>.<p>This came shortly after the Congress took a swipe at PM's GTA-themed post. </p><p>Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday posted a GTA-styled post on social media, using imagery from the trending game to highlight India's development under his government and target the Congress-led UPA government.</p>.PM Modi uses GTA VI release meme to highlight India's progress; apt as the game follows a 'criminal duo,' mocks Congress.<p>He shared a series of images to draw a comparison in development work witnessed by India between the two instalments of the game. "India is playing a whole new game," he wrote, posting 10 slides titled "Between GTA V and VI, here's how."</p>.<p>Shortly after PM's post gained attention on social media, the Congress took a jibe at it.</p> <p>Congress general secretary (Communications) Jairam Ramesh said, "The PM, in a desperate bid to reach out to the youth, has resorted to GTA V and GTA VI imagery on social media." "Recall that this video game follows a criminal duo. How very appropriate," he said on X. </p>.<p>Meanwhile, BJP's national general secretary Smriti Irani shared Modi's post, writing, "While the world waited for GTA VI, Team India levelled up big, turning every bold vision into a mission accomplished!"</p>.<p>BJP Goa also posted a GTA-themed video. Its caption said, "While GTA VI promises virtual adventures, Goa's political opposition seems to have its own money-themed storyline!"</p>.PM Modi uses GTA VI release meme to highlight India's progress; apt as the game follows a 'criminal duo,' mocks Congress.<p>BJP Rajya Sabha MP Vinod Tawde wrote on X that GTA 6 "reportedly earned over $1.5 billion from pre-orders alone".</p>.<p>"Behind it are writers who imagine, artists who design, engineers who build, musicians who score and testers who perfect. Our youth have this spark, and institutions like the Indian Institute of Creative Technology, Mumbai, now offer courses in gaming, animation and visual effects. A world of opportunity awaits. Creativity is economic power," he said.</p> <p>An action-adventure game developed and published by Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI was rolled out across the globe on Thursday, marking its entry into the GTA series following 2013's Grand Theft Auto V. </p>

headline: UP Assembly polls 2027: BJP allies up the ante for seats; party tasks CM Yogi, top leaders with talks
content: <p>Lucknow: As the next Assembly polls in <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/uttar-pradesh">Uttar Pradesh</a> get nearer, the alliance partners of the <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/bjp">BJP</a> have upped the ante on the number of seats to be allocated to them in the poll bound state.</p><p>Some BJP allies have even threatened to break ranks if their demand for more seats is not conceded.</p><p>Apna Dal (Sonelal) President and Union Minister Anupriya Patel, while speaking at a meeting of party workers recently said that her party was ready to contest all the 403 seats in the forthcoming Assembly elections in the state, scheduled to be held early next year.</p><p>Apna Dal (AD), a predominantly ‘Kurmi’ outfit having pockets of influence in some eastern regions in the state, has demanded 25 seats from the BJP. In the previous assembly polls, AD had contested 17 seats and won 12.</p><p>Another major BJP ally, Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), which has influence in the western UP’s Jat dominated districts, has demanded 30 seats.</p><p>Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) seems to be the biggest thorn in BJP’s flesh with its president and UP minister Om Prakash Rajbhar demanding 25 seats from the saffron party and also threatening, though subtly, that he had other options.</p>.Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls: Seat-sharing talks between Congress and SP hit pause amid unease over 181-seat demand.<p>The Nishad Party, another important BJP ally in the state, has demanded 36 seats. Party president and UP minister Sanjay Nishad had, on several occasions, embarked on dharna against his own government over demand for reservation for the Nishad (fishermen) community.</p><p>What has added to the BJP woes is the announcement by the Lok Janshakti Party (LJP) leader and union minister Chirag Paswan that his party was mulling the possibility of putting up its candidates in the UP polls, especially in the districts adjoining Bihar.</p><p>According to the sources in the BJP, the party was not ready to leave more than 60 seats for its alliance partners in the state. In the 2022 Assembly polls, BJP had left 33 seats for its allies.</p><p>The saffron party has entrusted its senior leaders with the task of speaking to the allies and persuading them to accept its offer.</p><p>While Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has taken upon himself the task of speaking to RLD president Jayant Chaudhary, Deputy CM Brijesh Pathak will be holding negotiations with Anupriya Patel.</p><p>State BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary will be speaking to Nishad Party while Keshav Prasad Maurya will hold talks with Om Prakash Rajbhar on the issue.</p>

headline: 'Not a BJP slave, won't compromise on my ideology': Minister Ramdas Athawale
content: <p>Hassan: "I am not a slave to the <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/bjp">BJP</a>. I am a follower of Baba Saheb Ambedkar. I will not compromise on my self-respect or my ideology" said Union Minister of State in the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and National President of Republican Party of India (RPI), <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/ramdas-athawale">Ramdas Bandu Athawale</a>. </p><p>Speaking after inaugurating the RPI's Mysuru divisional-level convention, at a ground near Housing Board Colony, in Hassan, on Friday, he said, "A scheme should be introduced to provide at least five acres of land to the landless poor in rural areas. The poor should not be kept in a state of poverty but steps taken to transform them".</p><p>Speaking to media persons later, he said, "My struggle is on behalf of the poor and against the atrocities committed against Dalits. I am carrying forward the struggle while holding the blue flag of self-respect, as envisioned by Babasaheb Ambedkar".</p>.No question of Gyanesh Kumar resigning, says Union Minister Ramdas Athawale.<p>"The atrocities on Dalits could not be tolerated. As the Congress did not respond to my demands, despite repeated insistence, I quit Congress and joined hands with the NDA. But, I am neither a member nor the slave of the BJP", he clarified.</p><p><strong>Rahul Gandhi's statement</strong></p><p>Commenting on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's recent statements, Ramdas said, "Rahul Gandhi has been damaging the country's image abroad by claiming that India is facing economic problems. The nation's economy has improved to the fourth position and significant progress has been made in infrastructure development".</p><p>"Earlier, it took five to six hours to travel between Bengaluru and Hassan. Now, we can reach it in 3.5 hours. The country is becoming stronger under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The allegations made by Rahul Gandhi are false and with the intention to divert the people. It is not right to defame the country abroad", Ramdas said.</p>

headline: Shinde’s Sena joins hands with Congress, Ajit Pawar’s NCP to keep BJP out of power in Cooperative Bank elections
content: MUMBAI: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena has once again upset its Mahayuti ally BJP by joining hands with opposition parties to capture leadership positions in two prominent district cooperative banks in Sangli and Satara, exposing growing fissures within the ruling alliance.In the elections for chairman and vice-chairman of the Sangli and Satara District Cooperative Banks, Shiv Sena aligned with Congress in Sangli and the NCP led by late Ajit Pawar in Satara, helping keep the BJP out of power in both institutions despite its presence on the boards.The political realignment comes amid growing differences between Mahayuti partners, with local political interests seemingly overriding alliance considerations.In Sangli, Shiv Sena joined hands with Congress to secure the top positions in the district cooperative bank. Congress's Mahendra Lad was elected chairman, while Shiv Sena's Tanaji Patil became vice-chairman, marking Congress's return to the chairmanship after 22 years.The 21-member board comprises six Congress directors, five each from Sharad Pawar's NCP and BJP, three from Shiv Sena and two from Ajit Pawar's NCP. With no party having a clear majority, the Congress-Shiv Sena alliance proved decisive, leaving the BJP without either of the two top posts.A similar arrangement unfolded in Satara, where Shiv Sena aligned with Ajit Pawar's NCP to secure control of the district cooperative bank, despite the BJP having the largest group on its board.The 21-member board has nine BJP directors, eight from Ajit Pawar's NCP and four from Shiv Sena. The NCP's Udaysinh Patil was elected chairman, while Shiv Sena's Deepak Chavan became vice-chairman.The alliance was reportedly brokered by NCP minister Makarand Patil and Shiv Sena minister Shambhuraj Desai. The development is particularly significant as the BJP and Shiv Sena had contested the bank elections together but parted ways during the contest for the chairman and vice-chairman posts. Shiv Sena had earlier been sidelined by the BJP in the District Panchayat elections despite having a larger number of members.Political observers said the latest developments reflect growing competition between the BJP and Shiv Sena for political space despite being partners in the state government.The differences had also surfaced during the recent MLC elections, when the BJP contested three seats but won only one. Shiv Sena rebelled against the BJP candidate in Pune by fielding its own nominee, while in Sambhaji Nagar it backed the opposition NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) candidate against the NCP nominee.The latest developments in Sangli and Satara are expected to fuel further debate over the widening differences within the Mahayuti alliance and the growing tendency of its partners to pursue independent political strategies at the local level..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Shiv Sena (UBT) proposes renaming Nagpur as 'Deekshabhoomi'
content: Shiv Sena (UBT) Rajya Sabha MP and senior leader Sanjay Raut on Friday demanded changing Nagpur's name to Deekshabhoomi, saying it would be a true tribute to Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar and his contribution to social transformation.Raut made this demand amid the political controversy surrounding the proposed renaming of Dadar railway station as Chaityabhoomi.Dadar is the place where Dr B. R. Ambedkar’s last rites were performed.The Shiv Sena (UBT) said his party would extend complete support to the proposal of renaming Nagpur if Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis took the initiative to bring it before the state assembly.Raut said Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray was also in favour of the suggestion and had conveyed his support during a discussion with him. He argued that Nagpur’s association with Dr Ambedkar’s historic movement made it more significant to consider renaming the entire city.Nagpur is the place where Dr BR Ambedkar announced deserting Hinduism and embraced Buddhism on October 14,1956 with his 40,000 to 50,000 followers.  This place is known as Deekshabhoomi.  The event marked a landmark moment in India’s social and religious history and continues to inspire the Ambedkarite movement..After row over Union minister's remarks, CM Fadnavis says he'll urge PM to change name of IIT Bombay.BJP’s parent organisation RSS headquarter is also based in Nagpur. Besides, it is the hometown of CM Devendra Fadnavis and Union Minister Nitin Gadkari.  Raut challenged Fadnavis, who represents the city politically, to take the lead in initiating the proposal. He indicated that the opposition party would support the government if it formally moved ahead with the demand.The proposal could open a fresh debate over the recognition of Ambedkar’s legacy.Raut also raised concerns over delays in the construction of Ambedkar memorial at Indu Mill in Mumbai, questioning the rising project cost and the time taken to complete the ambitious memorial.The decision to rename Dadar turned out to be a faux pas, with the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) clarifying a day later that it was Dadar Metro station, and not the railway station, that would be renamed.Interestingly, this news release was posted on the State government publicity department's social media handle, and the CMO also posted it, but later they deleted it and issued a clarification..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Not inviting CM VD Satheesan to the scheduled Mahila Congress protest triggers row in Keralam
content: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: The Kerala Jantar Mantar, to be organised by the Kerala Pradesh Mahila Congress in the state capital on Saturday, has sparked a controversy after a senior leader criticised the leadership for not inviting Chief Minister VD Satheesan. Following the announcement of the event, Mahila Congress general secretary Sheeba Ramachandran openly protested and expressed her displeasure over the move and criticised the party's women's wing president over the manner in which the event is being conducted."Leaders ranging from Mahila Congress state president Jebi Mather MP to the KPCC president Sunny Joseph and many others were directly invited to the 'Kerala Jantar Mantar' protest to be organised by the Mahila Congress state committee. Chief Minister V D Satheesan was the only one not invited. I register my strong protest against organising such a programme that would create factions in the party," she wrote on Facebook, indicating that Jebi Mather favouring KC Venugopal was the reason for not inviting the chief minister to the event.Kerala Jantar Mantar, to be held on Saturday near the Lok Bhavan, will be inaugurated by AICC general secretary K C Venugopal. The event is being organised in connection with the Congress' nationwide protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar."Kerala has a UDF chief minister. When the programme is being organised in the state capital, it is part of the political courtesy to invite him. What we need is the politics of inclusiveness, not unilateral decisions. Even Rahul Gandhi ensures that everyone is taken along in such programmes," Sheeba added. headline: TDP takes 22 ZP chairs, Jana Sena gets 4 & BJP 1
content: VIJAYAWADA: Ahead of the indirect elections to the Zilla Parishad (ZP) Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson posts on Friday, NDA leaders held consultations on sharing the posts among the three alliance partners — the TDP, Jana Sena Party (JSP) and BJP. It was decided to allot four ZP Chairperson posts to the JSP and one to the BJP, while the TDP took the remaining 22 posts.Of the total 28 Zilla Parishads in the State, the NDA bagged 27, while the YSRCP won the Alluri Sitharama Raju ZP.While the JSP was allocated the Chairperson posts of the Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Anakapalli and Kakinada ZPs, the BJP got the Chairperson post of the Krishna ZP.The list of candidates includes women leaders in several key districts, highlighting women’s representation in local governance.Among the prominent nominees, Majji Siri Sahasra has been named for Vizianagaram Zilla Parishad Chairperson, Gadu Aliveni for Visakhapatnam, Gollapalli Amulya for Dr B R Ambedkar Konaseema, Vanthala Rajeswari for Polavaram, Chintamaneni Sai Navyasri for Eluru, Kota Pullamma for NTR, Hemalatha for Tirupati, M Sailaja for Chittoor, P Rama Devi for Palnadu, P Rohini for Bapatla and Dara Aruna for Guntur.In other districts, Kandula Ramireddy has been named for Markapuram, Polamreddy Srinivasulu Reddy for Nellore, Paritala Sriram for Sri Sathya Sai and Putta Narasimha Reddy for Kadapa ZP.The announcement also includes nominees for Vice-Chairperson posts, with candidates from the TDP, JSP and BJP represented across various districts.While the JSP was allotted Vice-Chairperson posts in five ZPs — East Godavari, Dr B R Ambedkar Konaseema, Bapatla, Prakasam and Sri Sathya Sai — the BJP was allocated the posts in NTR and Tirupati ZPs.The official list, signed by TDP supremo N Chandrababu Naidu, was released late on Thursday night..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Rattled PM Blames Wealth Generators for His Own Failures: Congress
content: New Delhi: Congress MP Jairam Ramesh on Friday launched a scathing attack against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Centre over his remarks at FICCI’s centenary convention. Addressing a press conference, Jairam Ramesh claimed that PM Modi repeated Congress’ points on employment and salaries, for which he had criticised the opposition party. Invoking Congress’ manifesto for the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, the MP said, “The Nyay Patra was our manifesto for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. As part of this... our challenges regarding the economy were discussed at length. In this Nyay Patra, we stated that there have been no increases in salaries, employment and private investment since 2014. Inequalities have increased since 2014. The Prime Minister had strongly criticised us on this Nyay Patra. Then, the Prime Minister used to call himself ‘non-biological’. He said that the Nyay Patra is full of an ‘urban naxal’ mindset. Now he uses the word ‘dimaagi naxal’.” “He said that the Congress had insulted and not respected the wealth creators of the country. Yesterday, the Prime Minister addressed FICCI. A hundred years of FICCI is being celebrated. They were a prominent figure in the industrial world—we have known of them for a hundred years—and he played a role in the freedom struggle,” he added. Jairam Ramesh claimed that the Prime Minister made such remarks as he was “rattled” by the state of the economy. “The way he spoke makes it perfectly clear that the Prime Minister is rattled. The Prime Minister is despondent, worried and disappointed. The way he attacked wealth creators, which he accused us of. He repeated what we said in the Nyay Patra. He made a verbal attack with an urban naxal mindset and accused them,” he said. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh addresses a press conference at the AICC headquarters, in New Delhi, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. (PTI Photo) Earlier on Thursday, PM Modi pulled up the business tycoons, asking them if they increased the salaries of their employees and contributed to increasing the employment rate. Addressing the industry leaders at FICCI’s centenary convention, PM Modi said, “If I speak of industry, in recent years the government’s focus has been strongly on Ease of Doing Business. In 2014, the basic corporate tax rate was 30 per cent. We reduced it to 22 per cent. Today, there is no income tax on earnings up to Rs 12 lakh in India. I know you will not clap, because however much one gives, your appetite never seems to be satisfied. I have exempted income up to Rs 12 lakh from tax. Did you increase the salaries of your employees? Did you increase the number of employees? No. The attitude remains: Modi ji, you do it, we will see.”

headline: ‘PM Modi Shifted Responsibility On Industrialists’, Alleges Congress’ Vijay Wadettiwar On Remarks About
content: Maharashtra Congress leader Vijay Wadettiwar questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his remarks asking industry leaders whether they had sufficiently increased employee incomes following corporate tax reductions and other government reforms.He accused Modi of shifting responsibility on to industrialists and blaming them for the government’s failures, PTI reported.‘PM Evading Accountability’ “Look, the Prime Minister has shifted his responsibility onto industrialists,” Wadettiwar, the leader of the Congress Legislature Party in Maharashtra, was quoted by the news agency as saying. “You have waived loans worth ₹16 lakh crore. As the government and the Prime Minister, you had promised to create 2 crore jobs. So, that is your responsibility.”'Did You Increase Salaries Of Your Employees?': PM Questions India Inc On Jobs, Wage Growth After Corporate Tax Cuts Wadettiwar said that Modi should have explained the steps he had taken to generate employment. “But by pointing fingers at industrialists and shifting the responsibility onto them, he is trying to evade accountability,” he said. The Congress leader said that when Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi spoke about job creation in the United States, the Bharatiya Janata Party became “furious” and took offence. Zoho Skips 2026 Salary Hikes As AI Costs Surge; Sridhar Vembu Says Outlook For Software Jobs Is ‘Grim’ “But today, the Prime Minister himself has acknowledged and admitted the same reality—that our country is lagging behind in generating employment,” Wadettiwar said.What Did PM Modi Say? Modi made the remarks while addressing the annual general meeting of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. He urged businesses to assess how policy benefits had contributed to economic growth. "I have exempted income up to ₹12 lakh from tax. Did you increase the salaries of your employees? Did you increase the number of employees? No. The attitude remains: Modi ji, you do it, we will see," he added.

headline: If Congress Were In Power, Indian PM Would Be Sitting...: Rahul Gandhi Takes Swipe At PM Modi Over
content: New Delhi: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi after a photograph of US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin holding talks in China surfaced on social media. The two leaders were later joined by Chinese President Xi Jinping for a trilateral meeting.Reacting to the image shared on X, Gandhi suggested that India's Prime Minister would have been part of the high-level discussion had the Congress been in power. Taking a dig at Modi, he said, "If Congress were in power, India's Prime Minister would be sitting at this table." "A compromised PM can never sit at this table," the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha added, in an apparent reference to what he described as Modi's compromised position in international affairs.Trump, Putin And Xi Jinping Hold First-Ever Trilateral MeetingFollowing the bilateral engagement, Trump and Putin joined Chinese President Xi Jinping for a historic trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen.'Dozy Don' Trump Appears To Sleep Off As Xi Jinping Speaks Ahead Of Historic APEC Summit | Video The meeting, which lasted approximately 80 to 90 minutes, marked the first-ever formal trilateral engagement involving the leaders of the United States, Russia and China.The discussions covered global security, strategic stability, nuclear risks, energy cooperation and reforms to international institutions. The three leaders subsequently issued a joint declaration outlining their commitment to nuclear risk reduction, stable energy supplies and reforming the United Nations.Despite the high-profile engagement, the declaration did not lay out a concrete roadmap for resolving the Russia-Ukraine war or announce any immediate breakthrough on major international conflicts.

headline: Maha CM Devendra Fadnavis Calls For Long-Term Water Security Plans For Mumbai, Pune; 8 TMC Water From Mulshi
content: Pune, Nov,20: With Pune Metropolitan Region’s population projected to more than double to 4.12 crore by 2047, and Mumbai’s expanding industrial activity expected to significantly increase water demand in both the cities, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Friday directed authorities to prepare comprehensive, time-bound and financially viable water security plans for both metropolitan regions. While Mumbai’s water requirements will be assessed up to 2051, Pune’s long-term water planning will focus on meeting demand until 2047, with emphasis on developing additional sources, recycling treated sewage, controlling water leakage and improving the utilisation of existing resources.Fadnavis issued the directions during a review meeting on water planning and management in the Mumbai and Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA and PMRDA) areas, held at his official residence, Varsha, in Mumbai. Water Resources Minister Girish Mahajan, Mumbai city co-guardian minister Mangal Prabhat Lodha and senior officials were present.The Chief Minister stressed that future water planning must account for increasing domestic consumption, industrial expansion and the growing requirements of data centres. He directed authorities to expedite ongoing water projects, pursue necessary forest and environmental clearances, and undertake land acquisition and rehabilitation processes simultaneously to avoid delays.Fadnavis said, “An integrated, time-bound and financially viable long-term water plan should be prepared, keeping in mind the projected population, urbanisation and growing industrial requirements of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region up to 2051 and the Pune Metropolitan Region up to 2047. Along with new projects, emphasis must be placed on the reuse of treated sewage, controlling water leakage, rainwater harvesting and exploring alternative water sources.”He also instructed municipal corporations and councils to conduct water audits and maintain accurate records of water entering the distribution system, actual supply and billing. The use of smart meters for commercial and industrial consumers should be increased to progressively reduce non-revenue water.Pune demand for a water project to reach 100 TMC by 2047The Pune Metropolitan Region’s current population of approximately 1.80 crore is expected to increase to 4.12 crore by 2047, according to a presentation made by PMRDA Metropolitan Commissioner, Abhijit Chaudhary. The region currently has a water allocation of 36.90 TMC against an estimated demand of 41.65 TMC.By 2047, the total water requirement is projected to reach approximately 100 TMC, equivalent to 7,816 million litres per day (MLD), highlighting the widening gap between available resources and future demand.To address this, Fadnavis directed officials to examine the technical and financial feasibility of bringing approximately 8 TMC of water from Mulshi dam to the Khadakwasla area through a dedicated pipeline. He also called for exploring river-basin linking, additional water sources and groundwater recharge as part of Pune’s long-term water security strategy.Another major proposal discussed was the possibility of diverting water from the Savitri river basin in the central Konkan region towards the Kukadi, Bhima, Indrayani, Mula-Mutha and Nira river basins to meet Pune’s growing requirements.Fadnavis directed and said, “The Konkan-to-Bhima river-linking project could be a viable option for meeting the future water requirements of the Pune Metropolitan Region. A preliminary project report should be prepared to examine its feasibility.”The Chief Minister also emphasised the need to reduce dependence on freshwater sources by treating sewage through tertiary treatment and supplying it to industries, power plants and data centres. Water treated through secondary processes should be utilised for irrigation, reducing the demand for potable water.PMC Approves ₹2,634 Crore Land Acquisition Proposal For 43.6-Km High-Capacity Mass Transit Route (HCMTR)He further directed authorities to reduce leakage and unmetered water supply through 24 hour water supply schemes, smart meters and repairs to ageing pipelines.Chief Minister said, “These measures can help save approximately 350 million litres of water per day.”Separate company for industrial water supplyFadnavis also directed the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC) to prepare a proposal for establishing a wholly owned subsidiary to manage water supply for industries and data centres.The proposed company would procure water from conventional sources as well as treated wastewater from municipal sewage treatment plants and distribute it to industrial consumers. It would also integrate the operation and maintenance of existing treatment facilities with industrial water supply.Also Watch:Mumbai’s water demand to reach 16,139 MLD by 2051The Mumbai Metropolitan Region, which currently has a population of approximately 2.75 crore, is expected to require 16,139 MLD of water by 2051, according to a presentation made by MMRDA Metropolitan Commissioner Dr Sanjay Mukherjee.Existing sources, including Bhatsa, Pinjal, Tansa and Vaitarna, will continue to play a crucial role in meeting the region’s requirements. However, Fadnavis said that additional infrastructure and alternative sources would be necessary to bridge the projected gap between water availability and demand.He directed officials to expedite proposed water projects, including Kalu, Deharji, Balaganga, Kondhane, Khopalsapada and Shilar, by prioritising forest clearances, environmental permissions, land acquisition and rehabilitation.The Chief Minister instructed departments to secure the necessary permissions before commencing project work and ensure that implementation is not delayed due to administrative hurdles.The Mumbai region’s long-term water strategy will also incorporate sewage recycling through secondary and tertiary treatment, dedicated distribution networks for treated wastewater and rainwater harvesting.

headline: Thane Municipal Corporation Standing Committee Constituted With 16 Corporators; Shiv Sena Secures Nine Seats

headline: PM 'rattled', realised he will be 'outgoing PM' soon, says Congress
content: The Congress on Friday claimed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s “verbal assault” on wealth creators showed that he had realised he would soon become the “outgoing PM”. The party said he was blaming others when he should be looking within at his own policies, which were responsible for the economic situation. The opposition party said that instead of questioning others, the Prime Minister should acknowledge the shortcomings in his government’s performance and the “failure” of its policies. Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh said Modi must admit that after 12 years, “inflation remains uncontrolled, sufficient employment opportunities are not being created, and the pace of private investment is sluggish”. “Mr Prime Minister, the economy cannot be run merely by delivering speeches or offering advice to industrialists. It requires sound policies, an environment of trust, and an accountable government. The nation’s industrial sector deserves far better treatment and policies,” Ramesh said at a press conference. “Yesterday, the PM addressed industry leaders at a Ficci event. The way he addressed the gathering, it was clear that he was rattled, frustrated, dejected, concerned and disappointed. He attacked the same wealth creators. He repeated what we had said in our manifesto,” he said. Meanwhile, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday also attacked the Prime Minister over his remarks on job creation and wage growth. He said the PM’s criticism of industrialists amounted to an admission of his own government’s role in creating monopolies and undermining a level playing field. Reacting on X, Rahul Gandhi alleged that airports, ports, mines, forests, electricity, coal and roads had been handed over to a select few, and questioned how many jobs they had created.

headline: PM Balendra Shah's brief Delhi visit unfolds amid Nepal's domestic strains
content: When Nepal Prime Minister (PM) Balendra Shah (36) arrives in India on November 22 on his first state visit, it will be the briefest bilateral sojourn in New Delhi by any PM from that country: He leaves on November 23, without taking up the government’s offer of showing him around Bengaluru, Ahmedabad, Ayodhya, or Varanasi.

headline: Doing our bit: India Inc responds to PM's wake-up call on jobs and pay
content: A day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi came down heavily on India Inc for not creating jobs and hiking salaries despite steep corporate tax cuts, Vedanta group Chairman Anil Agarwal said the company had just recently “introduced a special ‘Chairman Grant’, providing nearly 100,000 employees with an additional 10 per cent of their annual salary”. Other industry leaders and business associations said they, too, were doing their bit, with some also making a case for additional measures to boost employment in their respective sectors. There was, however, no immediate reaction from major industry bodies. Modi, in his address on Thursday at the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry’s annual general meet, had pulled up corporate India for its continued dependence on imports in sectors such as pharmaceuticals and metals, and for treating the country’s vast domestic market as a “comfort zone” rather than raising product quality and building capabilities to compete globally. Mohini Milind Kelkar, president, Indian Machine Tool Manufacturers’ Association (IMTMA), said the association shared the Prime Minister’s concerns and had been working to bridge the workforce shortage. While acknowledging the mining sector’s “significant potential to generate employment, both directly and through allied activities such as transportation, equipment manufacturing and downstream processing”, the Federation of Indian Mineral Industries said that encouraging investment in mining and value addition, along with skill development, would help create quality employment. This would “strengthen India’s mineral security and reduce dependence on imports”, its spokesperson said. Expressing the industry’s support to the PM’s call, Sanjay Mehta, president, Material Recycling Association of India, added, “However, the material recycling sector has a unique challenge. India’s domestic scrap generation is currently insufficient to meet the growing requirements of its recycling industries, which is a key raw material.” Consequently, Mehta said, imports of quality scrap become “inevitable”. Echoing the sentiment, Rajamani Krishnamurti, president, Indian Stainless Steel Development Association (ISSDA), said the Prime Minister’s remarks resonated strongly with the Indian stainless steel industry’s aspirations and ground realities — but certain structural challenges needed urgent attention if India is to realise its full manufacturing potential. The ISSDA would like to highlight the need for strengthening raw material security, immediate implementation of quality control orders, fair trade and not unfair competition. Krishnamurti pointed to priority issues such as addressing unfair trade practices, promoting domestic value addition and encouraging investment, technology and employment. The central message of the Indian stainless steel industry, he added, was that it does not seek protection from competition; it seeks a level playing field. Ajai Rana of the Federation of Seed Industry of India (FSII) said India’s seed industry is recruiting people, and though the industry is sitting on huge inventories, it has not retrenched anyone. Most industry players were largely supportive of the Prime Minister’s call. Some also listed the factors holding them back. “The biggest drawbacks are bureaucracy and a parallel economy, both of which are hurting the country,” said a senior industry player who did not wish to be named. Another India Inc representative, who spoke on anonymity, added that the question of creating jobs and passing on the tax benefits varied from sector to sector. “Some industries, such as kitchenware and appliances, are adding jobs since they are growing,” the official said. That said, there has been a lull in major manufacturing sectors, the official added. A representative from the roads and infrastructure sector said the issues facing the roads sector were rather complicated with matters such as premium, bonus etc dominating the discourse. The Vedanta Group, meanwhile, said in a note that the group had also built a democratised employee stock option (ESOP) programme, extending ownership opportunities from entry-level professionals, including freshers, to senior leadership, covering nearly 40 per cent of its workforce. A senior NITI Aayog official urged the industry to view the government as a facilitator, not just as an entity for financial sops.

headline: Discoms not cooperative enough on EV charging infra: Advisor to PM
content: Electricity distribution companies (discoms) are not sufficiently cooperative in setting up electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure, said Tarun Kapoor, advisor to the Prime Minister, at a conference organised by the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (Siam) on Friday.  "We have to ensure that there's some nodal officer in every discom, who can be contacted in case there are issues or in case there are problems," he added. Kapoor said that discoms needed to recognise the growing importance of EVs as a source of power consumption, particularly as India was entering a phase of surplus electricity availability. "Discoms sometimes feel that they make most of their money through industries, so they should concentrate more on that. But this (EVs) is going to be a very major sector for them and I am quite sure that as we move forward, discoms will realise this and then they will make efforts to ensure that they facilitate charging infrastructure coming up in the country," he said. Kapoor also highlighted the high cost of establishing electricity connections for public charging stations, particularly those requiring higher power capacities of 200 kilowatts (kW) or more. Discoms sometimes demand substantial payments for the electricity infrastructure needed to connect such stations to the grid. Discoms are largely owned by state governments, although some are privately owned companies operating as licensed electricity distributors. The licences are granted by the respective state electricity regulatory commissions. Improving discoms' cooperation with EV charging operators will require coordination with state governments and electricity regulators. Kapoor said the government had made budgetary provisions under the PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) scheme to cover this cost, adding that a large part of the allocated money remained unspent. The government would be willing to provide additional funds if required, he added. Another challenge is the low utilisation of existing public charging stations, which is affecting their maintenance. Kapoor said oil marketing companies (OMCs) had reported utilisation of less than 1 per cent at some locations. "Earlier also, some charging stations were installed in various public locations and gradually, due to disuse, they were not maintained and then they became almost useless," he said. The government is looking beyond petrol pumps to expand charging infrastructure, he said, with housing societies, office complexes and public parking lots among the possible locations. Charging stations should be installed where vehicles are generally parked for longer periods, he added. Kapoor also called for greater use of daytime charging to utilise surplus electricity, particularly solar power. He said India often had surplus electricity during the day, while demand pressures were higher during peak hours. Installing chargers at workplaces could encourage people to charge their vehicles during the day. He said electric truck manufacturers should avoid developing exclusive charging networks for their respective vehicles. Charging stations along highways should be accessible to vehicles made by different manufacturers so that infrastructure gets sufficient users and remains properly maintained, he added. The government also wants charging infrastructure for electric buses, trucks and heavy vehicles used in mining and industrial applications. Kapoor said bus depots could be opened up for use by other EVs, and the government was asking state governments to facilitate this. Siam President Shenu Agarwal, in his speech at the conference, said the automobile industry, electricity distribution companies, OMCs, charging operators and state governments needed to work together to expand the network. "Automakers bring vehicle and charger compatibility, oil marketing companies bring prime land and retail reach, charge point operators bring technology and service, discoms bring grid access and states bring approvals, land and demand implications," he said. Agarwal described electric truck charging as the next frontier, adding that bus depots and freight corridors would require high-power charging facilities. Siam members were keen to work with energy and infrastructure partners to develop this network, he said.

headline: Adamant over Himachal minister’s dismissal, BJP stages walkout
content: Adamant about the dismissal of Revenue Minister Jagat Singh Negi, the opposition BJP on Friday staged a walkout of the Himachal Pradesh legislative assembly in Dharamshala.On the fifth day of the winter session, heated exchanges erupted as the BJP launched an offensive against the government over Negi’s remarks regarding the Indian Army on Wednesday.As proceedings began, Leader of the Opposition Jairam Thakur raised the issue, saying that a senior minister had made serious remarks concerning the Army and ‘Operation Sindoor’.Pressing for a public apology by Negi and his dismissal from the Cabinet.

headline: Revanth Reddy likens dissenting Congress leaders to people bitten by mad dogs
content: HYDERABAD: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Thursday took a swipe at dissenting Congress leaders, saying some members of his own party appeared to have been “bitten by mad dogs” for criticising the government in public while praising its work in private.Addressing a public meeting in Siddipet, the Chief Minister said some leaders were airing their criticism publicly even as they privately acknowledged the government’s achievements. He also said Congress workers would take such people to Erragadda, referring to the mental health facility in Hyderabad. .Although Revanth Reddy did not name anyone, his remarks were seen as an indirect response to Congress MLAs Komatireddy Raj Gopal Reddy and J Anirudh Reddy, who have recently questioned the government’s functioning.The comments came a day after Raj Gopal Reddy criticised the alleged unequal distribution of development funds. Speaking at a programme in Munugode on Wednesday, he questioned why constituencies represented by senior leaders were receiving substantial allocations while Munugode continued to face financial constraints..Warning against neglecting his constituency, the MLA said a “war” would begin if its development needs were ignored and compared the situation to Kurukshetra. He also flagged delays in road and irrigation projects as well as a proposed 100-bed hospital in Choutuppal.Jadcherla MLA J Anirudh Reddy, meanwhile, alleged that some government officials were demanding commissions from contractors to clear pending bills. His remarks raised questions over alleged corruption within the administration.The public criticism by the two legislators has brought differences within the ruling Congress into the open, with concerns over development funds and the functioning of the government becoming points of contention.During his Siddipet visit, Revanth Reddy also targeted the Opposition BRS and challenged former minister T Harish Rao over irrigation projects undertaken during the previous government’s tenure.(With inputs from agencies)

headline: Illegal quarrying: Police raid former DMK Minister Moorthy's residence in TN's Madurai
content: Madurai (Tamil Nadu): Police on Friday searched the residence of former DMK Minister P Moorthy here in connection with two cases of alleged illegal quarrying that reportedly caused a loss of Rs 5.39 crore to the state exchequer.According to police, the Madurai District Central Crime Branch (DCB) registered two cases based on a report submitted by the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO).The report followed an inspection by the Department of Geology and Mining into quarrying activities at Chathiravellalapatti in Vadipatti taluk of Madurai district.The inspection revealed that a quarry lessee had allegedly excavated excessive quantities of gravel illegally from unauthorised land. The RDO's report estimated the financial loss to the government at Rs 2.32 crore and Rs 3.07 crore in the two instances, totalling Rs 5.39 crore.Following the registration of the cases, a police team led by Madurai District Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) R Ponnarasu launched searches at Moorthy's residence on Roja Street in Ezhil Nagar, Iyer Bungalow.Police said the searches were being carried out after informing the Judicial Magistrate No. 1 to verify whether documents or materials linked to the alleged illegal quarrying were kept at the premises. Further investigation is underway.

headline: CM Revanth Reddy resorting to personal attacks to hide failures: KTR
content: Hyderabad: Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president K.T. Rama Rao criticised Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy for allegedly ignoring the distress of Telangana farmers amid prevailing drought conditions across the state and resorting to objectionable language instead of addressing pressing public issues.Rama Rao questioned the Chief Minister’s remarks at Siddipet on Thursday, alleging that he was making personal attacks while people were struggling with drought conditions and farmers were facing difficulties.He accused Revanth Reddy of remaining silent over the alleged diversion of Telangana’s water resources while blaming those who raised questions about the issue.The BRS leader also questioned Revanth Reddy’s credentials to speak about Telangana martyrs, alleging that he had betrayed the statehood movement and had failed to raise the slogan of Jai Telangana.KTR said the Chief Minister should focus on public welfare, development and responsible communication rather than making personal remarks against political opponents."The Congress government had neglected welfare schemes and was engaging in corruption while attempting to divert public attention through accusations and political rhetoric," he added.The BRS working president also said every Assembly constituency would respond to the Congress in the same manner as Siddipet and Sircilla, predicting a major electoral setback for the ruling party.He criticised Congress leaders for repeatedly targeting BRS president and former Chief Minister K Chandrashekar Rao (KCR), accusing them of being subservient to the party's leadership in Delhi.KTR described Chandrashekar Rao as a leader who had contributed to Telangana's development and contrasted his leadership with that of Revanth Reddy.BRS senior leader and former minister T Harish Rao also criticised Revanth Reddy over his speech in Siddipet, alleging that he had failed to address farmers’ distress, pending development works and welfare schemes while resorting to personal attacks against BRS leaders.Reacting to the Chief Minister’s remarks, Harish Rao said the speech, which lasted more than an hour, contained political claims but offered no relief to farmers facing drought conditions or any concrete agenda for the people.He alleged that Revanth Reddy had failed to mention development works worth Rs 1,070 crore pending in Siddipet. He also questioned the absence of any reference to the Indiramma life insurance scheme announced by the Congress government.Referring to the Telangana statehood movement, Harish Rao questioned whether Congress minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy had not defeated Shankaramma when K Chandrashekar Rao fielded her as a candidate in an Assembly election.He also accused the Congress government of claiming credit for projects initiated during the previous BRS administration. He alleged that the Chief Minister was inaugurating works undertaken by the BRS government and naming medical colleges established during its tenure without initiating comparable development projects.Disputing Revanth Reddy's claim that no welfare schemes introduced by the previous government had been discontinued, Harish Rao listed several programmes that he alleged had been stopped.These included KCR Kit, Nutrition Kit, Arogya Lakshmi, fee reimbursement, Dalit Bandhu, Rythu Bima, sheep distribution, fish distribution, Ramzan Tohfa, Christmas gift packs, Mana Ooru Mana Badi and Kanti Velugu.He accused Revanth Reddy of repeatedly targeting former Chief Minister K Chandrashekar Rao through personal criticism and challenged the Chief Minister to explain what additional development projects his government had undertaken or what benefits it had provided to Siddipet.

headline: PM Modi’s FICCI remarks admit economic policy failure, says CITU
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent remarks at the FICCI meeting, questioning corporate India over its failure to increase investment, generate employment and raise workers’ salaries despite successive tax concessions and incentives, constitute an important admission of the failure of his Government’s economic policies.His acknowledgement vindicates the position consistently advanced by the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU): corporate tax concessions and incentives do not automatically translate into productive investment, employment generation or improvement in workers’ living standards.CITU has consistently opposed the Government’s supply-side, pro-corporate economic strategy, which relies on tax concessions, subsidies and incentives to stimulate private investment while neglecting people’s purchasing power. This position was emphatically reiterated by CITU in its intervention at the pre-Budget consultation with Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on 20 November 2026.The economic data expose this contradiction. Corporate profits reached 4.8 per cent of GDP in FY 2023–24, a 15-year high, growing by 22.3 per cent, while employment grew by only 1.5 per cent. Employee expenses of listed companies grew by just 13 per cent, against 17 per cent in the previous year.More recently, the NITI Aayog’s November 2026 assessment of the 14 PLI schemes revealed that, by March 2026, they had achieved 76 per cent of their investment target and 64 per cent of their production target, but only 28 per cent of their employment target.Against a target of approximately 30.18 lakh jobs, only 8.49 lakh had been generated. The 2019 corporate tax reduction alone involved an estimated annual revenue loss of Rs 1.45 lakh crore.Meanwhile, banks wrote off Rs 7.41 lakh crore in loans to large industries and services between 2014–15 and 2022–23.Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, creditors have realised only around 33% of admitted claims in resolved corporate insolvency cases. CITU demands a fundamental reversal of this policy direction. The forthcoming Union Budget must abandon the approach of granting successive concessions to corporate capital and instead mobilise resources through progressive taxation. An effective wealth tax on the super-rich, inheritance/estate tax on large transfers of wealth and higher taxation of extraordinary corporate profits and massive wealth accumulation are essential. Those who have accumulated enormous wealth and benefited disproportionately from Government policies must contribute proportionately more towards national development. The increasing burden of indirect taxation on ordinary people must also end. CITU demands that the Budget prioritise the purchasing power of working people through a national floor-level minimum wage of Rs 42,000 per month, repeal of the Four Labour Codes, restoration of MGNREGA with a guarantee of at least 200 days of employment per rural household and introduction of an urban employment guarantee. Universal social security must be ensured for all workers, including unorganised, self-employed and platform workers, along with a minimum monthly pension of Rs 21,000 for all elderly persons. All vacant posts in government departments and public-sector enterprises must be filled, and eligible contractual and outsourced workers must be regularised with equal wages and service benefits. The Budget must substantially enhance public expenditure on healthcare and education, moving towards allocations of 3% and 6% of GDP respectively. It must guarantee MSP, strengthen public procurement and safeguard a robust, universal Public Distribution System. The Old Pension Scheme must be restored for government employees, while privatisation and monetisation of public assets must be halted. The Prime Minister’s admission must translate into a concrete policy reversal. Strengthening the purchasing power of working people is not an expenditure burden; it is the essential foundation for expanding domestic demand, stimulating productive investment and ensuring sustainable economic growth.

headline: Nepal PM Balendra Shah set for Nov 22-23 India visit focused on trade, MoUs
content: Kathmandu, Nov 20: Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah is scheduled to pay a two-day state visit to India on November 22-23 at the invitation of his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi, Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on Friday.Prime Minister Shah will depart for New Delhi on November 22 aboard a Nepal Airlines flight, accompanied by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Chief Adviser to the Prime Minister Kumar Byanjankar and other senior government officials.This will be Shah's first bilateral visit abroad since he was sworn in as prime minister on March 27. He had earlier visited New York in September to attend the United Nations General Assembly."During the visit, Shah will hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Modi on November 23 and discuss a range of issues of mutual interest," Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said at a press briefing on Friday.The two prime ministers will also jointly address a press conference following their bilateral talks. On the same day, Prime Minister Modi will host an official luncheon in honour of the Nepali prime minister and his delegation.Rai said the two countries were also expected to inaugurate several completed projects related to connectivity and energy cooperation and lay the foundation stones for new projects during the visit.Discussions between the two sides will focus on strengthening economic cooperation in trade, transportation, investment, energy, connectivity networks and infrastructure development, the ministry said.The two sides will also exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering cooperation in education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management and human resource development.The official government delegation departing from Nepal will comprise 34 members. Nepal's ambassador to India and some other members will join the delegation in New Delhi. A separate 52-member delegation of business representatives will participate in the visit at their own expense.The visit will also feature a Nepal-India Business Forum aimed at attracting Indian investment to Nepal. The forum will provide an opportunity to engage with Indian businesspeople, understand their concerns and present Nepal's policies and initiatives to encourage investment.During his stay in New Delhi, Shah is also scheduled to pay a courtesy call on Indian President Droupadi Murmu and meet External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar. He will also visit Rajghat to pay floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi.The visit is expected to provide fresh momentum to bilateral relations and strengthen cooperation between the two neighbouring countries, which share longstanding historical, cultural and people-to-people ties, the ministry said.It will also provide an opportunity for the two countries to review their wide-ranging bilateral cooperation and explore ways to further strengthen their partnership.Prime Minister Shah is scheduled to return to Kathmandu on November 23.(IANS)

headline: Madurai police conducts searches at residence of former DMK Minister P. Moorthy
content:

A case has already been registered over allegations of illegal and excessive quarrying of red soil and stones beyond permitted limits in Palamedu and Alanganallur.
