headline: Chandigarh civic polls on December 23, counting on December 26; Congress, AAP to go solo
content: CHANDIGARH: Chandigarh Municipal Corporation elections will be held on December 23, with counting of votes scheduled for December 26, State Election Commissioner Vijay Dev announced on Friday. The entire election process will be completed by December 31, while the Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) have ruled out an alliance and said they will contest independently.The nomination process will begin on November 26 and continue till December 3. Scrutiny of nomination papers will take place on December 4, while the last date for withdrawal of candidature is December 7. The number of wards will remain unchanged at 35.With the announcement of the election schedule, the model code of conduct has come into force with immediate effect. Chandigarh has around 4,60,209 voters who will cast their ballots across 566 polling booths.The Election Commission has also completed the draw for ward reservations. Wards 1, 3, 4, 9, 15, 29 and 32 have been reserved for Scheduled Castes (SCs) based on their population share as recorded in the 2011 Census. Of these, wards 3, 29 and 32 have been reserved for SC women.A total of 12 wards have been reserved for women, including nine for general-category women, wards 17, 21, 13, 25, 30, 2, 8, 11 and 26, and three for SC women.The civic polls are expected to be a keen contest among the major political parties, particularly the BJP, Congress and AAP, following changes in the political composition of the outgoing House.AAP, which contested the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation elections for the first time in the previous polls, won 14 seats and emerged as the single largest party. The BJP secured 12 seats, Congress eight and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) one.However, defections and changes in political affiliations subsequently altered the composition of the House. The BJP currently has 18 councillors, Congress 10 and AAP seven, while the SAD has no councillor, making the BJP the largest party in the outgoing corporation.Chandigarh Congress president H.S. Lucky ruled out an alliance with AAP, saying the earlier understanding between the two parties was limited to a post-poll arrangement to counter the BJP following the Lok Sabha elections. He alleged that AAP had walked away from that understanding and said differences in the functioning of the two parties made an alliance unlikely.Chandigarh AAP chief Vijay Pal Singh also said the party would contest all 35 wards independently, asserting that the understanding with Congress had lasted only until the 2024 Lok Sabha elections..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: ED summons Rajya Sabha MP Satnam Singh Sandhu in forex violations case
content: CHANDIGARH: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned nominated Rajya Sabha MP and Chandigarh University Chancellor Satnam Singh Sandhu to its Jalandhar office for questioning in connection with alleged foreign exchange violations involving funds transferred to entities linked to him.Sources said entities linked to the 57-year-old Sandhu had allegedly received funds from companies of the Vuenow Group, which are under investigation for reportedly orchestrating a multi-crore 'Cloud Particle Scam' in which the accused allegedly siphoned off money collected from the public. The ED has summoned Sandhu to ascertain the nature and purpose of the transactions. Sources clarified that he has not been summoned over any direct involvement in a money-laundering case.Sandhu was initially summoned to appear on November 12 but did not do so. He has now been asked to depose on November 25. An officer said the summons was issued by the ED's Jalandhar Zonal Office.The ED has arrested three persons in the case, including Vuenow Group CEO and founder Sukhwinder Singh Kharour and his wife, Dimple Kharour. The agency has been investigating the matter since 2024 under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act and the Foreign Exchange Management Act..ED writes to Punjab DGP seeking case over alleged 'transfer racket' linked to CM Mann's OSD.In a statement issued in February, the ED said the “underlying business of cloud particle, based on the Sale and Lease Back model (SLB model), was found substantively non-existent and grossly overstated to cheat the investors. “It is also revealed that no rental amount, or an insignificant amount, is received from the data centre clients as the entire business of Vuenow group was found to be only a money rotation scheme,” it added.The agency said around Rs 3,700 crore was collected from investors through the sale of cloud particles. Of this, approximately Rs 1,800 crore was returned to investors in the form of rent, while the remaining proceeds of crime were allegedly used for purposes other than business.There was no immediate response from Sandhu.A native of Rasulpur village in Punjab's border district of Ferozepur, Sandhu is an agriculturist-turned-education entrepreneur.He established his first venture, Chandigarh Group of Colleges (CGC), at Landran in Mohali in 2001, followed by Chandigarh University in 2012. He also founded the Indian Minorities Foundation, an NGO established with the vision of the Prime Minister's 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas' initiative to bring people from different minority communities together on a common platform..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Shah hails PM Modi Govt’s zero-tolerance terror policy
content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has said that India’s counter-terrorism stance has been fundamentally transformed under the ‘zero tolerance’ policy of the Modi Government. He said that Kashmir is now free of terrorists who are locally recruited and born in India, following the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) Lateef Bhat.Speaking at the opening session of a two-day counter-terrorism conference here on Thursday, Shah said the policy is working and that the system has undergone structural changes geared toward pre-emption rather than reaction.Shah said the defining characteristic of a good agency is the ability to nab the terrorists and put them in jail before they can carry out an attack. The Centre is building a system in which every police station in the country will be working under one strategy to combat terrorism.All forces should look at and adopt models that have worked in organised crime and related threats.On fugitives, Shah said 303 have been returned to India from 36 countries since 2019. He described the return of fugitives who were hiding abroad as essential and inextricably linked to the wider effort to dismantle terror financing networks. He said better coordination with the financial investigation agencies is required. He believes success in this endeavour can be achieved only through a simultaneous attack on the entire terror ecosystem, rather than through isolated actions.Shah made it clear that the outcomes would be very limited without a common objective and clearly defined accountability at every stage of the process. He called for a much more assertive, proactive, and offensive approach to counter-terrorism policy, with a clear focus on enhancing both structural and operational capabilities. Once a case comes to light, the investigation must continue until the entire network is broken. He stressed the ATS’s importance in this regard and directed that every state’s ATS strengthen its cyber expert unit.The minister also announced an expansion of the Multi-Agency Centre (MAC)’s remit to include cyber security, narco-terrorism and emerging hotspots of radicalisation, along with the establishment of a National Memory Bank. These were presented as the basis of a new approach to preparedness, and on the NIA, Shah said its legal powers have been augmented, and its national footprint expanded, with approval given for 16 new branch offices and 2 zonal offices. The agency has also been given powers to investigate cases involving Indians overseas.Shah described the PFI’s complete disintegration as a clear example of a well-planned operation. In one night, police from 11 states, along with central agencies, dismantled the PFI. He now calls it a textbook case of such an operation worldwide. In a separate development, authorities have declared the Pakistan national Shahzad Bhatti network a terrorist organisation under the UAPA. Authorities have broken up more than 40 of its modules.Shah released the NIA’s ‘Fail Safe Investigation’ publication during the event, laid the foundation stone for the NIA office complex in Chandigarh and inaugurated a residential complex at Maidan Garhi.The address was a very neat little list of claimed operational successes and institutional expansion. You could ask whether the claimed eradication of local recruitment in Kashmir, the scale of the returns of the fugitives and the effectiveness of the one-night coordinated actions actually amounts to any real diminution of terror capability (that’s for others to verify over time).The thrust of the address was clearly the move from a purely reactive investigative model to one of proactive disruption, with a focus on the financial networks of the terrorists and the expanded role of the NIA and ATS.

headline: IIT Delhi-Abu Dhabi campus holds first convocation, 17 graduates join energy, sustainability sector
content: IIT Delhi’s first international campus in Abu Dhabi held its inaugural convocation on November 19, with 17 students graduating from its Master of Technology (MTech) programme in Energy Transition and Sustainability. All graduates have secured employment across the UAE and the wider Gulf region, including 11 who are working with Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC).The ceremony was attended by Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi, Indian Ambassador to the UAE Deepak Mittal, Rima Al Mokarrab Al Muhairi, Chair of Tamkeen and Executive Director of the Strategic Affairs Unit, Executive Affairs Authority, along with members of IIT Delhi’s Board of Governors, faculty members, graduates and their families.The first graduating cohort marks a milestone for IIT Delhi’s international campus, established under an agreement signed in July 2023 in the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The campus was inaugurated in September 2024 by Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.Addressing the ceremony, Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi said, “It is an honor to be in Abu Dhabi to congratulate the first graduating cohort of IIT Delhi’s Abu Dhabi campus. The progress the institute has made in just three years reflects the strength of the UAE–India partnership. I commend IIT Delhi, our Abu Dhabi partners, the faculty and all who have worked to build this institution. Today’s graduates leave the first international campus of India’s highest-ranked university and begin a new role as bridge builders between India and the UAE.”Her Excellency Reem bint Ebrahim Al Hashimy, Minister of State for International Cooperation, said, “IIT Delhi–Abu Dhabi reflects the strength of the UAE–India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and our shared commitment to advancing cooperation in education, research and innovation. The graduation of its first cohort marks an important milestone in translating this partnership into meaningful opportunities for future generations, particularly in energy transition and sustainability. We look forward to the institution’s continued contribution to strengthening academic and scientific cooperation between our two countries.”Rima Al Mokarrab said, “IIT Delhi–Abu Dhabi reflects a core belief guiding Abu Dhabi’s progress: by bringing together world-class institutions, industry, and talent, we drive innovation and growth that benefit Abu Dhabi and the wider world. This graduating cohort, already contributing at leading energy companies across the region, is a testament to that vision.”IIT Delhi Director Rangan Banerjee said, “This first graduating class of IIT Delhi–Abu Dhabi reflects the academic standards that have defined IIT Delhi for decades, as well as the power of the UAE–India partnership. Our first international campus has allowed us to bring the academic foundations and culture of IIT Delhi into a distinctive Abu Dhabi context, while creating new opportunities for students, faculty and researchers across both campuses and countries.”Executive Director of IIT Delhi–Abu Dhabi Shantanu Roy said, “Every academic institution is ultimately judged by its graduates. This first cohort has set a high standard. Their achievements reflect the academic excellence at the heart of an IIT Delhi education, and I look forward to seeing the impact they have through industry, research and the careers they build.”The campus currently has a student population approaching 300, representing 13 nationalities across six academic programmes, including four undergraduate, one postgraduate and one doctoral programme. Its academic and research activities cover areas such as energy transition, computer science, artificial intelligence, chemical engineering and electrical engineering.The first batch of graduates will also become part of IIT Delhi’s global alumni network of more than 65,000 members. The institution has been working with industry partners, including ADNOC, as well as universities and research institutions in the UAE, to develop specialised skills and strengthen research collaboration in emerging technologies and the energy sector.

headline: Delhi rolls out ‘Ehsaas 2026’ policy to support students’ mental health
content: The Delhi Government on Thursday (November 19, 2026) launched the ‘Ehsaas 2026’ Mental Health and Well-Being Policy for schools and higher educational institutions in the national capital. The policy aims to ensure one counsellor for every 500 students, besides providing helplines and mental and emotional support services. Lieutenant-Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, spiritual leader Sri Sri Ravi Shankar and Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa were present at the launch. The policy seeks to raise awareness about mental health and encourage students, teachers and parents to speak openly about the subject, making mental and emotional well-being an integral part of education. Under the policy, special attention will be given to examination pressure, academic stress, anxiety, depression, interpersonal relationships and challenges related to digital behaviour. Students dealing with the pressure of board and entrance examinations will also receive guidance and support, according to the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO). The policy also provides for opportunities for students to develop stress-management and social-emotional skills, while sensitising teachers and parents to recognise early signs of mental health concerns. It also emphasises confidential mechanisms for reporting bullying, identity-based discrimination and cyberbullying, timely action on complaints, and protection from harassment for those filing complaints, according to an official statement. Equal support for all children The Lieutenant-Governor said making mental health and emotional well-being an integral part of education was the need of the hour. At a time when young people were facing increasing stress, the Delhi government’s initiative was timely and commendable. Mr. Sandhu said, “Every child’s feelings, aspirations and needs matter. No child should face discrimination on the basis of their background, abilities or circumstances. Children with disabilities and those from disadvantaged communities must be given equal opportunities, acceptance and support.” He added that responsibility for mental health rested not only with students but also with teachers, parents and school management. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the policy had been introduced keeping in mind the mental health and overall well-being of students and would be implemented across schools and higher educational institutions in Delhi. She said ‘Ehsaas’ would give millions of students studying in Delhi’s schools and colleges an opportunity to move forward with greater mental and emotional resilience. “The Delhi government wants every child to progress in life with happiness, positivity and confidence, and to know that the government, teachers and parents will stand by them through every challenge,” she said. Six-tier mechanism According to an official statement, the ‘Ehsaas’ policy will have a six-tier escalation mechanism to ensure student safety and address serious mental health crises. The mechanism will include the class teacher, school counsellor/first responder, school head/wellness team, District Well-Being Centre, hospital/emergency mental health services and relevant statutory agencies. Students will have access to specialised mental health services through District Well-Being Centres established at the district level. These centres will provide psychological assessments, therapeutic interventions and psychiatric consultations. “Schools will be responsible for early identification, initial psychosocial support and referrals, while clinical assessments and treatment will be handled by trained specialists, ensuring that students who need help receive appropriate care in time,” the statement further added. Staff to receive training Education Minister Ashish Sood said the government took up the issue after a school student attempted suicide a few days ago. Following the incident, he wrote to school principals and held discussions with them and mental health experts to work towards a comprehensive policy. He said the policy was an important initiative to understand children’s emotional needs, listen to them and provide appropriate support. He also thanked the Art of Living, UNESCO, IHBAS and expert institutions for their contribution to developing the policy. Mr. Sood said teachers, parents, principals, Educational and Vocational Guidance Counsellors (EVGCs), officials, drivers and other support staff would be trained to identify early changes in children’s behaviour and respond with sensitivity and appropriate support. Four key pillars The ‘Ehsaas’ policy is based on four key pillars. The first, the “Whole-Institution Approach”, seeks to make mental health part of an institution’s overall culture, with the participation of students, teachers, faculty, institutional heads, hostel staff and parents, according to the CMO. The second pillar, Proactive and Preventive Care, focuses on identifying early signs of mental health concerns, promoting social-emotional and life skills, and building mental resilience. The third, System-Level Accountability and Governance, seeks to ensure clearly defined responsibilities within institutions, staff training, capacity building and accountability of institutional leadership. The fourth pillar, Ethical Safety and Rights-Based Support, will protect students’ dignity, privacy and confidentiality, ensure age-appropriate consent for minors and respect the autonomy of adult students.

headline: Beyond Delhi’s smog: What does CPCB AQI data say about rest of India? Infographic
content:
Every evening, the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) releases data collected from multiple air pollution sensors in the country. According to this data, Delhi and surrounding areas remain some of the most polluted in the country all year round, and especially from October to February. However, winter trends show worsening conditions in some of the other parts of the country too. In this story we explore what the CPCB data says about year-on-year changes in the AQI numbers.

The bulletin, along with the visible smog, is a marker of fluctuating air quality in many parts of the country, mainly the national capital region (NCR), during winter months when pollution is known to spike. Every winter, the stories of Air Quality Index (AQI) levels rising make headlines. We decided to look at the winter days’ daily AQI bulletin and filter it in different ways to see how every winter compares with the other.

For a part of this analysis, we collected daily data between October and February for the past four winters – October 2022 to February 2023, October 2023 to February 2024, October 2024 to February 2025, and October 2025 to February 2026.

On October 31, the bulletin provided readings from 288 locations in the country. However, at the same time last year, there were 243 regions in the bulletin. To account for this difference in number of days monitored, we first filtered the data to only consider locations that have been in the system for 95% of the total days considered. So, if a region shows up in the data for at least 574 out of 604 days, it was considered for this analysis.

While Delhi, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad, Noida, and Gurugram formed the top (right-most) of the list, they were followed closely by Bhiwadi in Rajasthan, Meerut in Uttar Pradesh, Faridabad in Haryana, Patna and Hajipur in Bihar, Bulandshahr in Uttar Pradesh, Charkhi Dadri in Haryana, and Hapur in Uttar Pradesh.

All these locations fall in the Indo-Gangetic plain that is locked by the Himalayas on the north side. Multiple studies, like this one, have found that the post-monsoon and winter months have higher aerosol concentration than other months in this region.

headline: Delhi’s Air Quality Remains ‘Poor’ With AQI At 270
content: New Delhi: Delhi's air quality remained in the poor category on Friday morning, with the city recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 270, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).PM2.5 was the prominent pollutant recorded across the city, with several monitoring stations reporting AQI levels above 300, according to CPCB data at 7:05 am.Among the monitoring stations, Siri Fort recorded an AQI of 348, followed by Pusa at 337 and JNU at 338. Chandni Chowk and Burari Crossing both recorded an AQI of 331, placing them in the very poor category.Other monitoring stations also reported elevated pollution levels, with ITO recording an AQI of 322, Jahangirpuri 311, Punjabi Bagh 309 and North Campus 308.RK Puram recorded an AQI of 259, while Anand Vihar reported an AQI of 267, both falling under the 'poor' category.According to CPCB classification, an AQI between 0 and 50 is considered 'good', 51-100 'satisfactory', 101-200 'moderate', 201-300 'poor', 301-400 'very poor' and 401-500 'severe'.Meanwhile, dense fog covered several areas of Thiruvarur, Tamil Nadu, this morning.Earlier, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), on November 17, revoked Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) in Delhi-NCR, citing an improvement in air quality.According to an official statement issued by the CAQM, its sub-committee on GRAP decided to withdraw the restrictions imposed under Stage III with immediate effect. Consequently, all government, government-aided and recognised private schools in Delhi were directed to resume physical classes for all students.Earlier on Wednesday, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta reviewed the capital's pollution-control measures at a high-level meeting held at the Delhi Pollution Control Committee's (DPCC) Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC). According to an official press release, Gupta said Delhi had witnessed some relief in November compared with the past decade, but emphasised that the government would continue taking strict action against all sources of pollution.During the meeting, she directed various departments to coordinate their efforts and ensure visible results on the ground. She specifically instructed the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) and the Public Works Department (PWD) to intensify cleaning of roads, footpaths and central verges through mechanised sweeping, water sprinkling and road washing.The government has also intensified inspections at construction and demolition sites. Gupta directed officials to ensure the proper installation of green nets, barricades and windbreakers at construction sites, stressing that dust-control measures should not be treated as a mere formality.

headline: Pakistan minister gets nod to visit Taj Mahal, 3 Delhi sites; Nizamuddin shrine trip denied
content: Pakistan's Climate Change Minister, Musadik Masood Malik, who is in New Delhi to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisations Dialogue Forum, has been granted permission to visit the Taj Mahal in Agra and three other sites in Delhi. However, his request to visit the Hazrat Nizamuddin shrine has been denied on security grounds.Government sources said the Pakistan High Commission had sought permission for Malik to visit the Taj Mahal, Delhi Haat, Humayun's Tomb, Qila Rai Pithora and the Hazrat Nizamuddin shrine. Following a security assessment, authorities cleared the first four visits but withheld permission for the shrine.Speaking briefly to the media on the sidelines of the forum at Purana Qila, Malik described the gathering as an opportunity for countries in the region to engage in dialogue beyond their political and strategic differences.“I think all of our relationships in the region are in flux, as the politics are shifting very fast. So I am very hopeful that we will take a broader view, looking at social issues, poverty and other concerns, rather than missing out on these issues because of politics,” he said when asked whether the forum could help improve India-Pakistan relations.He said cultural and civilisational exchanges offered an opportunity for countries to come together despite their differences.“I think the easiest thing to do is to speak about things that affect us, and that is to talk about culture and civilisations and how these civilisations have affected all of us,” Malik said, thanking the SCO for providing a platform for such engagement.Referring to the civilisational links between India and Pakistan, Malik said dialogue was inherently about recognising diversity.“Dialogue is distinct entities. Singularity doesn't require a dialogue; singularity only requires a monologue. Dialogue is about diversity,” he said, adding that the region's shared history provided a basis for engagement.Malik is leading Pakistan's delegation at the first SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum, being held at the historic Purana Qila from November 20 to 22. He is the first Pakistani federal minister to visit India since the military confrontation between the two countries in May 2025, following the Pahalgam terror attack.The visit had initially drawn attention following reports that his engagements in India would be restricted to the multilateral event. The subsequent clearance for visits to prominent historical and cultural sites, with the exception of the Hazrat Nizamuddin shrine, came after a security assessment by Indian authorities.

content: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta, in the presence of Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, launched the capital’s first Mental Health & Well-being Policy at ‘EHSAAS 2026’. The initiative aims to benefit over 45 lakh students through dedicated counselling, a 24×7 mental health helpline and timely emotional support.

headline: Bulgarian foreign minister begins India visit in New Delhi
content: New Delhi, Nov 20: Bulgaria's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Velislava Petrova-Chamova, arrived in New Delhi on Friday for a three-day official visit.While extending a warm welcome to Velislava Petrova-Chamova in New Delhi, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on X stated, "The visit will provide an opportunity to further strengthen the longstanding and friendly India-Bulgaria relations and deepen bilateral cooperation across diverse sectors."Later in the day, Velislava Petrova will hold a meeting with Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal. She will call on President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan on Friday.On Saturday, Velislava Petrova is scheduled to hold a meeting with External Affairs Minister (EAM) S Jaishankar at Hyderabad House in New Delhi.Last month, Secretary (West) at the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Sibi George, and Bulgaria's Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, Christo Polendakov, co-chaired the India-Bulgaria Foreign Office Consultations, with both sides emphasising the early implementation of the India-European Union (EU) Free Trade Agreement (FTA)."Secretary (West) Sibi George co-chaired the India-Bulgaria Foreign Office Consultations with Mr Christo Polendakov, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Bulgaria," the MEA posted on X."They reviewed all aspects of bilateral cooperation, including political engagements, trade and investment, science and technology, AI, space, defence and people-to-people ties," it added.The two sides pitched for an early rollout of the trade pact between India and the 27-nation Bloc."Both sides emphasised the early implementation of the India-EU FTA, which would contribute to further strengthening of economic ties. They also exchanged views on regional and global issues of mutual interest," the MEA posted on X.India and Bulgaria share longstanding, warm and friendly ties. People-to-people contacts and cultural links between the two countries predate the establishment of diplomatic relations in 1954, and there are traces of contacts between the peoples of the two countries as early as the 8th Century AD, according to the MEA statement.In the past six decades, India and Bulgaria have developed a close, cordial and multi-dimensional relationship. The multi-faceted relationship has flourished based on continuity and mutual understanding and has progressively evolved into a binding friendship.(IANS)

headline: Selja seeks resumption of paddy procurement in Haryana, cites 8.3L tonne shortfall
content: Hisar: Congress MP from Sirsa and AICC general secretary Kumari Selja on Thursday demanded the immediate resumption of paddy procurement by govt, alleging that farmers across Haryana were still left with unsold produce in mandis after the closure of purchases on Nov 15.Citing Haryana State Agricultural Marketing Board data, Selja said govt agencies had procured 49.62 lakh metric tonnes of paddy against the 58-lakh-tonne target, leaving a shortfall of 8.38 lakh tonnes. headline: Five arhtiyas lose licences after mandi inspection reveals irregularities in Bathinda district
content: The licences of five commission agents (arhtiyas) have been suspended in Bathinda district after irregularities were detected during inspections of grain markets.Deputy Commissioner (DC) Rajesh Dhiman said the Market Committees of Raman and Talwandi Sabo had suspended the licences after inspection teams found that heaps of paddy belonging to different farmers had been mixed.As per the rules, arhtiyas are required to keep each farmer’s produce in separate heaps and properly earmark them. However, the inspection teams found violations of this requirement in the cases concerned.The licences were suspended for violating conditions of the Punjab Agricultural Produce Markets Act, the DC said. He added that the agricultural produce bought or sold by the respective commission agents in the notified market areas was also under scrutiny.The DC warned commission agents to strictly follow government norms to ensure that farmers did not face any inconvenience during procurement. He said officials were regularly conducting surprise inspections at grain markets.Meanwhile, the DC said 15,20,171 metric tonnes (MT) of paddy had arrived in 201 notified grain markets of the district so far. Of this, 20,093 MT arrived on Wednesday, he said.A total of 14,28,675 MT had been procured so far, including 31,666 MT on Wednesday, the DC said, adding that the lifting of procured paddy had also gathered pace, with 11,20,120 MT lifted so far.On the other hand, several farmers in mandis were claiming that they were facing hardships in selling their produce. Some of them claimed to be sitting in mandis for the past 10 to 14 days for selling their crop.

headline: Mandi farmers get direct market access, sell 25 quintals oranges
content: The ambitious HP SHIVA project of the state government has taken a significant step towards providing direct market accessories to fruit growers. Under the initiative, the Horticulture Department, Mandi, has facilitated a direct sales platform at the Seri Manch, enabling farmers to sell their produce to consumers without the involvement of middlemen.The initiative has received an encouraging response from local consumers. In the first phase of direct marketing, around 2.5 tonnes (25 quintals) of sweet oranges brought from the Chhuighat cluster of Mandi were sold directly to customers. The produce included the Blood Red and Jaffa varieties of oranges, which attracted buyers because of their quality and taste.Farmers received Rs 50 per kilogram for their produce, ensuring a direct and remunerative return for their efforts. The initiative is expected to strengthen the relationship between local fruit growers and consumers while reducing dependence on conventional marketing channels.Deputy Director of Horticulture, Mandi, Sanjay Gupta, who is also the chairman of the HP SHIVA Marketing Committee, said that the project had established 96 horticulture clusters covering around 996 hectares in the district. Fruit production from these clusters had now started reaching markets on a larger scale, he added.He said that Horticulture Minister Jagat Singh Negi had issued clear directions to ensure that farmers receive support not only in the adoption of modern cultivation techniques but also in securing reliable and profitable markets for their produce.Gupta added that the department was continuously connecting farmers associated with the clusters to major national-level buyers. In the current year, fruits such as plums, guavas and sweet oranges produced in different clusters of the district had been successfully marketed through prominent companies, including Reliance, Go-for-Fresh, Zepto and Orange Valley. The produce had also reached agricultural produce market committees in Ludhiana and Chandigarh.The department has expanded this market-linkage initiative and introduced direct sales at the local level under the Farm-to-Consumer model. The arrangement aims to eliminate unnecessary intermediaries and commission charges, allowing farmers to receive better returns while providing consumers with fresh, nutritious and locally produced fruits at reasonable prices.The department’s initiative is expected to create additional marketing opportunities for horticulturists and encourage more farmers to adopt fruit cultivation as a sustainable source of income under the HP SHIVA project.

headline: Gateway to the Himalayas
content: Time Travel “Is this really the world’s longest highway tunnel at a height above 10,000 ft?” Taran had just finished adventure sports in Manali and was headed to Sissu. His parents had been talking non-stop about the Atal-Rohtang tunnel. They were throwing words around like “engineering marvel” and “visionary”. “What makes it exciting,” said Appa, “is that it makes the Lahaul region accessible all year round. Before the tunnel, the only route was the Rohtang Pass, which shut down under snow from November to May. Now, after the tunnel was constructed, people can drive from Manali to Keylong in just two hours. Sissu, Keylong and the deeper Lahaul valley are accessible all year through.” Just then the tunnel began. It seemed endless, with lights all around. There were indications of the kilometres crossed. “It feels like I am in a sci-fi movie; I have been teleported to another dimension,” said Taran. “They cut through the Pir Panjal range for 9.2 km. That’s a long distance,” exclaimed Amma. “Imagine the difficulty of cutting through all that stone, water, and soil. I read somewhere that workers had to dispose of more than 8,00,000 m³ of excavated soil.” There were signs saying “No Stopping” and “No Photography”. After all, this was a tunnel, not a tourist attraction. Still, Taran couldn’t help thinking he was part of something special just by travelling through. They came out to the other side and stopped to take some photographs. Next, they stopped in Sissu village and played in the snow like proper tourists. They visited a little Buddhist monastery that overlooked the Sissu Lake. The landscape was stark and beautiful, with clear blue skies and hardly a cloud in sight. “It is like a portal. The landscape is so different from what is on the other side of the tunnel. I feel like Alice in Wonderland, going down the rabbit hole,” said Taran. Amma laughed and tousled his hair. “You have an active imagination.’ “Did they cut through the mountains from one side, or did they decide to dig from both sides and meet in the middle?” wondered Taran. “Interesting, I did not think of that. But what if they had missed and dug two tunnels?” laughed Appa. “Well, it was announced by the then Prime Minister, Atal Bihari Vajpayee, in 2000. I am quite sure the design team would have thought it through,” countered Amma. “I imagine children from the future coming here to understand how it all happened. It is truly an engineering marvel.” His father beamed. “Now, let’s enjoy another culinary marvel: a hot chocolate! I spot a coffee shop.” The family walked together in the cold, crisp air. “A perfect end to a perfect day.”

headline: Uproar in Himachal House over minister’s remarks on Rafale and Operation Sindoor, Opposition demands an apology
content: The Himachal Pradesh Assembly witnessed a heated confrontation between the treasury and Opposition benches on Thursday over remarks by Revenue and Tribal Affairs Minister Jagat Singh Negi on the Indian armed forces, the Rafale deal, Operation Sindoor and the Galwan conflict. Presiding Officer Sanjay Rattan, who was chairing the proceedings in the absence of Speaker Kuldeep Singh Pathania, assured the Opposition members that any remarks by Negi found to be against the defence forces would be expunged from the proceedings. He said the remarks appeared to have been made in passing and would be examined before a final decision was taken. The assurance came after Leader of Opposition Jairam Thakur and BJP MLAs demanded an unconditional apology from Negi, alleging that his remarks amounted to questioning the integrity and role of the armed forces. The confrontation began during a discussion on the adjourned motion, “Himachal on Sale”. Negi referred to reports alleging that the original cost of the Rafale fighter aircraft deal was lower and that the price had subsequently increased substantially. He also referred to the Galwan Valley clash and Operation Sindoor. Outside the Assembly, LoP Thakur accused Negi of making allegations of corruption in the Rafale deal and questioning the efficacy of fighter aircraft. He demanded an unconditional apology and questioned Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu over retaining Negi in the Cabinet despite what he termed repeated controversial remarks concerning the armed forces.

headline: Harjinder Singh Dhami re-elected SGPC chief for sixth consecutive term
content: Harjinder Singh Dhami was on Friday re-elected president of the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) for a sixth consecutive term, securing unanimous support at the annual General House meeting of the apex Sikh religious body. The election was held at Teja Singh Samundri Hall in the presence of Sri Guru Granth Sahib. A total of 112 SGPC members attended the session, which also saw Raghujit Singh Virk elected senior vice-president, Gurbakhsh Singh Khalsa junior vice-president and Gurpreet Singh Jhabbar general secretary. Eleven executive members were also elected. They include Mohan Singh Bangi, Bawa Singh Gumanpura, Ranjit Singh Kahlon, Navtej Singh Kauni, Bibi Paramjit Kaur Moonak, Ravinder Singh Khalsa, Darshan Singh Brar Mothanwali, Charan Singh Alamgir, Gurinderpal Singh Gora, Bibi Narinder Kaur Rania and Kuldeep Singh Nassupur. Born in 1956, Dhami, an advocate by profession, first became an SGPC member in 1996 and subsequently served on its Dharam Parchar Committee and Executive Committee. He was elected general secretary in 2019 and took over administrative responsibilities as the institution's chief secretary in 2020. He was first elected SGPC president in November 2021. Addressing the media after his re-election, Dhami thanked Guru Ramdas Ji, Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal and SGPC members for reposing faith in him. Outlining his priorities for the coming year, he announced plans to commemorate the birth centenary of Bhagat Ravidas Ji and the foundation anniversary of Sri Amritsar. He also said the SGPC would step up its Dharam Parchar activities and humanitarian work globally. Dhami said a Sikh centre being established in the United States would be completed soon, complementing the centre already operational in the United Kingdom. SGPC resolutions The General House passed several resolutions addressing religious, social and political issues, including Punjab's drug crisis, Sikh prisoners, the Kartarpur corridor and the controversy over amendments to the Jagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026. Expressing concern over the deaths of young people due to drugs, the SGPC referred to the recent murder of Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa and accused the Punjab government of failing to discharge its responsibility in tackling the menace. It said the drug crisis posed a direct threat to future generations. The House also condemned what it termed the Punjab government's evasive and misleading approach towards amendments to the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026. Maintaining that the legislation contained objectionable provisions, it demanded that its implementation be suspended until the clauses were removed. On the issue of Sikh political prisoners, the SGPC urged the Jathedar of Sri Akal Takht Sahib to issue clear directions on the mercy petition of Balwant Singh Rajoana and demanded the immediate release of all Bandi Singhs. It said their prolonged incarceration was fostering a sense of alienation among Sikhs. The House also called upon the Centre to ensure that SGPC general elections were held every five years in Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Chandigarh. It condemned what it described as continued interference by the Centre in Punjab's river waters, Chandigarh and representation in the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB). On Sikh religious heritage, the SGPC demanded the immediate reopening of the Sri Kartarpur Sahib corridor, an increase in the number of pilgrims allowed to visit Pakistan and protection of historic Sikh shrines there that remain closed. With Amritsar set to mark the 450th anniversary of its foundation in 2027, the House also called for urgent measures to tackle pollution and traffic congestion in the holy city. Other resolutions condemned discrimination against the Punjabi language, expressed concern over youth migration, supported the global abolition of the death penalty and urged the United Nations to protect religious minorities across the world. The session was attended by senior Sikh clergy, including Acting Head Granthi of Sachkhand Sri Harmandir Sahib Giani Amarjit Singh, Acting Jathedar of Sri Akal Takht Sahib Giani Kuldeep Singh Gargaj and Jathedar of Takht Sri Damdama Sahib Giani Tek Singh.

headline: School winter vacation 2026-27: Check state-wise holiday dates and reopening schedule
content: School Winter Vacation 2026-27: Schools across North India are expected to observe winter vacations during the 2026-27 academic session, with most states scheduling breaks between late December 2026 and mid-January 2027. However, the duration differs across states, depending on regional weather conditions, education department guidelines and school calendars.While schools in Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Bihar generally follow shorter winter breaks, institutions in Himalayan regions observe longer holidays because of falling temperatures and snowfall. Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh have some of the longest winter vacation periods.School winter vacation 2026-27: State-wise scheduleThe following schedule outlines the reported and tentative winter vacation dates and reopening timelines across selected North Indian states and Union Territories.State/UTWinter vacationReopening dateUttar PradeshDecember 31, 2026 to January 14, 2027January 15, 2027DelhiJanuary 1 to January 15, 2027January 16, 2027HaryanaJanuary 1 to January 15, 2027January 16, 2027RajasthanDecember 31, 2026 to January 10, 2027January 11, 2027BiharDecember 25 to December 31, 2026January 1, 2027PunjabDecember 22 to December 31, 2026 (tentative)January 1, 2027 (tentative)Jammu and KashmirDecember 7, 2026 to February 28, 2027 (up to Class 8); December 14, 2026 to February 21, 2027 (Classes 9 to 12)March 1, 2027 (up to Class 8); February 22, 2027 (Classes 9 to 12)Himachal PradeshDecember 24 to December 31, 2026 (lower areas); January 1 to February 9, 2027 (winter-closing areas)Varies by zoneState-wise holiday detailsIn Uttar Pradesh, the winter break is scheduled for 15 days, covering Basic Shiksha Parishad and recognised schools. Punjab's schedule remains tentative, with extensions possible depending on temperatures.In Jammu and Kashmir, vacation periods differ according to class levels. Himachal Pradesh follows separate arrangements for lower and winter-closing areas, with extended breaks in high-altitude and snowbound regions.Weather conditions and private school calendarsDistrict administrations and education departments may revise holiday schedules or change school timings during January because of severe cold, dense fog and high pollution levels.Private schools affiliated with CBSE, CISCE and international boards generally follow their institutional calendars. Many schedule Christmas and New Year breaks from December 24 or 25 until early January.States such as Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala generally have shorter Christmas and New Year holidays rather than extended winter vacations.
