headline: Fake drug manufacturing racket spanning UP, Himachal busted | Hindustan Times
content: LUCKNOW The alleged kingpin of an interstate counterfeit drug manufacturing and supply racket has been arrested, while FIRs are being lodged against two brothers from Saharanpur for their alleged involvement. The racket reportedly spanned Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh.Following the arrest and interrogation of Abhishek Singh alias Ravi, a joint team of the Uttar Pradesh Food Safety and Drug Administration (UPFSDA) and the Special Task Force (STF) raided two illegal drug manufacturing units in Solan and Baddi in Himachal Pradesh on November 18. The raids exposed facilities manufacturing counterfeit versions of several branded medicines, FSDA officials said.The raid at Rajpura-Khera bypass in Nalagarh tehsil of Solan district led to the recovery of machinery, raw materials and packaging material used for manufacturing and replicating branded medicines. Counterfeit versions of Pan-D, Clavam 625, Shelcal 500, Zerodol-SP, Cef-200LB and several other medicines were found at the facility. Blister and aluminium-aluminium packaging machines, capsule-filling equipment, weighing machines and printed pharmaceutical foils were also seized, they said.Interrogation of Singh allegedly revealed that Haseen and Waseem, two brothers originally from Chilkhana in Saharanpur, were getting spurious medicines manufactured in Himachal Pradesh and supplying them through an interstate network. Investigators have also found evidence of illegal manufacturing, storage and sale at locations linked to the brothers in Saharanpur, where FIRs are being lodged and further legal action initiated.The investigation began on October 30 with a raid on an unlicensed medical store in Kurouna village of Varanasi, where counterfeit Nurokind-LC tablets were seized. Mankind Pharma, the original manufacturer, confirmed that the medicines were spurious following comparative examination. Other illegally stocked medicines worth around ₹5 lakh were also seized, officials said.On November 2, the team recovered 17 varieties of allopathic medicines worth around ₹2 lakh from the residence of alleged stockist Surendra Nath Mishra in Parmanandpur, Varanasi. Eleven samples were collected after suspected counterfeit Gudcef-Plus and Nurokind-LC strips were found with serious labelling and spelling errors.Mishra allegedly identified Singh as his supplier, with whom he communicated through the encrypted Zangi application. An FIR was registered at Rohania police station on November 13 against four accused under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Singh was also allegedly involved in a major counterfeit drug case registered in Varanasi in 2023.Commissioner FSDA Roshan Jacob said that a second illegal manufacturing unit, operating under the name V.D. Pharma at Juddi Kalan in Baddi, was also found. Machinery for manufacturing tablets, capsules and syrups, along with raw materials and finished and semi-finished medicines, including antibiotics, antacids and cough syrups, was recovered. Himachal Pradesh drug control authorities are initiating legal action.

headline: UP Fake Medicine Racket Exposed, ₹7.57 Crore Drugs Seized, 24 FIRs Filed; Illegal Manufacturing Units Traced
content: Lucknow: Uttar Pradesh’s crackdown on counterfeit medicines has exposed a major interstate drug manufacturing and supply network operating across multiple states. Authorities have traced the supply of fake medicines to illegal manufacturing units in Himachal Pradesh, with links extending to Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Haryana and Punjab.The Uttar Pradesh Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) has seized counterfeit and illegal medicines worth approximately ₹7.57 crore so far and registered 24 FIRs in connection with the racket. Investigations have revealed that fake versions of medicines sold under popular pharmaceutical brands were being manufactured, packaged and distributed through an organised network.The investigation began after counterfeit medicines were detected at an unlicensed medical store in Varanasi. Subsequent raids and questioning of suspects led officials to suppliers, storage locations and illegal manufacturing facilities in Himachal Pradesh.Joint teams of UP FSDA and the Special Task Force (STF) raided manufacturing units in Solan and Baddi, uncovering machinery, raw materials, semi-finished products and finished medicines. Several products allegedly carried packaging and labels resembling those of established pharmaceutical companies.Investigators found counterfeit products bearing the names of well-known pharmaceutical brands, including medicines used for infections, gastric problems, pain relief and other health conditions. The raids also led to the recovery of blister-packing machines, capsule-filling equipment, printed pharmaceutical foils and packaging materials used to replicate branded medicines.

headline: Despite best pupil-teacher ratio, 420 Himachal schools face teacher vacancies
content: Despite having the highest pupil-teacher ratio (PTR) in the country, Himachal Pradesh continues to grapple with teacher vacancies in 420 government schools, while several institutions are also facing low or zero student enrolment.This information was furnished by Education Minister Rohit Thakur in a written reply to a question by Churah MLA Hans Raj in the Vidhan Sabha on Friday. The data also highlights concerns over the condition of school infrastructure, declining enrolment and student dropouts.The state’s PTR stands at 1:12 in primary schools, 1:11 in middle schools and 1:10 in high and senior secondary schools. Chamba has the highest number of teacher vacancies at 88, followed by Solan with 63, Kangra 50, Mandi 44, Sirmaur 42, Una 37, Kullu 33, Shimla 27, Hamirpur 19, Bilaspur 15 and Kinnaur with two. Lahaul-Spiti is the only district without a school reporting a teacher vacancy.The reply also revealed significant gaps in school infrastructure. As many as 64 school buildings have been declared unsafe, forcing classes to be held in alternative rented accommodation. Another 278 buildings have been declared partially unsafe, with one or two rooms damaged, while 423 buildings require repairs. In addition, 112 schools in the state do not have electricity.Mandi has the highest number of unsafe school buildings at 21, followed by Kullu with 16. Both districts suffered extensive damage during the monsoon disasters of 2023 and 2025.The Education Department has allocated Rs 10.58 crore for repairs to 272 school buildings. In the past three years, up to November 1, 2026, it spent Rs 110.61 crore on constructing new school buildings and Rs 37.82 crore on repairing damaged structures.The data further showed a steady decline in student enrolment from Classes 1 to 12. The total number of students fell from 7,05,342 in 2024-25 to 6,71,542 in 2025-26 and 6,55,131 in 2026-27.Meanwhile, 9,747 students dropped out or changed schools in 2024-25. The number rose to 11,396 in 2025-26 and 16,497 in the current academic year.Himachal Pradesh, which ranked 21st nationally in education, has improved to fifth position over the past three years, the reply stated. The state government has undertaken measures such as rationalisation and merger of schools with low enrolment.

headline: Organisation becomes scalable when responsibility can travel: Aniruddha Singh of VCL Group
content: VCL Group has spent nearly four decades leaving its mark on India. Its hospitals, metro stations, court buildings, and runways serve communities long after the teams that built them have moved on. With over 37 years of experience, an order book exceeding ₹10,000 crore, and a workforce of over 15,000 across more than 28 cities, it is an organisation built on execution discipline and nation-building ambition. Recently recognised under Mint’s India’s Iconic Workplaces initiative, the company is now at an inflection point: how do you carry the ownership and execution discipline that built the organisation into a larger, more complex version of itself?That is the question Aniruddha Singh, VCL’s newly appointed CHRO, has stepped in to answer. “An organisation becomes scalable when responsibility can travel beyond the people who built it,” he reflects. Everything he is building at VCL flows from that conviction.Design the organisation so ownership can travelScaling a company built on strong founder-led execution demands one thing above all: making ownership transferable. For Singh, this begins with building the right structures that enable accountability, consistency and sustainable growth.“We are designing the connections between board-level governance, executive leadership, functions, regions and project sites,” he explains. “Each layer must contribute something distinctive, with clear authority and accountability.” In a project-driven organisation spread across dozens of cities, ambiguity about who owns a decision does not just slow things down. It quietly erodes initiative. “Imagine a capable engineer at a remote site who can see a problem but cannot act because responsibility is unclear,” he adds. “The cost is lost time and, eventually, lost initiative. Removing that ambiguity releases human potential as well as business capacity.”Organisation design, in his framing, is strategy translated into everyday decisions: who resolves a constraint, who commits resources, who owns the outcome. That clarity is what makes role design, leadership development, and employee experience part of the same conversation rather than separate agendas.Make ownership possible before asking for itA career spent across multinational organisations, Indian businesses, and transformation assignments has taught Singh to look past the obvious when performance falls short. The visible symptom is often an individual’s missed target. The underlying cause usually sits somewhere else: between functions, in a delayed decision, or in an expectation that was never made clear.The implication is direct. Before asking people for greater ownership, make ownership possible. “That means connecting responsibility with authority, building capability and being willing to hear uncomfortable information,” he notes. “A review meeting should make the next decision clearer, rather than leave everyone more cautious.”How leaders respond to mistakes, in his view, is as formative as any policy or programme. “I also believe leadership begins with awareness of oneself,” he notes. “The way we respond to a mistake determines whether the next mistake is reported early or concealed. The way we listen determines whether people bring us their judgement or simply wait for instructions.” That shift in the conversation is, in practice, the difference between a culture of ownership and a culture of compliance.Keep purpose visible while the work is still hardFew industries leave their output in public view the way construction does. Singh is deliberate about keeping that significance alive in the daily texture of the work, not just in retrospective pride.“I think of an employee returning years later with their family and pointing to an asset they helped build,” he shares. “The pride in that moment comes from knowing that their work has become useful to others. Our responsibility as leaders is to keep that connection alive while the work is still demanding, unfinished and under pressure.” At VCL, that means explaining the value of a project, recognising the people behind its milestones, and reinforcing why safety and workmanship matter beyond compliance.Nation building, for Singh, includes the people dimension. “A young engineer who becomes a capable leader, or a worker who gains a new skill, carries that value forward,” he points out. The legacy of an infrastructure company lives not only in the assets it delivers but in the capabilities its people take into the future.Let AI surface the question, not replace the judgmentIn construction, the gap between a dashboard and a site can be considerable. Data without context can mislead as easily as it can inform. Singh’s approach to AI is shaped by that reality.“The most valuable use of AI in construction may be to help us ask a better question about performance,” he believes. Rather than tracking how many people are deployed, AI could connect schedules, workforce capability, and site readiness so that managers can anticipate constraints before they become problems. At VCL, his immediate focus is on building the role clarity, productivity definitions, and data discipline that would make those applications meaningful. Without that foundation, AI surfaces symptoms without enabling solutions.“A red indicator on a screen cannot explain the full reality of a site,” he emphasises. “People need confidence that information will be used fairly, and consequential decisions about them need human review.” AI can reveal where attention is needed. It cannot carry a leader’s responsibility. “Judgement, courage and empathy determine whether we respond to a warning by blaming someone or by solving the problem. That choice will continue to shape the workplace.”Culture must extend beyond the corporate officeFor an organisation operating across remote sites, diverse geographies, and projects of varying scale, the risk of culture becoming uneven is real. “Culture is tested furthest from the corporate office,” he puts it plainly. “At a remote site, a supervisor’s response to a concern or a manager’s decision under pressure tells people what the organisation truly values.” The operating model must give teams clarity about standards, decisions, and escalation, while leaving room for intelligent local responses. Consistency should build confidence without eliminating initiative.When two functions share a problem but neither owns the resolution, collaboration depends on personal relationships rather than clear structure. “Clear interfaces and accountable leadership make it more reliable,” he adds. His aspiration is unambiguous. “Distance should never determine how much an employee feels valued,” he stresses.That commitment to consistency, whether on a site in a remote city or in a leadership review at headquarters, is ultimately what Singh believes an iconic workplace must be judged by. Mint’s India’s Iconic Workplaces recognition, for Singh, raises the standard rather than marks an arrival. “I would judge our progress by what happens after the celebration,” he reflects, “how a new engineer is supported, how a site concern is resolved and whether a capable person can see a path to greater responsibility.” These ordinary moments are where a workplace’s reputation becomes real. “For me, an iconic workplace is one that keeps earning its people’s trust as it grows. That is the ambition I bring to VCL: to help build an institution whose strength is visible both in what it delivers and in the people it develops.”Disclaimer: No journalist from the Mint team was involved in the creation of this article.

headline: Mint Explainer | Why Himachal Pradesh, the nation’s pharmacy, is also a hub of fake drugs
content: This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. New Delhi: A joint raid by teams of Himachal Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh officials busted a unit making medicines without a licence in the Rajpura area of Nalagarh in Solan district on Thursday. Two people were arrested. The raid once again highlights the problem of fake drugs made in Himachal Pradesh, where one-third of the medicines sold in India are manufactured. People making fake drugs use the state's name to add credibility to the unlicensed medicines they try to sell. Mint explains the issue and why it matters for health safety. The raid began after counterfeit drugs were found being sold in the Varanasi area in Uttar Pradesh in October. The Uttar Pradesh Food and Drug Administration alerted the Himachal Pradesh Drug Control Administration about a place in Solan district where the spurious drugs were allegedly being made. Officials found medicine-making machines, finished tablets and capsules, and packing material inside a building operating without any government licence to manufacture drugs. They seized 67,000 tablets made of two antibiotic ingredients, cefixime and azithromycin, and 6,500 capsules of Pregabalin 300 mg, a medicine used for nerve pain and epilepsy. The officials also found 100 kg of printed aluminium foil carrying the names of other medicine companies, meant for packing the fake drugs under well-known brands.

headline: Himachal tables Bill for single-window mechanism to boost investment | Hindustan Times
content: The Himachal Pradesh government on Thursday introduced the Himachal Pradesh Investment Promotion and Facilitation Bill, 2026, in the state legislative assembly, proposing a series of measures to promote investment and industrial development in the state.The Bill, introduced by industries minister Harshwardhan Chauhan during the ongoing winter session in Dharamshala, seeks to establish a comprehensive framework for investment facilitation, including a time-bound approvals, digital processing of applications, self-certification, auto-renewal of specified approvals and reduction of regulatory compliance requirements.Under the proposed legislation, the government will establish a single window approval, Clearance, Reviewing and Monitoring Authority, headed by the chief minister, with the industries minister as its vice-chairperson. The chief secretary and secretaries of industries, revenue, power, finance, and environment, science and technology will be its members.The authority will be responsible for ensuring time-bound processing, approval and implementation of investment proposals. It may also constitute project review and approval committees at the state and regional levels to examine proposals and expedite clearances.Investment promotion, facilitation cellThe Bill also proposes setting up a dedicated Investment Promotion and Facilitation Cell in the industries department to assist investors in obtaining approvals and coordinating with various state and central government departments.The legislation provides for the creation of a land bank comprising public and private land parcels. The government may acquire land in accordance with the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, and make government land available for industrial clusters, estates, common facilitation centres and related infrastructure.It also empowers the government to notify financial and non-financial incentives, concessions and rebates for entrepreneurs in accordance with the applicable industrial policy. The proposed framework allows the government to develop industrial infrastructure through public-private partnerships (PPP), constitute special purpose vehicles and implementing agencies, and create a corpus fund to finance infrastructure development, land acquisition, capacity building and digital facilitation.The Bill additionally proposes measures to optimise land use in notified industrial areas, including flexibility in subdivision and amalgamation of plots, sub-leasing and transfer of land-use rights. It also provides for the designation of green industrial corridors and green industrial zones to minimise ecological disturbance.Govt introduces Sukhashray Bill to grant legal status to welfare schemesThe Himachal Pradesh government has proposed a legislation to provide statutory backing to its welfare schemes for orphaned, abandoned and surrendered children, as well as vulnerable women lacking adequate livelihood opportunities and family support.The state government on Thursday introduced the Himachal Pradesh Sukhashray (Social Security of Women and Children of the State) Bill 2026 in the legislative assembly, seeking to ensure continuity, effective implementation and timely delivery of benefits under schemes such as the Mukhyamantri Sukh Ashray Yojana and the Indira Gandhi Sukh Shiksha Yojana.The legislation, introduced by chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, aims to provide care, financial security, housing, education and rehabilitation to “children of the state” and vulnerable women without adequate means of livelihood.Under the Bill, “children of the state” include individuals aged between zero and 27 years, including male, female and transgender persons, who are orphans, abandoned or surrendered, under foster care, sponsorship or aftercare, as well as children of eligible women beneficiaries. The Bill also provides a statutory framework for the Sukhashray Kosh, retaining its initial corpus of ₹101 crore while allowing it to receive donations and corporate social responsibility contributions.‘648 industrial projects cleared in Himachal in three years’The Himachal Pradesh government has approved 648 industrial projects through its single-window clearance mechanism over the past three years.Replying to a question by Jaswan-Pragpur MLA Bikram Singh in the assembly on Thursday, the industries department said 148 projects were approved by the State Level Single Window Clearance and Monitoring Authority, while 500 were cleared by the State Review Committee.Of the 148 projects, 24 have started commercial production and 110 are taking steps towards establishment. Similarly, 77 of the 500 projects cleared by the review committee have commenced production, while 385 are in the process of setting up units.

headline: Congress names 81 secretaries ahead of 2027 polls, retains Uttar Pradesh team
content: NEW DELHI: The Congress on Thursday announced a reshuffle of its organisational structure, assigning 81 AICC secretaries to states, Union Territories and functional departments ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections, while relieving 25 outgoing secretaries and joint secretaries of their responsibilities.The changes, approved by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, take effect immediately, according to a statement issued by general secretary K C Venugopal.In poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, the party retained its six-member secretary team comprising Abhishek Dutt, Varun Choudhary, Kunal Choudhary, Jagdish Chander Jangid, Abdul Hannan and Sanjeev Arya. The state has the largest number of secretaries in the new list.Rahul Gandhi was involved in the selection process, holding one-on-one meetings with candidates for AICC secretary positions.The exercise followed a review in September, when Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and K C Venugopal met 64 AICC secretaries in groups. Each interaction lasted around 30 minutes.Rahul asked the secretaries about their work, challenges faced and the time they spent in their assigned states. He and Priyanka also asked them to identify five leading Congress workers in their respective states and name the three AICC secretaries they considered the best performers.Among other poll-bound states, Punjab has been assigned four secretaries — Hina Kaware, Ravindra Dalvi, Suraj Singh Thakur and Raj Kumar Maurya. Gujarat also has four, comprising Ramkishan Ojha, Subhashini Yadav, Hem Singh Shekhawat and Naresh Thakur.Manoj Yadav, Surender Sharma and Bhim Kumar have been assigned Uttarakhand, while Kamal Kant Sharma and Rahul Rajbhar will handle Himachal Pradesh and Chandigarh. Anjali Nimbalkar has been assigned Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Daman and Diu.Dheeraj Gurjar and Sushil Kumar Pasi will handle Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. Bihar has been assigned Pradeep Narwal, Prakash Sonawane and Mahaboob Pasha.Pranav Jha and Gaurav Pandhi have been assigned to the Congress president's office, while Vineet Punia and Ruchira Chaturvedi will handle communication, publicity and media, including social and digital media.Among those relieved of their responsibilities are Divya Maderna, Amba Prasad, Sanjana Jatav, Roji M John, T N Prathapan and B M Sandeep.The reshuffle comes three days after the Congress constituted screening committees for Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa and Manipur ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: World Bank to assist CAG in urban governance audit for 101 Indian cities
content: New Delhi: The World bank will assist India's Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) in examining how 101 Indian cities manage their finances, build infrastructure and deliver essential public services, as growing urban needs put pressure on municipal resources. The multilateral agency will provide technical expertise and international best practices to support the audit. The CAG is conducting a multi-year audit of urban infrastructure and services, starting with urban mobility, to provide a comprehensive assessment of municipal governance, finances and service delivery. The exercise will subsequently cover water and sanitation, housing, air quality management and liveable urban environments, with a different theme taken up each year, the comptroller and auditor general K. Sanjay Murthy said on Friday.The World Bank initiative, 'Strengthening Audit Capacity and Governance Accountability in India's Urban Sector', has been endorsed by the department of economic affairs. The exercise comes against the backdrop of growing need to strengthen municipal finances through better revenue mobilization, improved cost recovery and innovative financing mechanisms that are critical for cities to meet growing infrastructure and service delivery needs. Infrastructure push The Union budget for 2026-27 also underscored government's focus on urban infrastructure development and the need to boost finance streams of urban local bodies, particularly for their ability to diversify revenue sources, improve financial sustainability and mobilize resources for expanding civic infrastructure.Speaking at a two-day workshop on urban infrastructure financing and municipal finance in New Delhi, Murthy said the audit of 101 cities would provide a holistic and comparable assessment of how cities are performing. He called for a sectoral approach to auditing so that multiple aspects of urban development could be assessed together.The CAG emphasised that the delivery of services to citizens should remain central to the audit process. He highlighted the apex auditor's unique position, with access to all tiers of government across the country, to contribute constructively to the urban reform process.The World Bank's technical assistance is expected to bring international experience and technical depth to the exercise, particularly in assessing municipal finances, infra financing and delivery of urban services.Paul Procee, operations manager and acting country director of the World Bank's India office said the organization looked forward to supporting efforts to improve the quality of public service delivery and government initiatives aimed at enhancing public trust.The workshop draws on case studies from India and international best practices to provide actionable inputs for the audit process.

headline: MP Sribharat Wants Teamwork to Strengthen Rural Governance
content: Visakhapatnam MP M. Sribharat on Friday called for greater coordination among elected representatives to strengthen local bodies and accelerate rural development. Addressing the swearing-in ceremony at the Visakhapatnam zilla parishad (ZP) as a co-opted member, the MP congratulated the newly elected ZP chairperson Gadu Aliveni and vice chairperson Sukavasi Ajay. Anandapuram ZPTC member Enni Srinivasa Rao and Padmanabham ZPTC member Korada Satyavathi took their oath.Sribharat pointed out that the zilla parishad leadership has been allotted to the TD under the alliance arrangement. Noting that only four mandals currently remain under the zilla parishad's jurisdiction, as most parts of the district fall under the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation, the MP stressed the need for effective utilisation of local body funds.He said priority should be given to improving basic infrastructure in villages, including roads, drinking water supply, and sanitation facilities. Referring to the coalition government's focus on rural development under the leadership of Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan, Sribharat asked ZPTC and MPTC members, apart from sarpanches, to regularly visit villages, understand people’s grievances, and resolve them through coordinated efforts.Expressing confidence in the newly elected representatives, the MP asked them to work as a team, uphold public trust, and ensure better services for rural residents.

headline: Woman burnt alive, 3 injured as SUV hits bikes amid stubble-fire smoke in Punjab
content: A woman was burnt alive and three others were seriously injured in a freak accident in Punjab’s Ludhiana district, allegedly caused by poor visibility after a thick blanket of smoke from stubble burning engulfed the area on Thursday. On Friday, the Khanna police booked the farmer who had set the stubble in his fields on fire, and the driver of an SUV which collided with two motorcycles near Jaipura village. Harmanpreet Singh Cheema, Deputy Superintendent of Police (Payal), said the SUV collided with two bikes because of poor visibility caused by heavy smoke from nearby burning fields. The woman, identified as Manjit Kaur, 50, from Shahpur village, who was travelling on one of the bikes with her husband, was burnt alive on the spot. Her husband, Nagendra Singh, also suffered serious injuries and was referred to Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH), Ludhiana. Another couple who were travelling on the second bike - Jaspal Singh and his wife Surinder Kaur - also received fractures due to the collision and were admitted at the local Sidhu Hospital in Doraha, said the police. Field of fire In his statement to the police, Nagendra said he and his wife had visited Jaipura village to meet their daughter. While returning, around 4 pm, they reached a stretch of road where smoke from stubble burning in a nearby field had severely reduced visibility. The smoke had engulfed the entire area, leaving them unable to see the road ahead, he said. He said an SUV coming from the opposite side first collided with their motorcycle, and then with the other bike. He added that he and his wife, along with their bike, were tossed into the field, which was set on fire. “Our bike caught fire and there was an explosion as the flames engulfed the bike’s fuel tank. My wife was burnt to death on the spot in the burning fields and I also received severe injuries. The couple on the other bike also got injured,” he added. The Doraha police registered a First Information Report (FIR) against Gurdeep Singh, the farmer who had set stubble on fire, and Hardeep Singh, the SUV driver, for the offences including culpable homicide not amounting to murder, rash driving, act endangering life, causing grievous hurt, among others, under the sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). DSP Cheema said they will soon arrest both accused, who are missing.

headline: Punjab records 23.5% decline despite 22.4% spike in stubble burning incidents
content: Even as Punjab has recorded a sharp increase in paddy-residue fire incidents this season compared to last year, the actual agricultural area affected by stubble burning has declined by 23.5 per cent, revealing a significant divergence between the number of fires detected and the extent of land burnt. A district-wise analysis of satellite-based burnt-area data, compiled through the Punjab Pollution Control Board (PPCB), for the period September 15 to November 15 shows that the cumulative burnt area across Punjab fell from 19.41 lakh hectares in 2025 to 14.84 lakhhectares this year. This represents a net reduction of 4.57 lakh hectares. The decline was widespread, with 21 of Punjab's 23 districts registering a reduction in burnt area. Only two districts recorded an increase, both marginal. SAS Nagar saw its burnt area rise from 19,870 hectares last year to 21,780 hectares this year (an increase of 1,910 hectares, or 9.6 per cent), while Hoshiarpur recorded a marginal increase of 0.24 thousand hectares (0.8 per cent), from 31,740 to 31,980 hectares. The reduction in affected acreage comes despite a substantial increase in fire detections. Between September 15 and November 15, the state recorded 5,972 farm-fire incidents, up 22.4 per cent from 4,877 during the corresponding period in 2025. The gap widened further over the next four days: by November 19, the cumulative number of incidents had reached 6,874, compared to 5,034 last year — a jump of 36.5 per cent. Agricultural officials say one reason for the divergence could be a change in the extent of burning within individual fields. In some instances, farmers resort to partial burning of crop residue instead of setting entire fields on fire. Such instances are counted as individual fire incidents in satellite-based fire detection, irrespective of how much of the field is actually affected. Consequently, a higher number of fire detections does not necessarily translate into a proportionate increase in the total area burnt, added sources. PPCB sources said the two parameters capture different aspects of stubble burning: fire incidents indicate the number of detected ignition events, while burnt-area mapping helps assess the geographical extent of land affected. The latter, therefore, provides an important additional measure for understanding the actual spread of burning across agricultural fields. The distinction is significant for this year's figures. Despite the increase in the number of fire incidents, the satellite-based assessment shows that the overall burnt footprint has contracted substantially, suggesting that the fires have not translated into comparable increases in the area affected. Major gainers and laggards Among Punjab's major paddy-growing belts, Ferozepur recorded the steepest absolute reduction in burnt area, with a decline of 61,320 hectares, from 1.36 lakh hectares in 2025 to around 75,000 hectares this year. Sangrur, traditionally a major hotspot, followed with a reduction of 53,450 hectares, from 1.84 lakh to 1.31 lakh hectares, while Moga recorded a decline of 51,770 hectares, from 1.08 lakh to 56,690 hectares. Bathinda and Barnala completed the top five districts in terms of absolute reductions, with burnt areas declining by 41,990 hectares (from 1.25 lakh to 83,270 hectares) and 36,700 hectares (from 82,007 to 45,370 hectares), respectively. In percentage terms, Moga led the state with a 47.7 per cent reduction in burnt area, followed by Ferozepur (45.0 per cent), Barnala (44.7 per cent), Pathankot (44.0 per cent) and Mansa (42.4 per cent). Faridkot, too, recorded a 28 per cent reduction in burnt area, from 56,830 hectares to 41,000 hectares this year. However, the improvements were not uniform across the state, with several districts recording only modest reductions. Gurdaspur's burnt area declined by just 2.2 per cent, from 1.03 lakh hectares to one lakh hectares. Kapurthala recorded a 3.1 per cent reduction (75,330 to 73,030 hectares), Fazilka a 6.0 per cent decline (34,440 to 32,350 hectares), and SBS Nagar an 8.6 per cent reduction (31,002 to 28,350 hectares). The bigger picture The reduction assumes added significance when viewed against the scale of paddy cultivation in Punjab. The state's total rice acreage stood at 32.87 lakh hectares this year, of which around 26 lakh hectares was under paddy (non-Basmati), with the remaining area under Basmati. Satellite imagery had recorded 29.54 lakh hectares by November 15, leaving the final 15 days of the monitoring period, which runs from September 15 to November 30, still to be accounted for. Sangrur accounted for the largest share of the state's rice acreage at 2.36 lakh hectares, followed by Ludhiana (2.25 lakh hectares), Patiala (2.13 lakh hectares) and Bathinda (2.08 lakh hectares). The November 15 figures, therefore, offer a comparative picture of the extent of burning so far, rather than the final seasonal assessment. Both farm-fire incidents and burnt-area data continue to be monitored through November 30, and the remaining 15 days could add to the cumulative figures.

headline: Warring rides Chann’s cycle, puts Punjab faction feud on back pedal
content: The Punjab Congress on Thursday got a much needed shot in the arm as party's former state unit chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring joined former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi’s ‘Jawani Sambhal’ Yatra, hours after announcing his own ‘Insaaf March’, sending out a message of unity amid reports of political rivalry between the two leaders. Warring, the Ludhiana MP, joined Jawani Sambhal yatra at Beeja village in the district and cycled nearly 14 km with Channi till Khanna, where the week-long campaign concluded with a public rally. AICC in-charge for Punjab Sachin Pilot, PPCC president Pargat Singh, senior leaders Raj Babbar, Sukhpal Singh Khaira and Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa among others joined them. The sight of Warring sharing the stage with Channi came against the backdrop of months of differences between the two leaders over the Punjab Congress leadership. At a press conference in Ludhiana earlier in the day, where he announced the statewide ‘Insaaf March’, Warring had hinted that he could join Channi’s yatra, saying all Congress leaders were running campaigns on different issues and that the former chief minister was also their leader. “Maybe you will see all of us cycling with him soon,” he had said. In the evening, that remark turned into a show of unity as almost the entire top Punjab Congress leadership joined Channi for the concluding leg of his yatra. Channi’s week-long yatra had started from Chamkaur Sahib, an Assembly constituency that he had represented in the Vidhan Sabha thrice and considered his stronghold, on November 12. Pilot, Pargat Singh, Leader of Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa and Khaira were among those present at the flag-off. Warring had stayed away from the launch and had also not joined when the yatra moved through Ludhiana, the Lok Sabha constituency he represents, on November 13. Four of his loyalist former MLAs — Rakesh Pandey, Kuldip Vaid, Surinder Dawar and Sanjay Talwar — had also stayed away. Three-term former MLA Bharat Bhushan Ashu was then the only prominent Congress leader from Ludhiana Urban to participate. Warring's absence had fuelled speculation about continuing differences between him and Channi camps, particularly after the former CM's supporters had opposed the Ludhiana MP's continuation as Punjab Congress chief. The party eventually removed Warring and appointed Pargat Singh as state president. However, Warring on Thursday sought to brush aside any differences. “We all are one. Please stop asking questions on infighting,” he said, asserting that Congress leaders were running different campaigns as part of the broader Punjab Mangda Hisab' campaign, which was launched by Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi from Sangrur on November 4. "The motive is only to strengthen the Congress, not any show of strength. We all are taking forward the campaign which was started by Rahul Gandhi, Sachin Pilot and Pargat Singh. And in case you want to hear this particular name, we all are also working under the leadership of Sardar Charanjit Singh Channi. He is also our leader, and so is Pandey, Dawar, and myself. We all are one and a part of Congress,” he said. “Channi’s cycle yatra is also of the Congress party, not an individual,” he said, adding that the media should stop interpreting the absence of individual leaders from particular programmes as evidence of factionalism. "If some party leader doesn't put the photo of his colleague on the hoardings, it doesn't mean they are enemies," he said, seeking to play down the row that had erupted after his photo was missing from the initial posters issued for Channi's yatra. Addressing the cycle yatra’s concluding rally in Khanna, Warring also hit out at Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann. “Everyday (CM) Mann says that Congress is fractured. Let me tell him today, we are one and united. It doesn’t matter if the pardhaan is Warring or Pargat or someone else.From today, stop saying that there's infighting in Congress”. Warring also spoke on his reported differences with Pilot. “Sachin Pilot is my elder brother. He is the only person in entire Punjab who can rebuke me and I obey what he says. I congratulate Channi saab for the cycle yatra. We will bring Congress to power under leadership of Rahul Gandhi and Pilot”. Responding to Warring from the stage, Pilot said: “I have heard you a lot…you are an MP and have remained an MLA, a minister…but the truth is, neta waala bhaashan aapne aaj diya hai…(today you have spoken like a leader). I congratulate you…Congress is in your blood. We all can have personal interests but not at the cost of Punjab. We can get big posts but if Punjab is going to hell, then it is of no use. I can see Congress is winning Punjab”. Channi too spoke about party being united. “Have you ever seen Bhagwant Mann sharing the stage with his party colleagues? Never. He always stands alone. His own party colleagues don’t support him,” he said. The Congress has stepped up its political activity in Punjab ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections after Rahul Gandhi launched ‘Punjab Mangda Hisab’ campaign with an ‘Insaaf Rally’ in Sangrur on November 4. Pargat Singh, Bajwa and Khaira subsequently led the party’s ‘Punjab Mangda Jawab’ bus rally, while Channi launched his cycle yatra. Warring's ‘Insaaf March’ will start from Ludhiana Central constituency on November 21, beginning from Chaura Bazar and ending at Clock Tower. He said similar marches would be held across Ludhiana and subsequently in other parts of Punjab, including Zira, Bathinda, Mansa and Sri Muktsar Sahib. "This march will continue till voting in Punjab," he said, adding the yatra will raise the question 'Insaaf Kithe Hai?' and seek accountability from the Bhagwant Mann government over the drug menace, gangsterism, law and order and the state’s economic condition. “The motive is only to strengthen the Congress, not any show of strength,” Warring said, rejecting suggestions that the march was aimed at projecting his own political camp. Targeting the AAP government over law and order, he claimed 170 murder cases had been reported in Ludhiana between 2022 and 2024 and alleged that traders were living under threat of extortion. He also accused the government of failing to check the drug menace.

headline: When a child falls ill, Ludhiana govt schools have no medic to turn to
content: Ludhiana: If a child suddenly falls ill, gets injured or faces a medical emergency in a Ludhiana govt school, there is no dedicated medical room or trained medical staff on campus to attend to them.Govt primary and middle schools across the district are functioning without dedicated medical facilities or a designated post for handling medical emergencies involving students or teachers, education department officials and school staff told TOI.Visits to govt schools and conversations with teachers and education officials revealed that schools largely make do with limited resources. Teachers at a govt primary school said students receive iron supplements once a month and deworming tablets twice a year under prescribed schedules, but the school has no other dedicated medical facility.The medicines are obtained from nearby govt dispensaries based on the strength and requirements of individual schools.A teacher at another govt school said staff sometimes keep a limited stock of basic medicines themselves. Blood pressure monitors were distributed to schools a few months ago, but there is no trained medical staff to deal with emergencies.“The teachers mostly keep a limited stock of basic medicines, but there are no other medical facilities available in govt schools,” the teacher said, adding that BP monitoring machines had recently been provided.Deputy DEO (primary) Manoj Kumar acknowledged eh limited facilities and said the block primary education officers concerned would be better placed to provide details of any further measures. Deputy DEO (secondary) Amandeep Singh said the situation was similar in schools beyond the primary level.District education officer Dimple Madaan was unavailable for comment.BOX | What schools lackNo dedicated medical roomsNo trained medical staffNo designated post to handle medical emergenciesBP monitors among the limited equipment availableStudents receive iron supplements and deworming tablets under prescribed schedulesYou Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ludhiana | Silver Rate in Ludhiana | Bank Holidays in Ludhiana | Public Holidays in Ludhiana | Petrol Price in Ludhiana | Diesel Price in Ludhiana | CNG Price in Ludhiana | LPG Price in LudhianaStay updated with the latest Ludhiana news. headline: Probe finds lapses in Bholath procurement; 2 officials put on notice
content: The Punjab Government has initiated action against two officials following an inquiry into alleged irregularities in paddy procurement at Bholath. A PUNSUP probe found “procedural lapses”, following which notices have been issued to a mandi inspector and a field officer, a senior PUNSUP official told The Tribune.The action comes amid calls for a CBI probe into the alleged bogus procurement raised by Ferozepur MP Sher Singh Ghubaya, who also chairs the FCI’s State-Level Consultative Committee.In a letter to the Union Food and Supplies Minister, a copy of which is with The Tribune, Ghubaya alleged that misuse of the digital procurement system and the inflow of paddy from other states could undermine the credibility of the national procurement mechanism. He pointed out that gate passes for 22,000 bags of paddy were generated at Bholath and the produce was loaded in the mandi, transported and unloaded at a rice sheller in five hours.Ghubaya sought an investigation to determine whether the paddy had actually been produced in the area. Meanwhile, commission agents from Bholath have written to CM Bhagwant Mann, alleging the involvement of five commission agents, rice mill owners and a mandi inspector in the case. Separately, the Punjab Food and Supplies Department has constituted a four-member committee in Abohar to conduct a financial audit of the alleged bogus procurement.

headline: Punjab's Stubble-Burning Crisis Persists As Alternatives Are Costly For Small Farmers
content: PUNJAB, India – Farmer Ravinder Singh looks worried. He has just harvested his rice paddy crop and hired labourers to clear the remaining crop residue from his field. But the window for preparing the land and sowing the next crop is narrow, leaving him little time. Standing at the boundary of his field, Singh calls out to the labourers, urging them to finish their tea quickly and return to work. He hires labourers from nearby villages, paying each around ₹7,000 (approximately $70) to clear his fields. The arrangement serves two purposes: it gets his fields ready for the next crop and provides fodder for his animals during the winter. Every year, between October and November, farmers across Punjab harvest their rice crops and begin preparing their fields for the next sowing season. Nearly one million farmers in the state follow a rice-wheat cropping system, cultivating two crops a year. This leaves them with a narrow window of around 25 days to clear the leftover paddy stubble and prepare the land for wheat cultivation. The system has played a crucial role in India’s food security. Punjab contributes around 46.24% of the nation’s wheat and 31.22% of its rice.

headline: Madhya Pradesh scraps two-children limit for State government employees | Explained
content: The story so far: The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) scrapped the State government’s 25-year-old policy which put restrictions on serving government employees from having more than two living children while making aspirants who had more than two children ineligible for government jobs. In a brief, the government said that the reason behind the move was the declining fertility rates in the State as well as in the country. The move, however, holds significance as it comes amid a growing push by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) for Hindu families to consider having three children due to concerns over what it describes as “demographic imbalance” and varying birth rates across communities. At a special Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav at the Gandhi Sagar Forest Retreat in Mandsaur district, the Council of Ministers approved an amendment into the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services Rules to remove the provision and the related clarification concerning ‘more than two living children’. “The Cabinet approved the removal of Sub-rule (6) of Rule 6 of the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1961. It also approved the deletion of the clarification concerning ‘more than two living children’ mentioned in Sub-rule (4) of Rule 22 of the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1965,” the government said in a statement. The first provision held candidates with more than two children ineligible for government jobs, while the second treated having more than two children as a misconduct.

headline: PM to visit Bihar on 21 November
content: PM to inaugurate, lay foundation stones and dedicate to the nation development projects worth around Rs. 34,470 crore in Vaishali Projects span road connectivity, energy, urban infrastructure, water resources, education, healthcare and transport PM to dedicate Nitish Setu, a six-lane cable-stayed bridge across River Ganga, to the nation Bridge to ease traffic congestion and strengthen connectivity between North and South Bihar Griha Pravesh of over 26,900 PMAY (Urban) beneficiaries to also be held Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit Bihar on 21 November 2026. At around 1:15 PM, the Prime Minister will visit Nitish Setu in Vaishali district. Thereafter, at around 2 PM, he will inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects and lay the foundation stone of several projects worth around Rs. 34,470 crore in Vaishali. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.

headline: PM to visit West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh on 21 November
content: PM to participate in Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur PM to participate in the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow 52 national-level toppers from Industrial Training Institutes, National Skill Training Institutes and Institutes for Training of Trainers to be felicitated for outstanding achievements Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh on 21 November 2026. At around 9:45 AM, Prime Minister will participate in the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. After that, he will travel to Bihar to lay the foundation stone and inaugurate development projects in Vaishali. Thereafter, Prime Minister will travel to Uttar Pradesh. At around 5:30 PM, Prime Minister will participate in the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Gomti Nagar, Lucknow. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. Prime Minister will participate in the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur. He will also interact with 75 students of IIT Kharagpur, symbolising the Institute’s 75-year journey. IIT Kharagpur, established in 1951, was the first Indian Institute of Technology to be set up in the country. Recognised as an Institute of National Importance, it has played a pioneering role in advancing technical education, research and innovation in India.

headline: Doctor Recommended? UP Cracks Down On Health Supplement Claims, Bans Misleading Info On Labels
content: ‘Diabetes Care’, ‘Kidney Care’ and ‘Doctor Recommended’ – claims like these on health supplements will no longer be allowed in Uttar Pradesh, as the state’s food regulator has tightened its oversight of unproven claims in the nutraceutical sector, News18 has learnt. The regulator has directed manufacturers, sellers and e-commerce platforms to comply with rules on labelling, declarations, warning statements, health claims and operational requirements. The Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA), Uttar Pradesh, issued the order on 10 November. The order follows a review of products, which are manufactured, imported, marketed and sold in the state, including through e-commerce platforms. It says several products “exhibit apparent non-compliance with the applicable provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and regulations made thereunder.” The instances of concern include “non-compliant product formulations, not abiding with the prescribed dosage limit/RDA, use of unauthorised ingredients, misleading product and brand names, impermissible disease-related claims, inappropriate labelling declarations, inadequate scientific substantiation and non-adherence with prescribed conditions of manufacturing and marketing.” According to experts, such orders need constant monitoring to be effective enough. “It would need serious monitoring to check and penalise. If it is dependent on complaints, it won’t help the public,” said Arun Gupta, a paediatrician and child nutrition advocate in India. Health claims under scrutiny One of the most important moves is that the products cannot claim or suggest the prevention, treatment, diagnosis or cure of any human disease or disorder, “as such claims classify the product as an unauthorised drug”. Product names, brand names and trademarks that directly or indirectly suggest a product can cure, prevent, mitigate or treat diseases are also barred. This includes disease-specific and organ-specific branding. Claims that go beyond basic nutritional content into enhanced physiological performance require “rigorous documentation and scientific proof and approval from the Food Authority,” the order said. Claims made on e-commerce portals, brand websites, social media and paid advertisements “must precisely match the product label”. E-commerce platforms have been told to take appropriate corrective measures “including delisting of non-compliant products and suspension of their sale, wherever warranted under the applicable provisions.” Commenting on the move, public-health specialist Dr Rajeev Jayadevan said, “Not everyone is well-versed in medical terminology or has the healthcare training to critically analyse the contents of nutritional products available for direct purchase. When a person looks at a health supplement or specialised nutrition product on a store shelf or online, they need a clear idea not only of what the product is, but also of what it is not.” He believes accurate labelling is “a priority”, and this directive reinforces existing national food safety regulations. “Inappropriate labels can sometimes mislead patients into believing a product will treat or cure their disease. This could inadvertently even prompt a few patients to substitute it for their prescribed medications or lifestyle, potentially worsening their health. Also, he added, “Clarity is needed in stating the underlying scientific evidence and rationale, and also in the language used on the pack – it must be easily read and understood by everyday customers.” Warnings and labelling Every pack must prominently display the bold warning “not for medicinal use”. It must also carry a declaration stating “Not to exceed the recommended daily usage”, and an instruction that the product be “Stored out of reach of children”. Known side effects, contraindications, precautions and possible product-drug interactions must be declared wherever applicable. Each pack must state its exact category, such as “health supplement” or “nutraceuticals”, on the front. Health supplements and nutraceuticals must state each active ingredient or nutrient as a percentage of the Indian Council of Medical Research’s (ICMR) Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA). Who does it apply to? The directions apply to all Food Business Operators (FBOs) operating in Uttar Pradesh, whether they are established in the state or in other states or Union Territories. This covers manufacturers, importers, contract manufacturers, re-labellers, re-packers, brand owners, marketers, distributors, wholesalers, stockists, retailers and e-commerce platforms. The order states, “No FBO shall avoid its regulatory responsibility merely by attributing the non-compliance to another entity in the supply chain.”

headline: Mizoram State-Level Stakeholder Outreach Programme on Leveraging Free Trade Agreement Opportunities
content: The Department of Commerce (DoC), Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India, in collaboration with the Regional DGFT Authority, Guwahati, and Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Mizoram —with India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) as the Knowledge Partner—successfully convened a comprehensive State-Level Workshop on “Leveraging Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) – Outreach Programme” today at Woodland Hills, Aizawl, Mizoram. The high-level outreach brought together central and state policymakers, sectoral specialists, export promotion councils, entrepreneurs and local micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to establish a coordinated institutional framework for export competitiveness. Addressing the gathering as the Chief Guest, Shri F. Rodingliana, Hon’ble Minister for Commerce, Industries, Geology & Mining Department, Government of Mizoram, highlighted the critical role of MSMEs in the State’s economy, noting that MSMEs in the State contribute significantly to employment and economic activity. He highlighted about the state popular handholding scheme-Bana Kaih and its role in promoting entrepreneurial culture, and utilization of state rich bamboo resources while keeping export-oriented focus. He further mentioned one pressing challenge in some existing industrial area about encroachment, and the department willingness to a lot land among aspiring and eligible entrepreneurs. He emphasised that, given the State’s limited domestic market, sustained growth would depend on value addition, export diversification, and integration into regional and global value chains, particularly through neighbouring international markets. He further underscored the importance of enhancing FTA awareness and capacity-building and encouraged local enterprises to access opportunities in FTA partner countries by adopting international quality standards and export-ready packaging practices. Addressing the event as the Guest of Honour, Shri Richard Vanlalhmangaiha, Hon’ble Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha), underscored the significant opportunities arising from India’s expanding network of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and emphasized the need to ensure that MSMEs from Mizoram fully leverage the market access and trade benefits offered under these agreements. He encouraged local entrepreneurs and businesses to actively explore international markets, diversify their export footprint, and secure greater value realization for their products. He observed that Mizoram occupies a strategic geographic position as a natural economic bridge linking the North Eastern Region with Southeast Asian supply chain corridors. By effectively harmonizing FTA preferential provisions with the Act East Policy and multimodal transport networks, Mizoram can emerge as a vital regional international trade hub. Delivering the context-setting keynote address, Dr. C. Vanlalramsanga, IES, Economic Adviser, Department of Commerce, Government of India, emphasized upon the true measure of an FTA’s success lies not merely in the number of agreements signed, but in the economic opportunities, enterprise growth and sustainable livelihoods created through them. He further reiterated that international trade is increasingly accessible to farmers, artisans, entrepreneurs, self-help groups, women-led producer groups and micro-enterprises, enabling smaller businesses to participate directly in global markets. In this context, the FTA outreach initiative seeks to ensure that the benefits of preferential trade reach districts, production clusters and aspiring entrepreneurs across Mizoram and the wider North Eastern Region. He further noted that while Indian exports remain concentrated in a few states, Mizoram has an opportunity to strengthen its position in international trade by leveraging its local products, strategic international borders with Myanmar and Bangladesh, and emerging FTA opportunities. Dr. Vanlalramsanga also highlighted the Government of India’s efforts to improve the ease of doing business through digitalisation of trade processes, simplified regulatory procedures and stronger export facilitation mechanisms. He underscored that effective collaboration between the Central and State Governments, industry and local enterprises will be critical to translating FTA opportunities into tangible economic growth and prosperity for Mizoram. Dr H. headline: BJP moves poll commission over nomination process ‘irregularities’
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has approached the Punjab State Election Commission, alleging irregularities in the nomination process for the re-elections to 30 wards of the Municipal Corporation.The party has expressed apprehension that nomination papers of its candidates could be rejected during scrutiny on the grounds of incomplete documentation.In a representation submitted on Thursday, BJP district president Vijay Kumar Kuka, on behalf of the party candidates, alleged that the Returning Officers had refused to issue receipts or acknowledgements listing the documents submitted along with the nomination papers.The BJP apprehended that the election authorities might subsequently raise objections over missing documents and reject its candidates’ nominations during scrutiny. The party maintained that all its candidates had retained copies of the documents submitted and were ready to provide photocopies immediately if any deficiency was pointed out.Seeking urgent intervention, Kuka urged the State Election Commissioner to direct the Returning Officers to issue acknowledgements to every BJP candidate, specifying the documents received along with their nomination papers.Referring to the Supreme Court’s September 28, 2026, order directing videography of the nomination filing and scrutiny processes for the Patiala MC re-elections, the BJP sought preservation of the video recordings and their examination in the presence of Observers before any objection regarding missing documents was entertained.It further demanded that scrutiny be conducted under videography and in the presence of Observers, with reasoned orders passed on every objection and copies provided to the candidates concerned.Party questions SDO postingThe BJP has also alleged violation of directions issued by the Supreme Court-appointed Monitoring Committee in connection with the ongoing MC re-elections.In its complaint, the party alleged that SDO Rajdeep Singh of the Municipal Corporation, Patiala, had been assigned duties without obtaining the mandatory permission of the committee.The BJP also questioned his transfer and posting, alleging that the move could be aimed at extending undue benefits to certain Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) candidates ahead of the civic re-elections.The complaint further alleged that the SDO, purportedly acting on the directions of the Patiala MLA, was undertaking street repair and development works without following the prescribed tendering procedure.Citing specific instances in Ward No. 48, the BJP flagged repair work on Sood Street near Lahori Gate, alleging that it had been started without following the tendering procedure. It also raised concerns over a proposed street development and repair project on Loharan Street.

headline: Nomination process ends, 201 candidates in fray for MC repolls

The High Court has constituted a Judicial Monitoring Committee to oversee the re-election process.Phogat added that all necessary arrangements had been made to ensure free, fair and peaceful elections.

headline: Probe ordered into Bhakra canal bridge collapse in Patiala
content: A 60-metre-long steel truss bridge over the Bhakra Main Line Canal on the Patiala bypass section of National Highway-64 (New NH-07) collapsed in the early hours of Thursday near Passiana village in Patiala, leaving two trucks hanging precariously above the canal. No casualties were reported in the incident although the truck drivers sustained minor injuries. One of the trucks also caught fire, which was doused by the fire department.District Magistrate Himanshu Jain has ordered a magisterial probe into the incident and convened a meeting with NHAI Deputy General Manager Vipin Mehta and Project Director Amit Ojha seeking a detailed report regarding the bridge collapse incident.Meanwhile, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has also constituted an expert committee to investigate the cause of the collapse and recommend remedial measures to prevent such incidents.The bridge collapsed around 6 am when two trucks, reportedly overloaded with sand, were crossing the bridge. Preliminary findings suggest that excessive weight may have contributed to the collapse, but the exact cause will be established by technical experts.Following the incident, fire tenders, police personnel and rescue teams from the district administration rushed to the spot to control the fire and carry out rescue operations. District Magistrate Himanshu Jain also reached the spot to assess the situation.NHAI deployed its team and diverted traffic onto the service road to ensure the safety of commuters. Road safety marshals were also deployed while traffic police erected barricades. Signage, lighting arrangements and view-curtains have been installed around the damaged portion to secure the site.As an immediate restoration measure, NHAI is mobilising a 60-metre-span Bailey bridge, originally planned for traffic diversion at Vallah in Amritsar district. The NHAI authorities expect to restore traffic through the alternative bridge within three to four days.According to NHAI, the four-lane Patiala bypass section was handed over to the NHAI in 2018 and is currently under its maintenance contract. The four-laning work was executed by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) under the supervision of the Punjab Public Works Department.The bridge was constructed as part of the highway project, which was completed around 2016, raising questions about the structural integrity and maintenance of the infrastructure barely a decade after its construction. Further, NHAI said it was taking all necessary measures to ensure the safety of road users and facilitate the smooth movement of traffic along the affected stretch.

headline: 52 Lakh Marriages In 25 Days: India's Wedding Economy Set For Rs 7.5 Lakh Crore Windfall
content: India is gearing up for a massive wedding season, with around 52 lakh weddings expected to take place between November 21 and December 15, generating an estimated business of Rs 7.5 lakh crore, according to the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT). The 25-day wedding rush is expected to see more than two lakh weddings every day, driving demand across sectors ranging from jewellery, apparel and retail to hospitality, catering, transport and entertainment. Delhi-NCR alone is projected to account for around five lakh weddings and business worth Rs 2.5 lakh crore, CAIT said in a statement released Thursday. The estimates have been prepared by CAIT’s research arm, the CAIT Research and Trade Development Society, following consultations with more than 300 trade leaders and 550 trade associations across 25 states. Goods and retail purchases are expected to account for Rs 4.05 lakh crore, or 54% of the projected business, while services are likely to contribute Rs 3.45 lakh crore, making up the remaining 46%. Jewellery and precious metals are expected to lead the spending charts, generating an estimated Rs 1.2 lakh crore in business. Apparel and garments are projected to contribute another Rs 90,000 crore. Gifts and wedding accessories, along with grocery and food supplies, are each expected to account for Rs 37,500 crore. Electronics, dry fruits and sweets, furniture and household articles are projected to generate Rs 30,000 crore each. Among services, catering is expected to generate Rs 75,000 crore, followed by marriage venues, banquet halls and hotels at Rs 60,000 crore. Event management and wedding planning, as well as floral decoration and wedding decor, are each projected to contribute Rs 37,500 crore. Travel and transportation, music and entertainment services are expected to account for Rs 30,000 crore each, while photography, videography and beauty services are projected to generate Rs 22,500 crore apiece. The wedding season is also expected to create around 1.25 crore temporary, seasonal and part-time employment opportunities across sectors such as catering, decoration, photography, hospitality, transport, event management and beauty services. In Delhi, major trading hubs including Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazaar, Karol Bagh, Lajpat Nagar, Gandhi Nagar and Khari Baoli are expected to witness a surge in commercial activity. Wholesale markets in the region also cater to buyers from neighbouring states. Wedding expenditure varies widely, from around Rs 4-5 lakh for modest celebrations to Rs 4-5 crore or more for premium weddings, CAIT said. The CAIT’s estimates point to a steady rise in wedding-related business over the past few years. The sector generated an estimated Rs 3.75 lakh crore across 32 lakh weddings in 2022. This increased to Rs 4.74 lakh crore across 38 lakh weddings in 2023 and Rs 5.90 lakh crore across 48 lakh weddings in 2024. In 2025, wedding-related business was estimated at Rs 6.50 lakh crore across 46 lakh weddings. CAIT Secretary General Praveen Khandelwal said weddings generate economic activity by bringing together traders, manufacturers, artisans, small businesses and service providers. The traders’ body has also urged consumers to prioritise Indian-made products and local businesses, arguing that wedding-related spending can support domestic manufacturing and small enterprises.
