headline: 'Don't Fear Failure': Delhi Govt Launches Ehsaas 2026 Mental Health And Wellness Policy
content: The Delhi government on Thursday launched the “Ehsaas 2026 – Mental Health and Wellness Policy” at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium. Attending the event alongside Art of Living founder Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar were Lieutenant Governor Sardar Taranjeet Singh Sandhu, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, Education Minister Ashish Sood, and Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa. Speaking on the occasion, Delhi Education Minister Ashish Sood said that the Ehsaas 2026 Mental Health and Wellness Policy is not merely a policy document, but an important initiative towards understanding children’s emotional needs, listening to them, and providing them with sensitive support. Welcoming Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar—who arrived especially from Bengaluru for the launch—Sood noted that his contribution and guidance in the field of mental health and wellness are recognised worldwide, with work underway across five continents and more than 200 research studies conducted under his guidance. Expressing gratitude to Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, Sood shared that he had agreed to visit Delhi in November last year. During a foreign trip, he was requested via video call to attend the launch event so that the message of this initiative could reach as many people as possible through his guidance and presence. Sood thanked him for accepting Chief Minister Rekha Gupta’s request. The Education Minister also expressed gratitude to the Art of Living Foundation, which assisted in drafting the policy; Professor Rakesh Kriplani, Director, Cosmic Integrated Institute of Psychology and Security; Dr Amit Bhalla, Vice President, Manav Rachna University, and the School of Behavioural Sciences, Manav Rachna University; UNESCO; the Institute of Human Behaviour and Allied Sciences (IHBAS); and all associated institutions and experts. Addressing Academic Pressure and Loneliness Sood said Delhi felt the need for its own comprehensive mental health policy because, alongside academic and exam pressure, children today face mental pressures stemming from social expectations, comparison, the drive to get ahead of others, and the fear of falling behind. Describing Delhi as a miniature version of the country where families arrive from different parts of India in search of livelihoods, he noted that parents often remain busy with their responsibilities and work, leaving children feeling lonely and isolated. Constant pressure to score good marks and live up to expectations, he added, can adversely affect their mental health. Highlighting the need for a broader social shift, Sood observed that whenever people visit an acquaintance’s home, they often ask children about their studies and future careers, but rarely ask whether they are happy, how their day went, or how they are feeling. The objective of Ehsaas 2026 is to make this dialogue and sensitivity a natural part of society, ensuring children’s emotional needs receive the same priority as studies, good marks, and nutritious food. He further pointed out that hesitation and stigma around mental health persist in society, with many people trying to hide such issues rather than discussing them openly. Giving the launch event an enthusiastic and positive format was aimed at normalising conversations around mental health and removing the stigma attached to it. Paying attention to children’s mental and emotional well-being, he said, is just as essential as their physical health and academic achievements. Training Teachers and School Support Staff Sood shared that during the policy-making process, its scope was steadily expanded. Following sensitive incidents reported in schools and a key meeting on POCSO chaired by the Lieutenant Governor, it was recognised that raising awareness among parents alone is insufficient; every individual who comes into contact with children needs to be trained. This includes teachers, school principals, Educational and Vocational Guidance Counsellors (EVGCs), university vice-chancellors, officials, policymakers, and school support staff. He noted that school drivers, peons, ayahs, and other support staff interact regularly with children, making it vital to train them to recognise changes in behaviour, understand sensitive situations, and respond appropriately. Accordingly, capacity building and training of support staff alongside teachers have been built into the policy. He also thanked UNESCO experts for their suggestions and guidance during this process. In his address, the Education Minister urged students not to fear failure in life. Failure, he said, does not mean stopping or becoming afraid, but learning from experience and moving forward. Citing teachers and principals as examples, he reminded students that everyone encounters setbacks at some stage, and failure should be viewed as an opportunity to learn rather than the end of the road. For this, children must speak their minds openly, communicate, and never hesitate to seek help when needed. Key Provisions and Implementation Roadmap Sood stated that under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the leadership of Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, the Delhi government is committed to building a strong mechanism of dialogue, support, and mental health assistance for children. He expressed pride that Delhi is the first government in the country to introduce a comprehensive draft policy document on mental health and wellness covering both schools and higher educational institutions. Outlining key provisions of the policy, Sood said it provides for one counsellor for every 500 students, a dedicated helpline facility, and several targeted measures for mental and emotional support. Emphasising that the policy’s success hinges on effective execution, he affirmed that the Delhi government will work with full commitment to implement it on the ground. He assured that expert institutions will be engaged in the rollout. Noting that the Art of Living had previously supported the Delhi government with training and guidance in 2024, he said training programmes will continue with its support in the future. Additionally, a regular Impact Assessment of the policy will be conducted with the assistance of university vice-chancellors and subject experts to refine implementation where needed. Concluding his remarks, the Education Minister reiterated the Delhi government’s resolve to provide the necessary support and environment for a healthy, positive, and happy life for Delhi’s children, youth, and parents—reassuring young people that their emotions matter, they will be heard, and support will always be available when needed.

headline: Energy conservation vital for resource protection, energy security: Himachal governor
content: Shimla, Nov 20 (PTI) Energy conservation is essential for protecting natural resources, reducing pollution and strengthening the country’s power security, Himachal Pradesh Governor Kavinder Gupta said on Friday. He was addressing the winners of the State-Level Painting Competition-2026, organised by Sutlej Jal Vidyut Nigam (SJVN) under the National Awareness Campaign on Energy Conservation. Gupta said 2,38,548 students from classes 5 to 10 participated in the first phase of this year’s competition, reflecting growing environmental consciousness among young students. Emphasising the importance of responsible energy use, he said, “Energy is the foundation of modern development, but its judicious use is equally important. Small changes in our daily habits can bring a significant transformation at the national level”. According to a statement issued here, Gupta said India had made significant progress in clean energy, with non-fossil fuel-based installed power capacity reaching 300.50 GW as on July 31, 2026, accounting for over 54 per cent of the country’s total installed electricity capacity. The governor said students participating in the competition were not merely creating paintings but conveying an important social message through their imagination and creativity.

headline: BJP dealt state Rs 400-cr blow by selling properties at throwaway rates: Sukhu in HP assembly
content: Shimla/Dharamshala, Nov 20 (PTI) Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday accused the BJP of undermining the state’s interests and dealing it a blow of at least Rs 400 crore by selling real estate to industrialists at lower prices when it was in power. Sukhu made the charge while speaking in the state assembly on the adjournment motion: A government mired in corruption is putting Himachal on sale. A discussion on the opposition’s motion in the Himachal Legislative Assembly has been on since Tuesday. Addressing the issues raised during a nearly nine-and-a-half-hour-long discussion, the chief minister began by accusing the BJP of handing over the state’s valuable assets to industrialists at throwaway prices. On Friday, after Sukhu’s response, the motion was rejected by a voice vote. Earlier, before he could speak, Sukhu was welcomed with shouts and slogans from the opposition benches.

headline: Himachal Assembly passes bill to levy up to Rs 25 per tonne cess on clinker transported out of state
content: Shimla/Dharamshala (HP), Nov 20 (PTI) The Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly on Friday passed a bill providing for an environmental cess of up to Rs 25 per tonne on clinker transported out of the state. The Himachal Pradesh Taxation (on the Carriage of Certain Goods by Road) Amendment Bill, 2026 (Bill No. 20) was passed by a voice vote after amendments proposed by the opposition were rejected. During the discussion on the bill, Leader of the Opposition Jairam Thakur and BJP MLAs Randhir Sharma and Trilok Jamwal participated in the debate. Sharma argued that implementation of the bill would fuel inflation in the state, as transporters would pass on the burden of the cess to consumers, making house construction more expensive. Jamwal pointed out that the government was already collecting an environmental cess through electricity bills. He questioned whether the same individual could be made to pay a similar cess twice. Thakur also expressed concern that the passage of the bill would lead to an increase in costs.

headline: Over 2,200 drug manufactured in Himachal failed quality tests in past three years: Minister
content: Shimla/Dharamshala (HP), Nov 20 (PTI) As many as 2,216 pharmaceutical drugs manufactured in Himachal Pradesh failed to meet quality standards in the past three years, Health and Family Welfare Minister Colonel Dhani Ram Shandil informed the assembly on Friday. In a written response to a question by Bharmaur BJP MLA Dr Janak Raj, the minister further said licenses of three drug-manufacturing firms have been cancelled due to repeated failure to meet established quality criteria. Further, as many as 1,608 product licenses have been suspended and 59 licenses have been cancelled. In four instances, the manufacturer has been issued warnings. According to the government, these measures have led to either halt in the manufacturing of 1,667 products or the cancellation of their respective licenses. The minister said instructions have been issued to recall all drugs that failed to meet quality standards from the market, while the state’s drug control department has initiated legal action in 17 such cases. According to the government, 47 pharmaceutical companies have been identified whose product samples failed quality tests ten or more times over the past few years.

headline: One in every six TB patients diabetic in HP’s Hamirpur: Data
content: Hamirpur (HP), Nov 20 (PTI) Diabetes has emerged as an additional challenge for tuberculosis (TB) patients here, with 241 patients diagnosed with both conditions over the past two years, according to Health Department data. The data shows that around 17 per cent of TB patients in the district are also suffering from diabetes, requiring regular medical treatment and closer monitoring. Hamirpur recorded 780 TB cases in 2025, of which 132 patients were also diabetic. In 2026, 634 TB cases have been reported so far, with diabetes confirmed in 109 patients. Doctors said patients suffering from both conditions require consistent medical care, regular health check-ups and special attention to their diet. People with diabetes are at a higher risk of contracting TB, while managing both conditions simultaneously can make treatment more challenging. Chief Medical Officer Hamirpur Dr Satish Kumar said on Friday that the Health Department was ensuring regular availability of medicines to TB patients to facilitate their treatment.

headline: Manish Sisodia to lead AAP protest in Dharamshala; accuses Congress of failing to fulfil poll promises
content: Dharamshala (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 20 (ANI): Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Manish Sisodia on Friday accused the Congress government in Himachal Pradesh of betraying the people by failing to fulfil its 10 election guarantees, including Rs 1,500 monthly assistance to women, five lakh jobs for youth and 300 units of free electricity.Speaking to ANI in Dharamshala, Sisodia said not a single guarantee had been fulfilled and alleged that women and young people were particularly disappointed with the Congress government.He said AAP had taken to the streets to raise the concerns of women and youth and assured that the party would fulfil all its promises if voted to power in Himachal Pradesh. Citing the AAP government in neighbouring Punjab, he claimed that Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann had delivered on the party’s electoral commitments.On Delhi’s pollution crisis, Sisodia said air pollution was not confined to Delhi’s borders and required a coordinated effort by the Centre and all northern states. He said dust and pollution did not recognise state boundaries and called for a joint strategy involving Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and other northern states.He also urged authorities to stop blaming farmers for pollution, arguing that construction activities, vehicles and other sources also contributed to the problem. “It is a collective failure of North India, and the Centre must work with all northern states to find a solution,” he said.On the rising drug menace in Punjab, Sisodia rejected allegations that drug abuse had reached its peak in the state. He claimed that the Bhagwant Mann government had dismantled the political patronage system supporting drug trafficking and arrested around 90,000 drug smugglers.He alleged that previous Akali-BJP and Congress governments had allowed drug networks to operate with political support. He also accused the BJP of failing to prevent drug trafficking through Gujarat’s ports.Sisodia further said AAP would hold a protest march towards the Himachal Pradesh Assembly and decide its next course of action after reaching there. (ANI)

headline: Himachal Pradesh Government
content: Governor Kavinder Gupta while inaugurating the Winter Travel Exhibition organized by Travel and Tourism Bazaar, Kolkata, at the historic Gaiety Theatre, Shimla, today, said that Himachal Pradesh had immense tourism potential and such exhibitions could play an important role in promoting tourism activities, exploring new opportunities and strengthening tourism-related partnerships. Emphasizing the need for responsible tourism, the Governor said, ‘increasing the number of tourists alone cannot be the objective of tourism development. We must ensure that tourism goes hand in hand with environmental conservation, protection of local culture and the interests of local communities.’ He said the theme of this year's exhibition, ‘Importance of Sustainability in the Travel and Tourism Industry’, was highly relevant and stressed that tourism development must not put unnecessary pressure on forests, rivers, water sources and mountains. He said tourism should ensure a clean and enriching experience for visitors while creating employment and livelihood opportunities for local people and preserving the cultural identity of the state. Congratulating the organizers and participants, the Governor highlighted the prominent participation of Goa in this year's exhibition, saying it would provide an opportunity for Himachal Pradesh and Goa to exchange experiences, ideas and explore new tourism avenues. He said Himachal Pradesh was renowned across the world for its natural beauty, rich cultural heritage, spiritual traditions and adventure tourism. Its mountains, rivers, lakes, forests, historical sites and distinctive local lifestyle offered visitors a unique experience. Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision, the Governor said tourism was an important driver of employment, entrepreneurship and strengthening the local economy. Initiatives such as Vocal for Local and Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat also reflected the spirit of promoting local products, cultural heritage and tourism destinations. He expressed confidence that the exhibition would bring tourism stakeholders together, facilitate new ideas and partnerships and help establish Himachal Pradesh as a responsible, sustainable and quality tourism destination.

headline: HP High Court Bars Fresh Section 118 Land Permissions in Solan Without Court Approval
content: Shimla: The Himachal Pradesh High Court has temporarily barred the state government to grant fresh permissions for land purchases in Solan district under Section 118 of the Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972, without prior approval of the Court. The High Court has directed that no permission under Section 118 shall be granted in Solan district without its prior approval. The state government will also have to provide valid and justifiable reasons before seeking such approval. The order was passed by a division bench comprising Chief Justice Gurmeet Singh Sandhawalia and Justice Bipin Chandra Negi while hearing a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) concerning the alleged misuse of provisions governing land transfers to non-agriculturists and people from outside the state. Taking a serious view of the manner in which successive state governments have granted permissions under Section 118 over several decades, the Court observed that the stringent provisions of the law had gradually been diluted through unchecked approvals. As a result, the legal safeguards intended to regulate the transfer of land to non-agriculturists had largely lost their effectiveness. The Court also expressed concern over large-scale commercial construction, particularly apartment complexes, coming up in Solan district under the cover of permissions granted under Section 118. It observed that the state government had failed to control the situation and indicated that meaningful improvement would not be possible without strict judicial directions. The High Court has further directed the state government to submit a comprehensive report before the next hearing. The report must include a revised list of cases relating to Shimla district, along with data concerning the remaining areas of Kullu, Kangra and Sirmaur districts.

headline: IITF 2026: All you need to know about tickets, timings and entry gates
content: The 45th edition of the India International Trade Fair (IITF) opened to the general public at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on November 19. The annual event, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO), will continue until November 27. This fair has attracted significant attention from the capital city as well as the wider domestic and international business sectors. If you intend to attend the trade fair with your family or friends, remember to check ticket prices, visiting hours, entry points, and specific attractions within the halls. IITF is hosting exhibitors from India and abroad who are ready to welcome visitors as the fair gets underway. IITF 2026 dates and timingsThe ongoing edition of the IITF is taking place from November 14 to November 27, covering a total of 14 days. This year, the event has been separated into two segments to cater to both business attendees and the general public. The initial 5 days, running from November 14 to 18, were specifically allocated for business attendees and trade exhibitors. From November 19, the fair has opened its doors to the general public, welcoming families and younger guests, and will continue to do so until November 27. The fair will operate daily from 10 am until 7:30 pm, allowing entry until 5:30 pm. Each year, the trade fair draws in numerous visitors. Measures have been implemented to handle the crowd and ensure a smooth experience for all attendees.How to book IITF 2026 tickets and ticket prices?Visitors can buy tickets through an online platform from home. Those who prefer to acquire tickets in person can go to ticket counters established at 55 metro stations throughout the Delhi-NCR region. Visitors should be aware that the Supreme Court metro station, which is nearest to Bharat Mandapam, will not have a ticket counter for IITF. headline: Fake medicines sold under big pharma brands, racket busted in UP, Himachal
content: A probe into counterfeit medicines in Uttar Pradesh has exposed an interstate drug manufacturing and supply racket, with investigators uncovering two unlicensed pharmaceutical units in Himachal Pradesh. The raids in Himachal’s Solan and Baddi led to the seizure of drug manufacturing machinery, raw materials, semi-finished products and finished medicines bearing the names of established pharmaceutical brands.The investigation, which began with the seizure of suspected fake medicines from a medical store in Varanasi, gradually led the Uttar Pradesh Food Safety and Drug Administration (UPFSDA) to the suppliers, storage facilities and manufacturing locations. The department carried out the operation in coordination with the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF).The latest breakthrough came with the discovery of an unlicensed manufacturing unit at V.D. Pharma in Baddi's Jhundikalan area, following an earlier raid in Solan district. The Himachal Pradesh drug control authorities and police are now taking further action.The operation was conducted under the supervision of the UPFSDA Commissioner as part of the Uttar Pradesh government's zero-tolerance policy towards the illegal drug trade.VARANASI MEDICAL STORE RAID SET INVESTIGATION IN MOTIONThe investigation began on October 30, 2026, when a UPFSDA team raided SP Medical Store in Varanasi. The store was operating without a drug licence and was found selling Nurokind-LC tablets bearing the name of the pharmaceutical company Mankind.During questioning, the store owner, Sunil Kumar Patel, told investigators that he had purchased the medicines without bills from Ashok Kumar Verma, a salesman associated with Super Drug Agency in Lahartara.The team contacted Mankind for verification. Following the company's complaint and a comparative examination of the products, the medicines were confirmed to be counterfeit. The team also seized other illegal medicines worth around Rs 5 lakh during the operation.The findings prompted investigators to trace the supply agency and identify the people involved in distributing the suspected fake medicines.STORAGE FACILITY EXPOSED, 17 TYPES OF MEDICINES SEIZEDActing on the information gathered during the first raid, a joint UPFSDA team questioned Ashok Verma and delivery agent Priyanshu Tiwari on November 2.Their questioning led investigators to the residence of Surendra Nath Mishra in Varanasi. A room on the premises contained a large stock of 17 types of allopathic medicines stored without bills or a licence.Investigators noticed serious labelling and spelling errors on strips of Gudcef-Plus and Nurokind-LC, raising suspicions that the medicines were counterfeit. Eleven samples were collected for testing, while the remaining stock, estimated to be worth around Rs 2 lakh, was seized.The discovery shifted the focus of the investigation from retail outlets and distributors to the people storing and supplying the medicines in bulk.ZANGI APP LEADS INVESTIGATORS TO KEY SUPPLIERDuring questioning, Surendra Nath Mishra told investigators that he received the suspected counterfeit medicines from Abhishek Singh alias Ravi, a resident of Anpara in Sonbhadra district.He also disclosed that he communicated with Singh through the encrypted messaging application Zangi App.Following this lead, an FIR was registered at Rohania police station against four accused under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), on the complaint of a drug inspector.Investigators also found that Abhishek Singh had earlier been named as the main accused in a major counterfeit medicine case registered at Varanasi's Sigra police station in 2023. His arrest proved crucial in tracing the alleged manufacturing network.ACCUSED'S QUESTIONING LEADS TEAM TO HIMACHALDuring questioning, Abhishek Singh provided information about the locations where the suspected counterfeit medicines were being manufactured. The names of Saharanpur residents Haseen and Waseem, both sons of Salim and originally from Chilkhana, also emerged during the investigation.Investigators found that the two were getting medicines manufactured in the Solan region of Himachal Pradesh before supplying them to different markets.After corroborating the information with inputs from informers, a UPFSDA special investigation team, along with the Lucknow STF, conducted a raid on November 18 at a manufacturing unit in the Rajpura-Khera bypass area of Nalagarh tehsil in Solan district.The unit was found operating without a licence. Investigators also recovered machinery used in manufacturing medicines and materials for replicating the packaging of established pharmaceutical brands.MACHINERY, PACKAGING MATERIAL FOR BRANDED MEDICINES RECOVEREDThe raid led to the recovery of materials linked to several pharmaceutical products, including Pan-D (Alkem), Pressiz-300, C-AZ, A-Cipex-625, Neruro-300, Clavam-625, Clav-625, Cef-200LB, Obefix LB-200, Alcemox-CV, Zedi-200-LB, V-Clav-625, Zerodol-SP and Shelcal-500 mg.The premises had machinery for manufacturing and packaging medicines, including blister-packing machines, Alu-Alu packing machines, capsule-filling machines and weighing equipment.Investigators also found printed foil, stereo-printing materials and other packaging equipment. The recovered material is being examined to establish how medicines bearing the names and packaging of established pharmaceutical brands were being manufactured and supplied.SECOND ILLEGAL UNIT FOUND IN BADDIFurther leads obtained during the Solan operation took investigators to V.D. Pharma in Jhundikalan, Baddi.The team found another pharmaceutical manufacturing unit operating without a licence. Machinery and equipment used for manufacturing tablets, capsules and syrups were recovered from the premises.A substantial quantity of raw materials, semi-finished medicines and finished products was also seized. These included materials associated with the manufacture of antibiotics, antacids and cough syrups.The scale of the machinery and material recovered indicated that the premises had an extensive arrangement for drug manufacturing. Further legal action in connection with the unit is being undertaken by the Himachal Pradesh drug control department.INVESTIGATION ALSO EXTENDS TO SAHARANPURThe investigation has now expanded to locations in Saharanpur linked to Haseen and Waseem. Investigators have found leads relating to the alleged illegal manufacture, storage and sale of medicines at identified premises in the district.Legal action is being initiated at these locations, including the process of registering FIRs.The UPFSDA investigation has thus moved beyond the initial counterfeit medicine seizure in Varanasi to suspected manufacturing facilities, bulk storage locations and supply channels spread across multiple states. Investigators are continuing to examine the network and establish the extent of its operations.- EndsMust Watch

headline: Unauthorised drug unit busted in Nalagarh; 73k pills seized, 2 held | Hindustan Times
content: The Himachal Pradesh Drug Control Administration, working closely with the Uttar Pradesh Food and Drug Administration (UP FDA), has uncovered an unauthorised drug manufacturing and storage facility in Rajpura, Nalagarh, in Himachal Pradesh’s Solan district.Officials seized 67,000 antibiotic tablets, about 6,500 capsules of Pregabalin 300 mg, and roughly 100 kg of printed aluminium foil bearing other pharmaceutical companies’ logos. Following the recovery, two persons present at the premises were also arrested.The action was initiated following an information received from the Uttar Pradesh FDA regarding the recovery of certain drugs in Uttar Pradesh, which had been found to be substandard and were also suspected to be spurious.Acting promptly on the information shared by UP FDA, Dr Manish Kapoor, state drugs controller, Himachal Pradesh, constituted dedicated teams of drug inspectors to investigate the source and verify the suspected manufacturing premises in the Rajpura area of Nalagarh.During the search operation, the team discovered an unauthorised premises operating without any manufacturing licence issued by the Himachal Pradesh drug control administration. The premises, comprising certain rooms in a building at Rajpura, Nalagarh contained plant and machinery apparently intended for drug manufacturing, along with substantial quantities of medicines and pharmaceutical packaging material.The enforcement team seized approximately 67,000 tablets of various antibiotics and around 6,500 capsules of Pregabalin 300 mg. In addition, approximately 100 kg of printed aluminium foil bearing the branding of certain other pharmaceutical companies was recovered and seized.Taking cognisance of the evidence collected during the operation and the apparent involvement of two persons present at the premises, the drug inspectors arrested both individuals under the relevant provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. Further investigation is underway to establish the source, manufacturing network and intended distribution channels of the seized medicines.Searches conducted at suspected locations in BaddiDuring the operation, an informer accompanying the Uttar Pradesh Police special task force (STF) also provided leads regarding two additional suspected locations in the Baddi industrial area. Responding immediately, Dr Manish Kapoor constituted two separate dedicated teams of drug inspectors to conduct searches at these locations.At the first location, the team found that the premises were operating as a food-related facility under a valid FSSAI licence. No drug-related violation or recovery of medicines was detected during the search.At the second location, the team verified that the premises also held a valid wholesale drug licence in a dedicated space. As a precautionary regulatory measure, samples of the medicines available there were drawn for testing and further examination to ascertain their quality and compliance with applicable regulatory standards.

headline: Outsourced workers protest in Shimla over ‘delayed’ ₹25 minimum wage hike | Hindustan Times
content: Workers employed under outsourced services in various government departments and institutions in Himachal Pradesh staged a protest in Shimla on Thursday, demanding immediate implementation of the ₹25 daily hike in minimum wages announced by the state government in its budget.The protesters, led by the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU), also demanded timely payment of salaries to outsourced workers and alleged delays in the registration of trade unions, accusing labour authorities of favouring industrial establishments.Addressing the gathering, Vijender Mehra, CITU Himachal Pradesh state president, said the government had announced a ₹25 increase in daily minimum wages for workers across different categories in March, with the revised wages supposed to be effective from April 1. However, the notification implementing the hike had not been issued despite eight to nine months having passed.“Despite the announcement in March that minimum wages would be increased by ₹25 per day from April 1, the government has not issued the notification even after eight to nine months. Workers were supposed to receive an additional ₹750 per month, but the increase has still not been implemented,” Mehra said. He alleged that the government was citing financial constraints and the implementation of labour codes as reasons for delaying the wage revision, while spending substantial amounts on politicians, board chairpersons and influential officials.Mehra also criticised the government over the delayed implementation of the ₹1,000 monthly honorarium hike announced for anganwadi workers and helpers, alleging that although the increase was due from April, it was implemented only from November, depriving workers of seven months’ arrears.He alleged that trade union registration applications were being deliberately delayed for years, particularly in industrial areas such as Baddi, Barotiwala and Nalagarh, despite the prescribed registration process.He said the protesters had submitted a memorandum to the labour commissioner and sought discussions on the pending demands, warning that they would intensify their agitation if the government failed to act.

headline: HC halts Section 118 approvals in Solan over hill-cutting violations | Hindustan Times
content: Taking a stern view of alleged illegal construction and damage to trees in the famous tourist destination of Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh high court has directed that no permission under Section 118 of the Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972, shall be given by the state for Solan district without the permission of the court, after giving justifiable reasons.The court also directed the impleadment of the three builders, the director, town and country planning, and the secretary, urban development, after finding gross violation of the Hill Cutting Norms at Kasauli.The order was passed in a suo motu public interest litigation by a division bench comprising chief justice Gurmeet Singh Sandhawalia and justice Bipin Chander Negi.The sub-divisional officer (civil), Kasauli, who was present in person, submitted his status and inspection report in compliance of the earlier orders dated September 28 and October 26. It was stated that during a joint inspection, excavation work was found in progress at the property known as Woodvilla, adjoining the complainant’s house at Ferozi Village, Lower Mall, Kasauli, with the roots of certain existing trees exposed due to the excavation.Through a notice on October 16, the general manager/authorised representative of the project was directed to stop the ongoing work, to ensure that the exposed roots are immediately restored and the existing trees are adequately protected. The forest department reported the enumeration of 35 existing trees, with no felled trees found during patrolling, and it was found that no NOC had been issued by gram panchayat Kasauli Garkhal for the property.The court noted that massive construction and excavation is taking place at the site by three builders, namely, Reviera Luxury Project Five LLP, Sretan Luxury Project Four LLP and Jambavati Project Reality Three LLP.Going through the photographs, the court observed that there has been gross violation of the Hill Cutting Norms of the Policy Guidelines for Cutting, Conservation and Preservation of Hill, 2025 and that the necessary requisite permissions do not seem to be in place.The court directed that the said notices be strictly enforced against the three builders, failing which the SHO of the concerned jurisdiction shall ensure compliance. Notice has been issued to the newly impleaded respondents. The court also noted that the sub-divisional officer (civil), who was present, himself admitted that the greenery and the damage caused to the hill side just below the Radio Tower can be seen from Shimla, Kasauli being at least 25 kms away by “Crow’s flight.”The court observed that, if one is to lift the “Corporate Veil,” the three developers got the necessary permission by setting up different partnerships for the same project, which the state has conveniently given, making Section 118 of the Act a dead letter.Taking note of the action taken report of the sub-divisional officer (civil) and the report of the Central Empowered Committee, which pointed to hill cutting and extensive alteration of the natural terrain for the construction of resorts and hotels, permissions not being communicated to the forest department and the Pollution Control Board, and differing site plans and numbers of trees proposed to be felled before different departments, the court directed the sub-divisional officer (civil) to ensure inspection of all major constructions, primarily commercial in nature, since the green cover in the Kasauli range is being reduced at a very rapid rate for commercialisation purpose. The state has been directed to file its response to the action taken report.The court observed that rampant permissions granted under Section 118 of the Act in the Solan district are leading to commercial construction in the shape of flats, that the state government has been unable to take grip of the situation, and that no consolidated data has been placed on record.Though the counsel for the state strongly opposed the grant of interim orders on the issue, the court was of the considered opinion that, until extreme orders are passed, the state will not remedy itself, as these permissions have been unabatedly given over the last decades by successive governments, thus diluting the strict provisions of Section 118 of the Act. The matter is listed for further hearing on December 7, 2026.

headline: Tunneling trouble in Shimla: Himachal HC allows NHAI to survey damaged properties | Hindustan Times
content: The Himachal Pradesh high court allowed the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) to conduct a survey of affected properties to ascertain the actual extent of damage and determine necessary safety measures.The HC was hearing the petition relating to widespread structural damage to residential buildings owing to construction of twin tunnels in Shimla’s densely populated Shantibihar and Lower Cemetery areas. NHAI has already reiterated before the HC that it will not “resume tunnelling activities until the IIT Roorkee expert team gives its approval on safety aspects”.A single bench of justice Sandeep Sharma, while hearing a writ petition filed by affected residents on November 17, clarified that there was no restraint on NHAI conducting a building construction survey during the pendency of the case. The court observed, “The exercise was necessary to establish the actual damage, if any, caused to residential houses and to enable the authorities to take appropriate safety measures wherever required”.The petitioners also assured the HC of all necessary cooperation to NHAI for the survey from the residents.A number of affected residents have approached the HC, alleging that the NHAI and the executing construction company deviated from the earlier surveyed alignment and diverted the underground tunnel route beneath inhabited areas without obtaining requisite environmental and other statutory permissions and without following prescribed construction norms.The residents of Sanjauli, had moved the HC saying that NHAI has resorted to construction of twin tunnels without following the safety measures, as a result, large number of houses situated on the upper side of the tunnel are in danger.At least 16 buildings in the vicinity have developed similar structural damage, triggering panic among nearly 1,000 local families residing in one of the most densely populated areas of Shimla.The petition averred that though in original plans for construction of Shimla Bypass project on NH 05, there was no proposal to construct twin tunnel and bypass was proposed to be constructed through Chhakrail, Bhatta Kufar and Dhalli as a surface highway. The petitioners pointed out that the NHAI had not only acquired the land which was to be used for surface highway through Chhakrail, Bhatta Kufar and Dhalli, but compensation to the tune of approximately ₹600 crore was disbursed among the various land and house owners. On account of aforesaid acquisition, approximately 88 families have been already displaced as their houses were demolished.“Subsequently, without there being any plausible justification, NHAI abandoned the idea of making a surface highway and proposed to construct a twin tunnel from Chalauthi, Sanjauli to Bhatta Kufar,” the petitioners said.The petition pointed out that during construction of the twin tunnel, many houses have already suffered cracks and in the recent past, houses of the petitioners were also declared unsafe.The residents have been demanding a high-level independent technical committee comprising experts in geology, geotechnical engineering, structural engineering, tunnel engineering and rock mechanics to investigate the circumstances leading to the damage.

headline: Schools Shut In 10 Odisha Districts Today Amid Cyclone Akvan; Check State-Wise Update
content: Schools in 10 districts of Odisha will remain closed on Friday, November 20, due to the impact of Cyclone Akvan. The state government has announced precautionary closures in cyclone-affected areas to ensure the safety of students and staff. While schools in several districts of Odisha will remain shut, educational institutions in Delhi, Bihar, Rajasthan, West Bengal and Himachal Pradesh are expected to function normally on Friday, unless local authorities issue fresh orders. Odisha: Schools closed in 10 districts In view of the cyclone warning, schools in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Kandhamal have been ordered to remain closed from November 19 to November 21. Additionally, schools in Khordha, Malkangiri, Rayagada and Koraput will remain closed on November 20. The closures apply to government, government-aided and private schools in the affected districts. The administration has advised residents to remain alert and follow official weather advisories as the cyclone may affect coastal and adjoining areas. Delhi: Schools to remain open No citywide school holiday has been declared in Delhi for November 20. Schools are expected to conduct regular classes, with offline teaching continuing following the lifting of GRAP Stage 3 restrictions. However, parents and students are advised to check school notices for any changes in the schedule, particularly in view of air pollution levels. Bihar: No holiday announced Schools in Bihar are expected to remain open on Friday as the extended Diwali and Chhath Puja holidays have concluded. Regular academic activities are scheduled to resume. Tamil Nadu and West Bengal Tamil Nadu has not announced a statewide school holiday for November 20. However, district administrations in areas affected by heavy rainfall may announce closures depending on local weather conditions. In West Bengal, November 20 is not listed as a holiday in the state’s academic calendar. Government schools are expected to remain open, although private schools affiliated with CBSE and ICSE may follow their individual schedules. Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh Schools in Rajasthan are expected to function normally on Friday, as the mid-term break from November 4 to November 15 has already concluded. Similarly, November 20 is not listed as a gazetted holiday in Himachal Pradesh’s government calendar for 2026. Schools are therefore expected to remain open. Parents and students should check official school communications and district administration advisories before heading to school, as holiday orders may be revised depending on weather conditions.
